title.zh: 新唐書卷二十七上 志第十七上 曆三上
title.en: 新唐書卷二十七上 志第十七上 曆三上
title.raw: 新唐書卷二十七上 志第十七上 曆三上

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，麟德曆署日蝕比不效，詔僧一行作新曆，推大衍數立術以應之，較經史所書氣朔、日名、宿度可考者皆合。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan year 9, the Lindé calendar directorate's solar-eclipse comparisons did not match; an edict ordered the monk Yi Xing to compose a new calendar, deriving the numbers of the Great Expansion and establishing methods to respond to them; when compared with qi-periods, new moons, day-names, and lodge-degrees recorded in the classics and histories that could be verified, all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 9 the Lindé Calendar office's predicted solar eclipses failed to match observation. The emperor ordered the monk Yi Xing to draft a new calendar, deriving the Dayan numbers and establishing computational methods to fit the heavens; checked against verifiable qi-periods, new moons, day-names, and lodge-degrees in the classics and histories, everything agreed.

sentences.zh: 十五年，草成而一行卒，詔特進張說與曆官陳玄景等次為曆術七篇、略例一篇、曆議十篇，玄宗顧訪者則稱制旨。

translations.literal: In year 15 the draft was completed but Yi Xing died; an edict ordered Zhang Yue, holder of special advancement, with calendar officials Chen Xuanjing and others to compile in order seven treatises on calendrical methods, one summary of principles, and ten discourses on the calendar; where Emperor Xuanzong had personally consulted, these were labeled imperial directives.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the draft was finished but Yi Xing died. An edict ordered Zhang Yue, as specially advanced minister, and the calendar officials Chen Xuanjing and others to arrange in sequence seven treatises on calendrical method, one summary of principles, and ten calendar discourses; passages on which Emperor Xuanzong had personally consulted were labeled as imperial directives.

sentences.zh: 明年，說表上之，起十七年頒于有司。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Yue memorialized and presented it; from year 17 it was promulgated to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Yue memorialized and presented it; from year 17 it was issued to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 時善算瞿曇譔者，怨不得預改曆事，二十一年，與玄景奏：「大衍寫九執曆，其術未盡。

translations.literal: At the time Qutan Zhan, skilled in calculation, resented not being allowed to take part in the calendar reform; in year 21 he and Xuanjing memorialized: 'The Dayan calendar copies the Nine Foundations calendar; its methods are not complete.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time the skilled calculator Qutan Zhan, resentful that he had not been allowed to join the calendar reform, memorialized jointly with Chen Xuanjing in year 21: 'The Dayan calendar merely copies the Nine Foundations calendar; its methods are incomplete.'

sentences.zh: 」太子右司禦率南宮說亦非之。

translations.literal: ' The Right Bureau of the Crown Prince's Guard, Commandant Nangong Shuo, also opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: ' Nangong Shuo, commandant of the crown prince's right guard bureau, also opposed it.

sentences.zh: 詔侍御史李麟、太史令桓執圭較靈臺候簿，大衍十得七、八，麟德纔三、四，九執一、二焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Attending Censor Li Lin and Grand Astrologer Huan Zhigui to compare against the Spirit Terrace observation records: the Dayan calendar scored seven or eight out of ten, the Lindé only three or four, and the Nine Foundations one or two.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Attending Censor Li Lin and Grand Astrologer Huan Zhigui to check the Spirit Terrace observation records against the calendars: the Dayan scored seven or eight cases in ten, the Lindé only three or four, and the Nine Foundations one or two.

sentences.zh: 乃罪說等，而是否決。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nangong Shuo and the others were punished, and the matter was decided in the negative.
translations.idiomatic: Nangong Shuo and his allies were then punished, and their objections were rejected.

sentences.zh: 自太初至麟德，曆有二十三家，與天雖近而未密也。

translations.literal: From the Taichu calendar to the Lindé, there were twenty-three calendar systems; though close to heaven, they were not yet precise.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taichu calendar down to the Lindé there had been twenty-three systems; they approached the heavens but were not yet precise.

sentences.zh: 至一行，密矣，其倚數立法固無以易也。

translations.literal: When it came to Yi Xing, it was precise; relying on numbers to establish law, there was truly nothing to replace it.
translations.idiomatic: With Yi Xing it became precise; founded on numerical principles, his system could not be improved upon.

sentences.zh: 後世雖有改作者，皆依倣而已，故詳錄之。

translations.literal: Although later ages had revisers, all merely followed his model; therefore it is recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Later reformers only followed his model, which is why it is set down here at length.

sentences.zh: 略例，所以明述作本旨也；

translations.literal: The summary of principles clarifies the author's original intent;
translations.idiomatic: The summary of principles states the author's original purpose;

sentences.zh: 曆議，所以考古今得失也。

translations.literal: the calendar discourses examine the gains and losses of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: the calendar discourses weigh what past and present calendars got right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 其說皆足以為將來折衷。

translations.literal: Their arguments are all sufficient to serve as standards for future arbitration.
translations.idiomatic: Their arguments are sufficient to guide future judgments between competing methods.

sentences.zh: 略其大要，著于篇者十有二。

translations.literal: Selecting the main points, twelve topics are set out in the treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Selecting the main points, twelve topics are set out in the treatises.

sentences.zh: 其一曆本議曰：

translations.literal: The first, the discourse on the calendar's foundation, says:
translations.idiomatic: The first discourse, on the calendar's foundation, reads:

sentences.zh: 易：「天數五，地數五，五位相得而各有合，所以成變化而行鬼神也。

translations.literal: The Changes: 'Heaven's numbers are five, earth's numbers are five; the five positions matching one another each have their conjunctions, thereby effecting change and moving spirits and ghosts.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 'Heaven's numbers are five, earth's numbers are five; when the five positions pair with one another each attains its conjunction, and thereby change is wrought and spirits and ghosts set in motion.'

sentences.zh: 」天數始於一，地數始於二，合二始以位剛柔。

translations.literal: ' Heaven's numbers begin at one, earth's numbers begin at two; combining the two beginnings positions yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: ' Heaven's numbers begin at one and earth's numbers at two; joining the two beginnings sets yin and yang in place.

sentences.zh: 天數終於九，地數終於十，合二終以紀閏餘。

translations.literal: Heaven's numbers end at nine, earth's numbers end at ten; combining the two endings records intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's numbers end at nine and earth's numbers at ten; joining the two endings records the intercalary remainder.

sentences.zh: 天數中於五，地數中於六，合二中以通律曆。

translations.literal: Heaven's numbers center at five, earth's numbers center at six; combining the two centers connects pitch-pipes and calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's numbers center at five and earth's numbers at six; joining the two centers links pitch-pipes and calendar.

sentences.zh: 天有五音，所以司日也。

translations.literal: Heaven has five tones, thereby governing the day.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has the five tones, and thereby governs the day.

sentences.zh: 地有六律，所以司辰也。

translations.literal: Earth has six pitch-standards, thereby governing the chronogram.
translations.idiomatic: Earth has the six pitch-standards, and thereby governs the chronogram.

sentences.zh: 參伍相周，究於六十，聖人以此見天地之心也。

translations.literal: Three and five interweave, culminating at sixty; the sage thereby perceives heaven and earth's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Three and five interweave until they reach sixty; by this the sage perceives the mind of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 自五以降，為五行生數；

translations.literal: From five downward are the generating numbers of the five phases;
translations.idiomatic: From five downward come the generating numbers of the five phases;

sentences.zh: 自六以往，為五材成數。

translations.literal: from six upward are the completion numbers of the five materials.
translations.idiomatic: from six upward come the completion numbers of the five materials.

sentences.zh: 錯而乘之，以生數衍成位。

translations.literal: Interlacing and multiplying them, the generating numbers extend into positional values.
translations.idiomatic: Interlaced and multiplied, the generating numbers extend into positional values.

sentences.zh: 一、六而退極，五、十而增極；

translations.literal: One and six retreat to the limit, five and ten advance to the limit;
translations.idiomatic: One and six retreat to the limit, five and ten advance to the limit;

sentences.zh: 一、六為爻位之統，五、十為大衍之母。

translations.literal: one and six are the governing numbers of line-positions, five and ten are the mother of the Great Expansion.
translations.idiomatic: one and six govern the line-positions, five and ten are the mother of the Dayan numbers.

sentences.zh: 成數乘生數，其算六百，為天中之積。

translations.literal: Completion numbers multiplied by generating numbers yield six hundred in calculation, the accumulation at heaven's center.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying completion numbers by generating numbers gives six hundred in calculation—the accumulation at heaven's center.

sentences.zh: 生數乘成數，其算亦六百，為地中之積。

translations.literal: Generating numbers multiplied by completion numbers likewise yield six hundred, the accumulation at earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying generating numbers by completion numbers likewise gives six hundred—the accumulation at earth's center.

sentences.zh: 合千有二百，以五十約之，則四象周六爻也；

translations.literal: Combined they are twelve hundred; reduced by fifty, this yields the four images completing the six lines;
translations.idiomatic: Together they make twelve hundred; divided by fifty, this yields the four images completing the six lines;

sentences.zh: 二十四約之，則太極包四十九用也。

translations.literal: reduced by twenty-four, the Supreme Ultimate embraces the forty-nine uses.
translations.idiomatic: divided by twenty-four, the Supreme Ultimate embraces the forty-nine uses.

sentences.zh: 綜成數，約中積，皆十五。

translations.literal: Aggregating completion numbers and reducing the central accumulation, all are fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Aggregating the completion numbers and reducing the central accumulation, each is fifteen.

sentences.zh: 綜生數，約中積，皆四十。

translations.literal: Aggregating generating numbers and reducing the central accumulation, all are forty.
translations.idiomatic: Aggregating the generating numbers and reducing the central accumulation, each is forty.

sentences.zh: 兼而為天地之數，以五位取之，復得二中之合矣。

translations.literal: Taken together as heaven-and-earth's numbers, selecting by the five positions, one again obtains the conjunction of the two centers.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together as the numbers of heaven and earth and selected by the five positions, one again obtains the conjunction of the two centers.

sentences.zh: 蓍數之變，九、六各一，乾坤之象也。

translations.literal: In the changes of yarrow numbers, nine and six each occur once—the image of Qian and Kun.
translations.idiomatic: In the changes of yarrow numbers, nine and six each occur once—the image of Qian and Kun.

sentences.zh: 七、八各三，六子之象也。

translations.literal: Seven and eight each occur three times—the image of the six children.
translations.idiomatic: Seven and eight each occur three times—the image of the six children.

sentences.zh: 故爻數通乎六十，策數行乎二百四十。

translations.literal: Therefore line-numbers extend through sixty, and stalk-numbers run through two hundred forty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the line-numbers extend through sixty, and the stalk-numbers run through two hundred forty.

sentences.zh: 是以大衍為天地之樞，如環之無端，蓋律曆之大紀也。

translations.literal: Thus the Great Expansion is the pivot of heaven and earth, like a ring without end—indeed the great norm of pitch-pipes and calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Dayan is the pivot of heaven and earth, like a ring without end—the great norm of pitch-pipes and calendar.

sentences.zh: 夫數象微於三、四，而章於七、八。

translations.literal: Numbers and images are subtle at three and four, and manifest at seven and eight.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers and images are subtle at three and four, and fully manifest at seven and eight.

sentences.zh: 卦有三微，策有四象，故二微之合，在始中之際焉。

translations.literal: The hexagram has three subtleties, the stalks have four images; thus the conjunction of two subtleties lies at the juncture of beginning and center.
translations.idiomatic: The hexagram has three subtleties and the stalks four images; thus the conjunction of the two subtleties lies at the juncture of beginning and center.

sentences.zh: 蓍以七備，卦以八周，故二章之合，而在中終之際焉。

translations.literal: Stalks are complete at seven, hexagrams cycle at eight; thus the conjunction of two manifestations lies at the juncture of center and end.
translations.idiomatic: The stalks are complete at seven and the hexagrams cycle at eight; thus the conjunction of the two manifestations lies at the juncture of center and end.

sentences.zh: 中極居五六間，由闢闔之交，而在章微之際者，人神之極也。

translations.literal: The central pole stands between five and six; passing through the juncture of opening and closing, at the juncture of manifestation and subtlety—this is the pole of human and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The central pole stands between five and six; passing through the juncture of opening and closing, at the juncture of manifestation and subtlety—this is the pole of human and spirit.

sentences.zh: 天地中積，千有二百，揲之以四，為爻率三百；

translations.literal: The central accumulation of heaven and earth is twelve hundred; sorting by four gives the line-rate of three hundred;
translations.idiomatic: The central accumulation of heaven and earth is twelve hundred; sorted by four this gives the line-rate of three hundred;

sentences.zh: 以十位乘之，而二章之積三千；

translations.literal: multiplied by the ten positions, the accumulation of two manifestations is three thousand;
translations.idiomatic: multiplied by the ten positions, the accumulation of the two manifestations is three thousand;

sentences.zh: 以五材乘八象，為二微之積四十。

translations.literal: multiplying the five materials by eight images gives the accumulation of two subtleties, forty.
translations.idiomatic: multiplying the five materials by the eight images gives the accumulation of the two subtleties, forty.

sentences.zh: 兼章微之積，則氣朔之分母也。

translations.literal: Combining the accumulations of manifestation and subtlety, this is the denominator of qi-period and new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Combining the accumulations of manifestation and subtlety yields the denominator for qi-period and new moon.

sentences.zh: 以三極參之，倍六位除之，凡七百六十，是謂辰法，而齊於代軌。

translations.literal: Referencing the three poles, doubling and dividing by six positions, altogether seven hundred sixty—this is called the chronogram method, aligning with the generation-track.
translations.idiomatic: With the three poles as reference, doubled and divided by the six positions, the total is seven hundred sixty—called the chronogram method, aligning with the generation-track.

sentences.zh: 以十位乘之，倍大衍除之，凡三百四，是謂刻法，而齊于德運。

translations.literal: Multiplied by the ten positions, doubled and divided by the Great Expansion, altogether three hundred four—this is called the clepsis method, aligning with the virtue-cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplied by the ten positions, doubled and divided by the Dayan, the total is three hundred four—called the clepsis method, aligning with the virtue-cycle.

sentences.zh: 半氣朔之母，千五百二十，得天地出符之數，因而三之，凡四千五百六十，當七精返初之會也。

translations.literal: Half the mother of qi-period and new moon is fifteen hundred twenty, obtaining the number of heaven and earth issuing tokens; tripling it gives four thousand five hundred sixty, matching the conjunction when the seven luminaries return to their starts.
translations.idiomatic: Half the mother of qi-period and new moon is 1,520, obtaining the number when heaven and earth issue their tokens; tripling it gives 4,560, matching the conjunction when the seven luminaries return to their starts.

sentences.zh: 易始于三微而生一象，四象成而後八卦章。

translations.literal: The Changes begins with three subtleties to generate one image; when the four images are formed, then the eight trigrams are manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes begins with three subtleties to generate one image; once the four images are formed, the eight trigrams become manifest.

sentences.zh: 三變皆剛，太陽之象。

translations.literal: Three changes all yang—image of great yang.
translations.idiomatic: Three changes all yang—the image of great yang.

sentences.zh: 三變皆柔，太陰之象。

translations.literal: Three changes all yin—image of great yin.
translations.idiomatic: Three changes all yin—the image of great yin.

sentences.zh: 一剛二柔，少陽之象。

translations.literal: One yang and two yin—image of lesser yang.
translations.idiomatic: One yang and two yin—the image of lesser yang.

sentences.zh: 一柔二剛，少陰之象。

translations.literal: One yin and two yang—image of lesser yin.
translations.idiomatic: One yin and two yang—the image of lesser yin.

sentences.zh: 少陽之剛，有始、有壯、有究。

translations.literal: In the yang of lesser yang there are beginning, flourishing, and completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the yang of lesser yang there are beginning, flourishing, and completion.

sentences.zh: 少陰之柔，有始、有壯、有究。

translations.literal: In the yin of lesser yin there are beginning, flourishing, and completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the yin of lesser yin there are beginning, flourishing, and completion.

sentences.zh: 兼三才而兩之，神明動乎其中。

translations.literal: Embracing the three powers and doubling them, spirit and clarity move within.
translations.idiomatic: Embracing the three powers and doubling them, spirit and clarity move within.

sentences.zh: 故四十九象，而大業之用周矣。

translations.literal: Therefore forty-nine images, and the function of the great enterprise is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with forty-nine images, the function of the great enterprise is complete.

sentences.zh: 數之德圓，故紀之以三而變於七。

translations.literal: The virtue of number is round, therefore it is recorded by threes and changes at seven.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of number is round, so it is recorded in threes and changes at seven.

sentences.zh: 象之德方，故紀之以四而變于八。

translations.literal: The virtue of image is square, therefore it is recorded by fours and changes at eight.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of image is square, so it is recorded in fours and changes at eight.

sentences.zh: 人在天地中，以閱盈虛之變，則閏餘之初，而氣朔所虛也。

translations.literal: Humankind stands between heaven and earth to observe the changes of fullness and emptiness; then at the beginning of intercalary remainder lies what qi-period and new moon leave vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Humankind stands between heaven and earth to observe fullness and emptiness; at the beginning of intercalary remainder lies what qi-period and new moon leave vacant.

sentences.zh: 以終合通大衍之母，虧其地十，凡九百四十為通數。

translations.literal: Using the end-conjunction to penetrate the mother of the Great Expansion, diminishing earth's ten, altogether nine hundred forty is the universal number.
translations.idiomatic: Using the end-conjunction to penetrate the mother of the Dayan, diminishing earth's ten, nine hundred forty in all is the universal number.

sentences.zh: 終合除之，得中率四十九，餘十九分之九，終歲之弦，而斗分復初之朔也。

translations.literal: Dividing by the end-conjunction, one obtains the central rate forty-nine, remainder nine-nineteenths—the year's quarter-moon, and the new moon when the Dipper's fraction returns to the start.
translations.idiomatic: Divided by the end-conjunction, one obtains the central rate of forty-nine, remainder nine-nineteenths—the year's quarter-moon, and the new moon when the Dipper's fraction returns to the start.

sentences.zh: 地於終極之際，虧十而從天，所以遠疑陽之戰也。

translations.literal: Earth at the juncture of ultimate end diminishes ten to follow heaven, thereby keeping far from the battle of doubtful yang.
translations.idiomatic: Earth at the juncture of ultimate end diminishes ten to follow heaven, thereby keeping far from the battle of doubtful yang.

sentences.zh: 夫十九分之九，盈九而虛十也。

translations.literal: Nine-nineteenths: full at nine and empty at ten.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-nineteenths means full at nine and empty at ten.

sentences.zh: 乾盈九，隱乎龍戰之中，故不見其首。

translations.literal: Qian full at nine, hidden within the dragon's battle, therefore its head is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, full at nine, is hidden within the dragon's battle; therefore its head is not seen.

sentences.zh: 坤虛十，以導潛龍之氣，故不見其成。

translations.literal: Kun empty at ten, to conduct the qi of the hidden dragon, therefore its completion is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Kun, empty at ten, conducts the qi of the hidden dragon; therefore its completion is not seen.

sentences.zh: 周日之朔分，周歲之閏分，與一章之弦，一蔀之月，皆合於九百四十，蓋取諸中率也。

translations.literal: The new-moon fraction of the circuit-day, the intercalary fraction of the circuit-year, together with one chapter's quarter-moon and one obscuration's month, all combine at nine hundred forty—taken from the central rate.
translations.idiomatic: The new-moon fraction of the circuit-day, the intercalary fraction of the circuit-year, one chapter's quarter-moon, and one obscuration's month all combine at nine hundred forty—taken from the central rate.

sentences.zh: 一策之分十九，而章法生；

translations.literal: One stalk's fraction is nineteen, and the chapter method is born;
translations.idiomatic: One stalk's fraction is nineteen, and from it the chapter method is born;

sentences.zh: 一揲之分七十六，而蔀法生。

translations.literal: one sorting's fraction is seventy-six, and the obscuration method is born.
translations.idiomatic: one sorting's fraction is seventy-six, and from it the obscuration method is born.

sentences.zh: 一蔀之日二萬七千七百五十七，以通數約之，凡二十九日餘四百九十九，而日月相及於朔，此六爻之紀也。

translations.literal: One obscuration's days are twenty-seven thousand seven hundred fifty-seven; reduced by the universal number, altogether twenty-nine days remainder four hundred ninety-nine, and sun and moon meet at new moon—this is the record of the six lines.
translations.idiomatic: One obscuration's days are 27,757; reduced by the universal number, this is twenty-nine days remainder 499, when sun and moon meet at new moon—this is the record of the six lines.

sentences.zh: 以卦當歲，以爻當月，以策當日，凡三十二歲而小終，二百八十五小終而與卦運大終，二百八十五，則參伍二終之合也。

translations.literal: Using hexagrams for years, lines for months, stalks for days—in all thirty-two years make a small completion; two hundred eighty-five small completions match the hexagram-cycle's great completion; two hundred eighty-five is the conjunction of the two completions of three and five.
translations.idiomatic: Hexagrams stand for years, lines for months, stalks for days—in all thirty-two years make a small completion; two hundred eighty-five small completions match the hexagram-cycle's great completion; two hundred eighty-five is the conjunction of the two completions of three and five.

sentences.zh: 數象既合，而遯行之變在乎其間矣。

translations.literal: Numbers and images having combined, the changes of receding motion lie between them.
translations.idiomatic: Once numbers and images have combined, the changes of receding motion lie between them.

sentences.zh: 所謂遯行者，以爻率乘朔餘，為十四萬九千七百，以四十九用、二十四象虛之，復以爻率約之，為四百九十八、微分七十五太半，則章微之中率也。

translations.literal: What is called receding motion: multiply new-moon remainder by the line-rate to get one hundred forty-nine thousand seven hundred; void it with the forty-nine uses and twenty-four images, then reduce again by the line-rate to four hundred ninety-eight, minute-parts seventy-five and a half—this is the central rate within chapter-subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: What is called receding motion: multiply new-moon remainder by the line-rate to get 149,700; void it with the forty-nine uses and twenty-four images, then reduce again by the line-rate to 498, minute-parts 75½—this is the central rate within chapter-subtlety.

sentences.zh: 二十四象，象有四十九蓍，凡千一百七十六。

translations.literal: Twenty-four images; each image has forty-nine yarrow-stalks, altogether one thousand one hundred seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four images; each image has forty-nine yarrow-stalks, 1,176 in all.

sentences.zh: 故虛遯之數七十三，半氣朔之母，以三極乘參伍，以兩儀乘二十四變，因而幷之，得千六百一十三，為朔餘。

translations.literal: Therefore the voided receding number is seventy-three; half the mother of qi-period and new moon, multiplied by the three poles and by three-and-five, multiplied by the two instruments and twenty-four changes, then combined, gives one thousand six hundred thirteen as new-moon remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the voided receding number is seventy-three; half the mother of qi-period and new moon, multiplied by the three poles and three-and-five, multiplied by the two instruments and twenty-four changes, then combined, gives 1,613 as new-moon remainder.

sentences.zh: 四揲氣朔之母，以八氣九精遯其十七，得七百四十三，為氣餘。

translations.literal: Four sortings of the mother of qi-period and new moon, with eight qi and nine luminaries receding seventeen, gives seven hundred forty-three as qi-remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Four sortings of the mother of qi-period and new moon, with eight qi and nine luminaries receding seventeen, gives 743 as qi-remainder.

sentences.zh: 歲八萬九千七百七十三而氣朔會，是謂章率。

translations.literal: At eighty-nine thousand seven hundred seventy-three years qi and new moon meet—this is called the chapter rate.
translations.idiomatic: At 89,773 years qi and new moon meet—this is called the chapter rate.

sentences.zh: 歲二億七千二百九十萬九百二十而無小餘，合于夜半，是謂蔀率。

translations.literal: At two hundred seventy-two million nine hundred thousand nine hundred twenty years without small remainder, matching at midnight—this is called the obscuration rate.
translations.idiomatic: At 272,900,920 years without small remainder, matching at midnight—this is called the obscuration rate.

sentences.zh: 歲百六十三億七千四百五十九萬五千二百而大餘與歲建俱終，是謂元率。

translations.literal: At sixteen billion three hundred seventy-four million five hundred ninety-five thousand two hundred years the great remainder and year-establishment both end—this is called the origin rate.
translations.idiomatic: At 16,374,595,200 years the great remainder and year-establishment both end—this is called the origin rate.

sentences.zh: 此不易之道也。

translations.literal: This is the unchanging Way.
translations.idiomatic: This is the unchanging Way.

sentences.zh: 策以紀日，象以紀月。

translations.literal: Stalks record days, images record months.
translations.idiomatic: Stalks record days, images record months.

sentences.zh: 故乾坤之策三百六十，為日度之準。

translations.literal: Therefore the stalks of Qian and Kun are three hundred sixty, the standard of daily motion.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the stalks of Qian and Kun are three hundred sixty—the standard of daily motion.

sentences.zh: 乾坤之用四十九象，為月弦之檢。

translations.literal: The uses of Qian and Kun are forty-nine images, the gauge of lunar quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The uses of Qian and Kun are forty-nine images—the gauge of lunar quarters.

sentences.zh: 日之一度，不盈全策；

translations.literal: One day-degree does not fill the full stalk-count;
translations.idiomatic: One day-degree does not fill the full stalk-count;

sentences.zh: 月之一弦，不盈全用。

translations.literal: one lunar quarter does not fill the full use.
translations.idiomatic: one lunar quarter does not fill the full use.

sentences.zh: 故策餘萬五千九百四十三，則十有二中所盈也。

translations.literal: Therefore stalk-remainder fifteen thousand nine hundred forty-three is what the twelve centers exceed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore stalk-remainder 15,943 is what the twelve centers exceed.

sentences.zh: 用差萬七千一百二十四，則十有二朔所虛也。

translations.literal: Use-difference seventeen thousand one hundred twenty-four is what the twelve new moons leave vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Use-difference 17,124 is what the twelve new moons leave vacant.

sentences.zh: 綜盈虛之數，五歲而再閏。

translations.literal: Aggregating the numbers of excess and vacancy, every five years there is intercalation again.
translations.idiomatic: Aggregating the numbers of excess and vacancy, intercalation occurs again every five years.

sentences.zh: 中節相距，皆當三五；

translations.literal: Mid-season nodes are separated, all matching three-five;
translations.idiomatic: Mid-season nodes are separated, all matching three-five;

sentences.zh: 弦望相距，皆當二七。

translations.literal: quarters and full moons are separated, all matching two-seven.
translations.idiomatic: quarters and full moons are separated, all matching two-seven.

sentences.zh: 升降之應，發斂之候，皆紀之以策而從日者也。

translations.literal: Responses of ascent and descent, signs of issuing and gathering—all are recorded by stalks and follow the day.
translations.idiomatic: Responses of ascent and descent, signs of issuing and gathering—all are recorded by stalks and follow the day.

sentences.zh: 表裏之行，朓朒之變，皆紀之以用而從月者也。

translations.literal: Inner and outer motion, changes of waxing and waning—all are recorded by uses and follow the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer motion, changes of waxing and waning—all are recorded by uses and follow the moon.

sentences.zh: 積算曰演紀，日法曰通法，月氣曰中朔，朔實曰揲法，歲分曰策實，周天曰乾實，餘分曰虛分。

translations.literal: Accumulated counts are called evolving eras; day-divisor is called universal method; month-qi is called central-new-moon; new-moon substance is called sorting method; year-fraction is called stalk substance; circuit of heaven is called Qian substance; remainder-fraction is called void fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated counts are called evolving eras; day-divisor is called universal method; month-qi is called central-new-moon; new-moon substance is called sorting method; year-fraction is called stalk substance; circuit of heaven is called Qian substance; remainder-fraction is called void fraction.

sentences.zh: 氣策曰三元，一元之策，則天一遯行也。

translations.literal: Qi-stalk is called three origins; one origin's stalks are heaven-one receding motion.
translations.idiomatic: Qi-stalk is called three origins; one origin's stalks are heaven-one receding motion.

sentences.zh: 月策曰四象，一象之策，則朔、弦、望相距也。

translations.literal: Month-stalk is called four images; one image's stalks are the spacing of new, quarter, and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Month-stalk is called four images; one image's stalks are the spacing of new, quarter, and full moon.

sentences.zh: 五行用事，曰發斂。

translations.literal: The five phases' dominion is called issuing and gathering.
translations.idiomatic: The five phases' dominion is called issuing and gathering.

sentences.zh: 候策曰天中，卦策曰地中，半卦曰貞悔。

translations.literal: Qi-stalk is called heaven-center, hexagram-stalk is called earth-center, half-hexagram is called correct and repentant.
translations.idiomatic: Qi-stalk is called heaven-center, hexagram-stalk is called earth-center, half-hexagram is called correct and repentant.

sentences.zh: 旬周曰爻數，小分母曰象統。

translations.literal: Ten-day cycle is called line-number, small denominator is called image-unifier.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-day cycle is called line-number, small denominator is called image-unifier.

sentences.zh: 日行曰躔，其差曰盈縮，積盈縮曰先後。

translations.literal: Daily motion is called progression; its difference is called excess and deficiency; accumulated excess and deficiency is called before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Daily motion is called progression; its difference is called excess and deficiency; accumulated excess and deficiency is called before and after.

sentences.zh: 古者平朔，月朝見曰朒，夕見曰朓。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was mean new moon: when the moon was seen in the morning it was called waning visibility, when seen in the evening waxing visibility.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars used mean new moons: a moon visible at dawn was called waning visibility, one visible at dusk waxing visibility.

sentences.zh: 今以日之所盈縮、月之所遲疾損益之，或進退其日，以為定朔。

translations.literal: Now one adds and subtracts according to the sun's excess and deficiency and the moon's slow and fast, sometimes advancing or retreating the day, to make the fixed new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Today one adjusts for the sun's excess and deficiency and the moon's slow/fast anomaly, advancing or delaying the day as needed to obtain the fixed new moon.

sentences.zh: 舒亟之度，乃數使然，躔離相錯，偕以損益，故同謂之朓朒。

translations.literal: Degrees of slack and urgency are thus caused by numbers; progression and departure interweave, both adjusted by addition and subtraction—hence together they are called waxing/waning visibility.
translations.idiomatic: Slow and fast degrees arise from numerical relations; solar progression and lunar departure cross and are corrected together, which is why both are grouped under waxing/waning visibility.

sentences.zh: 月行曰離，遲疾曰轉度，母曰轉法。

translations.literal: Lunar motion is called departure; slow and fast is called rotation-degree; the denominator is called rotation-factor.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar travel is termed departure; the slow/fast variation is rotation-degree, and its denominator the rotation-factor.

sentences.zh: 遲疾有衰，其變者勢也。

translations.literal: Slow and fast have attenuation; what varies is momentum.
translations.idiomatic: The slow/fast cycle declines over time; what actually shifts is the underlying tendency.

sentences.zh: 月逶迤馴屈，行不中道，進退遲速，不率其常。

translations.literal: The moon winds and meanders, travels not on the central path, advances and retreats, slow and fast, not following its constant rate.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's path is winding and irregular; it does not keep to the mean track, and its speed varies rather than holding steady.

sentences.zh: 過中則為速，不及中則為遲。

translations.literal: Passing the mean makes it fast; not reaching the mean makes it slow.
translations.idiomatic: When motion passes the mean rate it is fast; when it falls short, slow.

sentences.zh: 積遲謂之屈，積速謂之伸。

translations.literal: Accumulated slowness is called bending; accumulated speed is called extending.
translations.idiomatic: Built-up lag is termed bending; built-up speed, extending.

sentences.zh: 陽，執中以出令，故曰先後；

translations.literal: Yang, holding the mean to issue commands, is therefore called before and after;
translations.idiomatic: Yang holds the center to give orders, hence the term before and after;

sentences.zh: 陰，含章以聽命，故曰屈伸。

translations.literal: Yin, harboring pattern to heed commands, is therefore called bending and extending.
translations.idiomatic: Yin holds its pattern and receives command, hence bending and extending.

sentences.zh: 日不及中則損之，過則益之。

translations.literal: When the sun does not reach the mean, subtract; when it passes, add.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun falls short of the mean, one subtracts; if it overshoots, one adds.

sentences.zh: 月不及中則益之，過則損之。

translations.literal: When the moon does not reach the mean, add; when it passes, subtract.
translations.idiomatic: If the moon falls short of the mean, one adds; if it overshoots, one subtracts.

sentences.zh: 尊卑之用睽，而及中之志同。

translations.literal: High and low serve divergent roles, yet the aspiration to reach the mean is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Superior and subordinate work in opposite ways, but both aim at the same mean.

sentences.zh: 觀晷景之進退，知軌道之升降。

translations.literal: Observing the gnomon shadow's advance and retreat, one knows the orbit's rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: By watching how the gnomon shadow lengthens and shortens, one learns whether the solar track is ascending or descending.

sentences.zh: 軌與晷名舛而義合，其差則水漏之所從也。

translations.literal: Orbit and gnomon differ in name yet agree in meaning; their difference is what the water clepsydra follows.
translations.idiomatic: Orbit and gnomon are differently named but refer to the same thing; the clepsydra measures the interval between them.

sentences.zh: 總名曰軌漏。

translations.literal: Collectively they are called orbit-clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, these are called orbit-clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 中晷長短謂之陟降。

translations.literal: Midday gnomon length, short and long, is called ascent and descent.
translations.idiomatic: Variations in the midday gnomon shadow are termed ascent and descent.

sentences.zh: 景長則夜短，景短則夜長。

translations.literal: When the shadow is long, the night is short; when the shadow is short, the night is long.
translations.idiomatic: Long shadows mean short nights; short shadows mean long nights.

sentences.zh: 積其陟降，謂之消息。

translations.literal: Accumulating ascent and descent is called ebb and flow.
translations.idiomatic: The running total of ascent and descent is known as ebb and flow.

sentences.zh: 遊交曰交會，交而周曰交終。

translations.literal: Wandering intersection is called conjunction; completing a cycle of intersection is called conjunction-end.
translations.idiomatic: A crossing encounter is termed conjunction; when the crossing completes a full cycle, conjunction-end.

sentences.zh: 交終不及朔，謂之朔差。

translations.literal: When conjunction-end falls short of new moon, it is called new-moon discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: If conjunction-end does not reach new moon, the offset is called new-moon discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 交中不及望，謂之望差。

translations.literal: When conjunction-center falls short of full moon, it is called full-moon discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: If the crossing midpoint falls short of full moon, the offset is called full-moon discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 日道表曰陽曆，其裏曰陰曆。

translations.literal: The sun's path on the outside is called the yang calendar; on the inside, the yin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's outward track is the yang calendar; its inward track the yin calendar.

sentences.zh: 五星見伏周，謂之終率。

translations.literal: The five planets' cycles of appearance and disappearance are called the terminal rate.
translations.idiomatic: The period in which the five planets appear and hide is termed the terminal rate.

sentences.zh: 以分從日謂之終日，其差為進退。

translations.literal: Following the sun by fractional parts is called the terminal day; its difference is advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Tracking the sun by fractional degrees yields the terminal day; the resulting offset is advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 其二中氣議曰：

translations.literal: The second discourse on qi-periods says:
translations.idiomatic: The second treatise on qi-periods states:

sentences.zh: 曆氣始于冬至，稽其實，蓋取諸晷景。

translations.literal: Calendar qi begins at winter solstice; examining the facts, it is essentially taken from gnomon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Calendrical qi-periods start from the winter solstice; in practice they derive from gnomon measurements.

sentences.zh: 春秋傳僖公五年正月辛亥朔，日南至。

translations.literal: The Zuoshi Commentary: Duke Xi's year 5, first month, xinhai new moon—the sun reached south.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuoshi Commentary records that in Duke Xi's fifth year, on the xinhai new moon of the first month, the sun reached its southern limit.

sentences.zh: 以周曆推之，入壬子蔀第四章，以辛亥一分合朔冬至，殷曆則壬子蔀首也。

translations.literal: By Zhou calendar reckoning, it enters the fourth chapter of the renzi obscuration, with xinhai one-part conjunction new moon and winter solstice; the Yin calendar takes the renzi obscuration head.
translations.idiomatic: Reckoned by the Zhou calendar, this falls in the fourth chapter of the renzi obscuration, with winter solstice and conjunction new moon at xinhai plus one part; the Yin calendar places it at the head of the renzi obscuration.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十年二月己丑朔，日南至。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao's year 20, second month, jichou new moon—the sun reached south.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary also records Duke Zhao's twentieth year, second month, jichou new moon, with the sun at its southern limit.

sentences.zh: 魯史失閏，至不在正。

translations.literal: Lu's annals missed intercalation; the solstice was not in the proper month.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's chronicle had failed to intercalate, so the solstice did not fall in the correct month.

sentences.zh: 左氏記之，以懲司曆之罪。

translations.literal: Zuoshi recorded it to punish the calendar officers' fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoshi preserved the entry to rebuke the calendar officers for their error.

sentences.zh: 周曆得己丑二分，殷曆得庚寅一分。

translations.literal: The Zhou calendar obtains jichou two-parts; the Yin calendar, gengyin one-part.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhou calendar the solstice falls at jichou plus two parts; by the Yin calendar, at gengyin plus one part.

sentences.zh: 殷曆南至常在十月晦，則中氣後天也。

translations.literal: The Yin calendar's sun-at-south often falls on the last day of the tenth month—then the qi-period is after heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yin calendar the solstice usually lands on the last day of the tenth month, meaning qi-periods run late.

sentences.zh: 周曆蝕朔差經或二日，則合朔先天也。

translations.literal: The Zhou calendar's eclipse-new moon discrepancy passes by up to two days—then conjunction new moon is before heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou calendar's eclipse and new-moon dates can be off by as much as two days, so conjunction new moons come early.

sentences.zh: 傳所據者周曆也，緯所據者殷曆也。

translations.literal: What the Commentary relies on is the Zhou calendar; what the apocrypha relies on is the Yin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary follows the Zhou calendar; the apocryphal texts follow the Yin calendar.

sentences.zh: 氣合于傳，朔合于緯，斯得之矣。

translations.literal: Qi matching the Commentary, new moon matching the apocrypha—thus one gets it right.
translations.idiomatic: Match qi-periods to the Commentary and new moons to the apocrypha, and the reckoning holds.

sentences.zh: 戊寅曆月氣專合于緯，麟德曆專合于傳，偏取之，故兩失之。

translations.literal: The Wuyin calendar's month-qi exclusively matched the apocrypha; the Lindé calendar exclusively matched the Commentary—each took one side, so both missed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyin calendar aligned only with the apocrypha, the Lindé only with the Commentary; by taking one source each, both went wrong.

sentences.zh: 又命曆序以為孔子脩春秋用殷曆，使其數可傳於後。

translations.literal: Further, the Calendar Order claimed Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn using the Yin calendar, so its numbers could be transmitted to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Order also asserts that Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals with the Yin calendar so its figures could be handed down.

sentences.zh: 考其蝕朔不與殷曆合，及開元十二年，朔差五日矣，氣差八日矣。

translations.literal: Examining its eclipses and new moons, they do not match the Yin calendar; by Kaiyuan year 12, new moon was off by five days and qi by eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Checked against eclipses and new moons, the figures fail to agree with the Yin calendar; by Kaiyuan 12 the new-moon error had reached five days and the qi error eight.

sentences.zh: 上不合於經，下不足以傳於後代，蓋哀、平間治甲寅元曆者託之，非古也。

translations.literal: It does not match the classics above and cannot be transmitted to later ages below—likely forged by those who made the Jiayin origin calendar between the Ai and Ping reigns; it is not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: It fits neither the canonical texts nor any workable tradition for posterity; it was probably ascribed by compilers of the Jiayin origin calendar in the Ai–Ping period and is not genuinely old.

sentences.zh: 又漢太史令張壽王說黃帝調曆以非太初。

translations.literal: Also, Han Grand Astrologer Zhang Shouwang invoked the Yellow Emperor's adjusted calendar to criticize the Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Grand Astrologer Zhang Shouwang also cited the Yellow Emperor's adjusted calendar to attack the Taichu system.

sentences.zh: 有司劾：「官有黃帝調曆不與壽王同，壽王所治乃殷曆也。

translations.literal: The authorities impeached: "The office has the Yellow Emperor's adjusted calendar, which does not match Shouwang's; what Shouwang worked on was the Yin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him: "The directorate holds a Yellow Emperor adjusted calendar that differs from Shouwang's; Shouwang's work is in fact the Yin calendar.

sentences.zh: 」漢自中興以來，圖讖漏泄，而考靈曜、命曆序皆有甲寅元，其所起在四分曆庚申元後百一十四歲。

translations.literal: " Since Han's restoration, charted prophecies leaked forth; Examining the Luminous Glaze and Calendar Order both have a Jiayin origin, which begins one hundred fourteen years after the Sifen calendar's gengshen origin.
translations.idiomatic: " After the Han restoration, prognostic charts circulated widely; both Examining the Luminous Glaze and the Calendar Order posit a Jiayin origin starting 114 years after the Quarter-Remainder calendar's gengshen epoch.

sentences.zh: 延光初中謁者亶誦，靈帝時五官郎中馮光等，皆請用之，卒不施行。

translations.literal: In early Yanguang, Palace Attendant Shan Song; under Emperor Ling, Five Offices Gentleman Feng Guang and others all requested its adoption—it was ultimately not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yanguang the palace attendant Shan Song, and under Emperor Ling the five-offices gentleman Feng Guang and others, all petitioned to adopt it, but it was never put into use.

sentences.zh: 緯所載壬子冬至，則其遺術也。

translations.literal: The renzi winter solstice recorded in the apocrypha is its surviving method.
translations.idiomatic: The renzi winter solstice preserved in the apocrypha is a remnant of that system.

sentences.zh: 魯曆南至，又先周曆四分日之三，而朔後九百四十分日之五十一。

translations.literal: The Lu calendar's sun-at-south is also three-fourths of a day before the Zhou calendar, while new moon is fifty-one parts in nine hundred forty of a day after.
translations.idiomatic: In the Lu calendar the solstice comes three-quarters of a day earlier than in the Zhou calendar, while new moon falls fifty-one nine-hundred-fortieths of a day later.

sentences.zh: 故僖公五年辛亥為十二月晦，壬子為正月朔。

translations.literal: Therefore in Duke Xi's year 5, xinhai was the last day of the twelfth month, and renzi the first month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in Duke Xi's fifth year xinhai was the last day of the twelfth month and renzi the new moon of the first month.

sentences.zh: 又推日蝕密於殷曆，其以閏餘一為章首，亦取合於當時也。

translations.literal: Also, eclipse reckoning is closer to the Yin calendar; taking intercalary remainder one as chapter head also accorded with the time.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse calculations also fit the Yin calendar more closely, and setting the intercalary remainder at one for the chapter head suited conditions of the day.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年十一月，陽城測景，以癸未極長，較其前後所差，則夜半前尚有餘分。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan year 12, eleventh month, Yang Cheng measured shadow; taking guiwei as longest, comparing the differences before and after, there were still leftover fractional parts before midnight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaiyuan 12 Yang Cheng measured the gnomon shadow; on guiwei the shadow was longest, and comparing readings before and after showed fractional parts still remaining before midnight.

sentences.zh: 新曆大餘十九，加時九十九刻，而皇極、戊寅、麟德曆皆得甲申，以玄始曆氣分二千四百四十三為率，推而上之，則失春秋辛亥，是減分太多也。

translations.literal: The new calendar's great remainder is nineteen and added time ninety-nine quarters, yet the Huangji, Wuyin, and Lindé calendars all yield jiashen; taking the Xuanshi calendar's qi fraction of two thousand four hundred forty-three as the rate and extrapolating upward, then the Spring and Autumn xinhai is missed—this is because the reduced fraction is too great.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar gives a great remainder of 19 and an added time of 99 quarters, while the Huangji, Wuyin, and Lindé calendars all yield jiashen. Using the Xuanshi calendar's qi fraction of 2,443 as the rate and extrapolating backward into the past misses the Spring and Autumn xinhai date—meaning the reduced fraction is too large.

sentences.zh: 以皇極曆氣分二千四百四十五為率，推而上之，雖合春秋，而失元嘉十九年乙巳冬至及開皇五年甲戌冬至、七年癸未夏至；

translations.literal: Taking the Huangji calendar's qi fraction of two thousand four hundred forty-five as the rate and extrapolating upward, though it matches the Spring and Autumn, it misses the Yuanjia year 19 yisi winter solstice, the Kaihuang year 5 jiaxu winter solstice, and the year 7 guimwei summer solstice;
translations.idiomatic: Using the Huangji calendar's qi fraction of 2,445 as the rate and extrapolating backward matches the Spring and Autumn but misses the winter solstice of Yuanjia year 19 (yisi), the winter solstice of Kaihuang year 5 (jiaxu), and the summer solstice of Kaihuang year 7 (guimwei);

sentences.zh: 若用麟德曆率二千四百四十七，又失春秋己丑。

translations.literal: If one uses the Lindé calendar's rate of two thousand four hundred forty-seven, one again misses the Spring and Autumn jichou.
translations.idiomatic: With the Lindé calendar's rate of 2,447, the Spring and Autumn jichou date is missed again.

sentences.zh: 是減分太少也。

translations.literal: This is because the reduced fraction is too small.
translations.idiomatic: That means the reduced fraction is too small.

sentences.zh: 故新曆以二千四百四十四為率，而舊所失者皆中矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the new calendar takes two thousand four hundred forty-four as the rate, and what the old calendars missed all hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar therefore adopts 2,444 as the rate, and every date the older calendars missed now agrees.

sentences.zh: 漢會稽東部尉劉洪以四分疎闊，由斗分多。

translations.literal: In Han, Liu Hong, Commandant of the Eastern Division of Kuaiji, held the Quarter-Remainder calendar to be loose and broad because its dipper fraction was too large.
translations.idiomatic: During the Han, Liu Hong of Kuaiji's eastern commandery found the Quarter-Remainder calendar too coarse, owing to an excessively large dipper fraction.

sentences.zh: 更以五百八十九為紀法，百四十五為斗分，減餘太甚，是以不及四十年而加時漸覺先天。

translations.literal: He changed to five hundred eighty-nine as era method and one hundred forty-five as dipper fraction; the reduced remainder was excessive, so within less than forty years added time was gradually perceived as preceding heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the era method to 589 and the dipper fraction to 145, but cut the remainder too drastically; within forty years the added times were noticeably running ahead of heaven.

sentences.zh: 韓翊、楊偉、劉智等皆稍損益，更造新術，而皆依讖緯「三百歲改憲」之文，考經之合朔多中，較傳之南至則否。

translations.literal: Han Yi, Yang Wei, Liu Zhi, and others each made slight additions and subtractions, devising new methods, all following the apocryphal text 'every three hundred years revise the calendar'; examining the classics, new-moon conjunctions mostly hit, but comparing with the Annals for south arrival it did not.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yi, Yang Wei, Liu Zhi, and others each tweaked the parameters and devised new methods, all citing the apocryphal maxim that the calendar should be revised every three hundred years. Against the classics their new moons mostly agreed, but against the Annals' winter solstices they did not.

sentences.zh: 玄始曆以為十九年七閏，皆有餘分，是以中氣漸差。

translations.literal: The Xuanshi calendar held that nineteen years with seven intercalations each had a surplus fraction, so mid-qi gradually diverged.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanshi calendar treated the seven intercalations in nineteen years as each carrying a surplus fraction, causing mid-qi to drift over time.

sentences.zh: 據渾天，二分為東西之中，而晷景不等；

translations.literal: According to the armillary-heaven model, the two equinoxes are the center of east and west, yet gnomon shadows are not equal;
translations.idiomatic: On the armillary-heaven model the equinoxes mark the midpoint between east and west, yet the gnomon shadows at those points are unequal;

sentences.zh: 二至為南北之極，而進退不齊。

translations.literal: The two solstices are the extremes of north and south, yet advance and retreat are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The solstices mark the northern and southern extremes, yet the sun's advance and retreat are uneven.

sentences.zh: 此古人所未達也。

translations.literal: This the ancients had not comprehended.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had not grasped this.

sentences.zh: 更因劉洪紀法，增十一年以為章歲，而減閏餘十九分之一。

translations.literal: Further following Liu Hong's era method, he added eleven years to make the chapter year, and reduced the intercalary remainder by one nineteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Building on Liu Hong's era method, he added eleven years to the chapter year and cut the intercalary remainder by one nineteenth.

sentences.zh: 春秋後五十四年，歲在甲寅，直應鍾章首，與景初曆閏餘皆盡。

translations.literal: Fifty-four years after the Spring and Autumn, the year standing at jiayin directly corresponded to the zhong chapter head, and the Jingchu calendar's intercalary remainder was fully exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-four years after the Spring and Autumn era, in the jiayin year, the cycle aligned directly with the zhong chapter head, at which point the Jingchu calendar's intercalary remainder ran out entirely.

sentences.zh: 雖減章閏，然中氣加時尚差，故未合于春秋。

translations.literal: Although chapter intercalation was reduced, yet mid-qi added time still differed, therefore it did not match the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Despite trimming the intercalary chapter, the times of mid-qi still diverged, so it failed to agree with the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 其斗分幾得中矣。

translations.literal: Its dipper fraction nearly hit the center.
translations.idiomatic: Its dipper fraction came very close to the correct value.

sentences.zh: 後代曆家，皆因循玄始，而損益或過差。

translations.literal: Later calendar makers all followed the Xuanshi in succession, yet their additions and subtractions sometimes exceeded proper limits.
translations.idiomatic: Later calendrists all followed the Xuanshi model, but their adjustments sometimes overshot or undershot.

sentences.zh: 大抵古曆未減斗分，其率自二千五百以上。

translations.literal: Generally the ancient calendars, not having reduced the dipper fraction, had rates from two thousand five hundred upward.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, older calendars that had not reduced the dipper fraction used rates of 2,500 and above.

sentences.zh: 乾象至于元嘉曆，未減閏餘，其率自二千四百六十以上。

translations.literal: From the Qianxiang through the Yuanjia calendar, not having reduced the intercalary remainder, rates ran from two thousand four hundred sixty upward.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qianxiang through the Yuanjia calendar, which did not reduce the intercalary remainder, rates ranged from 2,460 upward.

sentences.zh: 玄始、大明至麟德曆皆減分破章，其率自二千四百二十九以上。

translations.literal: The Xuanshi, Daming, and on through the Lindé calendar all reduced fractions and broke chapters; their rates ran from two thousand four hundred twenty-nine upward.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanshi, Daming, and Lindé calendars all reduced fractions and split chapters, with rates from 2,429 upward.

sentences.zh: 較前代史官注記，惟元嘉十三年十一月甲戌景長，皇極、麟德、開元曆皆得癸酉，蓋日度變常爾。

translations.literal: Comparing with prior dynasties' historiographers' annotated records, only Yuanjia year 13 eleventh month jiaxu with long shadow—the Huangji, Lindé, and Kaiyuan calendars all yield guiyou; likely the solar degree changed from its constant.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with annotated records from earlier dynasties' historiographers, only for the long-shadow solstice of Yuanjia year 13, month 11, jiaxu do the Huangji, Lindé, and Kaiyuan calendars all yield guiyou—presumably because the sun's apparent position varied from its mean rate.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之既失甲戌冬至，以為加時太早，增小餘以附會之。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi having missed the jiaxu winter solstice, deemed the added time too early and increased the small remainder to force a fit.
translations.idiomatic: After missing the jiaxu winter solstice, Zu Chongzhi decided the added time was too early and inflated the small remainder to make the numbers fit.

sentences.zh: 而十二年戊辰景長，得己巳；

translations.literal: Yet in year 12 the wuchen long shadow yielded jisi;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in year 12 the long-shadow solstice fell on wuchen while his calendar gave jisi;

sentences.zh: 十七年甲午景長，得乙未；

translations.literal: Year 17 jiawu long shadow yielded yiwei;
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the long-shadow solstice was jiawu but he obtained yiwei;

sentences.zh: 十八年己亥景長，得庚子。

translations.literal: Year 18 jihai long shadow yielded gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 the long-shadow solstice was jihai but he obtained gengzi.

sentences.zh: 合一失三，其失愈多。

translations.literal: One hit and three misses—the misses grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He matched one and missed three—the errors piled up.

sentences.zh: 劉孝孫、張冑玄因之，小餘益強，又以十六年己丑景長為庚寅矣。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosun and Zhang Zhouxuan followed this, strengthening the small remainder further, and again took year 16 jichou long shadow as gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun and Zhang Zhouxuan followed suit, pushing the small remainder even harder, and likewise placed the year 16 jichou long-shadow solstice on gengyin.

sentences.zh: 治曆者糾合眾同，以稽其所異，苟獨異焉，則失行可知。

translations.literal: Calendar makers gather what all agree on to examine what differs; if alone it differs, errant motion can be known.
translations.idiomatic: A calendrist should gather what most calendars agree on and scrutinize the outliers; if a calendar stands alone in disagreement, its faulty reckoning becomes evident.

sentences.zh: 今曲就其一，而少者失三，多者失五，是捨常數而從失行也。

translations.literal: Now bending to fit one case, the lesser misses three, the greater misses five—this is abandoning constant numbers and following errant motion.
translations.idiomatic: Bending the constants to fit a single case yields three misses in one instance and five in another—abandoning the stable numbers to chase an anomaly.

sentences.zh: 周建德六年，以壬辰景長，而麟德、開元曆皆得癸巳。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Jiande year 6, taking renchen long shadow, yet the Lindé and Kaiyuan calendars both yield guisi.
translations.idiomatic: At the long-shadow solstice of Northern Zhou Jiande year 6, observed on renchen, the Lindé and Kaiyuan calendars both give guisi.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年，以癸未景短，而麟德、開元曆皆得壬午。

translations.literal: Kaihuang year 7, taking guimwei short shadow, yet the Lindé and Kaiyuan calendars both yield renwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the short-shadow solstice of Kaihuang year 7, observed on guimwei, the Lindé and Kaiyuan calendars both give renwu.

sentences.zh: 先後相戾，不可叶也，皆日行盈縮使然。

translations.literal: Before and after contradict one another and cannot be harmonized—all are caused by the sun's daily excess and deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: The discrepancies between earlier and later cases cannot be reconciled—they all arise from the sun's variable apparent speed.

sentences.zh: 凡曆術在於常數，而不在於變行。

translations.literal: Generally calendrical method lies in constant numbers, not in variable motion.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar making rests on fixed constants, not on chasing variable motion.

sentences.zh: 既叶中行之率，則可以兩齊先後之變矣。

translations.literal: Once harmonized with the rate of mean motion, one can then make both agree for the variations of before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Once the mean-motion rate is established, both early and late deviations can be balanced together.

sentences.zh: 麟德已前，實錄所記，乃依時曆書之，非候景所得。

translations.literal: Before the Lindé, what the Veritable Records record was written according to the calendar of the time, not obtained from observing shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Lindé era, the Veritable Records simply copied the reigning calendar, not actual gnomon observations.

sentences.zh: 又比年候景，長短不均，由加時有早晏，行度有盈縮也。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years observing shadows, long and short were uneven, because added time had early and late, and motion-degrees had excess and deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Recent shadow observations have also been inconsistent, since added times vary and solar motion is uneven.

sentences.zh: 自春秋以來，至開元十二年，冬、夏至凡三十一事，戊寅曆得十六，麟德曆得二十三，開元曆得二十四。

translations.literal: From the Spring and Autumn down to Kaiyuan year 12, winter and summer solstices totaled thirty-one matters; the Wuyin calendar got sixteen, the Lindé got twenty-three, the Kaiyuan got twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: From the Spring and Autumn through Kaiyuan year 12, there are thirty-one verifiable winter and summer solstices. The Wuyin calendar matches sixteen, the Lindé twenty-three, and the Kaiyuan twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 其三合朔議曰：

translations.literal: The third, the discourse on new-moon conjunction, says:
translations.idiomatic: The third discourse, on new-moon conjunction, states:

sentences.zh: 日月合度謂之朔。

translations.literal: Sun and moon at the same degree is called new moon.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun and moon share the same celestial degree, that is called the new moon.

sentences.zh: 無所取之，取之蝕也。

translations.literal: With nothing to take from, one takes from eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Having no other anchor to rely on, one turns to eclipses.

sentences.zh: 春秋日蝕有甲乙者三十四。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn solar eclipses on jia or yi days number thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records thirty-four solar eclipses falling on jia or yi days.

sentences.zh: 殷曆、魯曆先一日者十三，後一日者三；

translations.literal: The Yin and Lu calendars one day early number thirteen, one day late number three;
translations.idiomatic: Against the Yin and Lu calendars, thirteen eclipses fall one day early and three one day late;

sentences.zh: 周曆先一日者二十二，先二日者九。

translations.literal: The Zhou calendar one day early numbers twenty-two, two days early numbers nine.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Zhou calendar, twenty-two fall one day early and nine two days early.

sentences.zh: 其偽可知矣。

translations.literal: Its falsity can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Its spuriousness is obvious.

sentences.zh: 莊公三十年九月庚午朔，襄公二十一年九月庚戌朔，定公五年三月辛亥朔，當以盈縮、遲速為定朔。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang year 30 ninth month gengwu new moon, Duke Xiang year 21 ninth month gengxu new moon, Duke Ding year 5 third month xinhai new moon—ought to take excess and deficiency, slow and fast as fixed new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The new moons of Duke Zhuang year 30 (9th month, gengwu), Duke Xiang year 21 (9th month, gengxu), and Duke Ding year 5 (3rd month, xinhai) should be determined as fixed new moons, accounting for solar excess and deficiency and lunar slow and fast motion.

sentences.zh: 殷曆雖合，適然耳，非正也。

translations.literal: Though the Yin calendar matches, it is merely chance, not correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin calendar may appear to agree, but that is coincidence, not proof of correctness.

sentences.zh: 僖公五年正月辛亥朔，十二月丙子朔，十四年三月己丑朔；

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 5 first month xinhai new moon, twelfth month bingzi new moon, year 14 third month jichou new moon;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi's year 5 (1st month xinhai, 12th month bingzi) and year 14 (3rd month jichou) new moons;

sentences.zh: 文公元年五月辛酉朔，十一年三月甲申晦；

translations.literal: Duke Wen year 1 fifth month xinyou new moon, year 11 third month jiashen last day of month;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen's year 1 (5th month xinyou new moon) and year 11 (3rd month jiashen, last day of month);

sentences.zh: 襄公十九年五月壬辰晦；

translations.literal: Duke Xiang year 19 fifth month renchen last day of month;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang year 19, 5th month renchen, last day of month;

sentences.zh: 昭公元年十二月甲辰朔，二十年二月己丑朔，二十三年正月壬寅朔、七月戊辰晦：皆與周曆合。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao year 1 twelfth month jiachen new moon, year 20 second month jichou new moon, year 23 first month renyin new moon and seventh month wuchen last day of month: all match the Zhou calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao's year 1 (12th month jiachen), year 20 (2nd month jichou), and year 23 (1st month renyin new moon and 7th month wuchen last day)—all agree with the Zhou calendar.

sentences.zh: 其所記多周、齊、晉事，蓋周王所頒，齊、晉用之。

translations.literal: What it records are mostly Zhou, Qi, and Jin affairs—presumably promulgated by the Zhou king and used by Qi and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Its entries chiefly concern Zhou, Qi, and Jin—likely calendars issued by the Zhou court and adopted by Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 僖公十五年九月己卯晦，十六年正月戊申朔；

translations.literal: Duke Xi's year 15 ninth month jimao last day of month, year 16 first month wushen new moon;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi's year 15 (9th month, jimao, last day) and year 16 (1st month, wushen new moon);

sentences.zh: 成公十六年六月甲午晦；

translations.literal: Duke Cheng year 16 sixth month jiawu last day of month;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cheng's year 16 (6th month, jiawu, last day);

sentences.zh: 襄公十八年十月丙寅晦、十一月丁卯朔，二十六年三月甲寅朔，二十七年六月丁未朔：與殷曆、魯曆合。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang year 18 tenth month bingyin last day of month and eleventh month dingmao new moon, year 26 third month jiayin new moon, year 27 sixth month dingwei new moon: match the Yin and Lu calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang's year 18 (10th month bingyin last day and 11th month dingmao new moon), year 26 (3rd month jiayin new moon), and year 27 (6th month dingwei new moon)—all agree with the Yin and Lu calendars.

sentences.zh: 此非合蝕，故仲尼因循時史，而所記多宋、魯事，與齊、晉不同可知矣。

translations.literal: These are not eclipse conjunctions; therefore Confucius followed the chronicles of the age, and what was recorded was mostly Song and Lu affairs—different from Qi and Jin, as can be known.
translations.idiomatic: These are not records tied to eclipses, so Confucius followed contemporary annals; since those annals chiefly record Song and Lu, they naturally differ from Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 昭公十二年十月壬申朔，原輿人逐原伯絞，與魯曆、周曆皆差一日，此丘明即其所聞書之也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao year 12 tenth month renshen new moon, people of Yuanyu drove out Lord Yuan Jiao—differs one day from both Lu and Zhou calendars; this Qiu Ming wrote as he heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao's year 12 (10th month, renshen new moon) records the expulsion of Lord Yuan Jiao by Yuanyu—one day off from both the Lu and Zhou calendars; Qiu Ming recorded it as he had heard it.

sentences.zh: 僖公二十二年十一月己巳朔，宋、楚戰于泓。

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 22 eleventh month jisi new moon, Song and Chu fought at Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi's year 22 (11th month, jisi new moon): Song and Chu fought at Hong.

sentences.zh: 周、殷、魯曆皆先一日，楚人所赴也。

translations.literal: Zhou, Yin, and Lu calendars are all one day early—what the Chu people reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou, Yin, and Lu calendars all run one day ahead—reflecting the date the Chu envoys reported.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十年六月丁巳晦，衞侯與北宮喜盟；

translations.literal: Duke Zhao year 20 sixth month dingsi last day of month, Marquis of Wei covenanted with Beigong Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao's year 20 (6th month, dingsi, last day): the Marquis of Wei made a covenant with Beigong Xi;

sentences.zh: 七月戊午朔，遂盟國人。

translations.literal: Seventh month wuwu new moon, then covenanted with the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu new moon of the 7th month he covenanted with the state's people.

sentences.zh: 三曆皆先二日，衞人所赴也。

translations.literal: All three calendars are two days early—what the Wei people reported.
translations.idiomatic: All three calendars are two days ahead—what the Wei envoys reported.

sentences.zh: 此則列國之曆不可以一術齊矣。

translations.literal: Thus the calendars of the various states cannot be aligned with one method.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the states' calendars cannot be forced into a single system.

sentences.zh: 而長曆日子不在其月，則改易閏餘，欲以求合。

translations.literal: Yet when the Long Calendar's day-marker falls outside its month, one alters the intercalary remainder, hoping to achieve agreement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Long Calendar places a day outside its proper month, calendrists tamper with the intercalary remainder trying to force a match.

sentences.zh: 故閏月相距，近則十餘月，遠或七十餘月，此杜預所甚繆也。

translations.literal: Therefore intercalary months can be separated by as little as ten-plus months or as much as seventy-plus months—this is what Du Yu was profoundly wrong about.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary months therefore end up spaced anywhere from a little over ten to more than seventy months apart—a grave error in Du Yu's approach.

sentences.zh: 夫合朔先天，則經書日蝕以糾之。

translations.literal: When new-moon conjunction precedes heaven, the canonical texts' solar eclipses correct it.
translations.idiomatic: If conjunction dates run ahead of heaven, solar eclipses in the classics serve as a corrective.

sentences.zh: 中氣後天，則傳書南至以明之。

translations.literal: When mid-qi lags heaven, the Annals' recording of south arrival clarifies it.
translations.idiomatic: If mid-qi dates lag heaven, the Annals' winter solstice entries clarify the error.

sentences.zh: 其在晦、二日，則原乎定朔以得之。

translations.literal: When it falls on the last day or the second day, one derives it from fixed new moon.
translations.idiomatic: When dates fall on the last day of the month or the second day, fixed-new-moon calculation supplies the answer.

sentences.zh: 列國之曆或殊，則稽於六家之術以知之。

translations.literal: When the various states' calendars differ, one consults the six schools' methods to know.
translations.idiomatic: Where state calendars diverge, comparison with the six schools' methods reveals the truth.

sentences.zh: 此四者，皆治曆之大端，而預所未曉故也。

translations.literal: These four are all major principles of calendar-making—what Yu did not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: These four points are the main pillars of calendrical science—points Du Yu failed to grasp.

sentences.zh: 新曆本春秋日蝕、古史交會加時及史官候簿所詳，稽其進退之中，以立常率。

translations.literal: The new calendar draws on Spring and Autumn solar eclipses, ancient histories' conjunction times and added hours, and historiographers' observation logs in detail; examining their advance and retreat for the mean, it establishes constant rates.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar is founded on Spring and Autumn eclipses, ancient records of conjunction times, and detailed observation logs; from their advance and retreat it derives mean rates.

sentences.zh: 然後以日躔、月離、先後、屈伸之變，偕損益之。

translations.literal: Then with solar progression, lunar departure, sequence, and waxing-waning change, it adjusts together.
translations.idiomatic: It then applies compensating adjustments for the sun's progression, the moon's departure, sequencing, and waxing and waning.

sentences.zh: 故經朔雖得其中，而躔離或失其正；

translations.literal: Thus though mean new moon may hit the center, progression and departure may miss their correctness;
translations.idiomatic: Mean new moon may therefore be accurate while solar progression or lunar departure still miss their marks;

sentences.zh: 若躔離各得其度，而經朔或失其中，則參求累代，必有差矣。

translations.literal: If progression and departure each get their degrees but mean new moon misses its center, then comparing across successive eras there must be discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: If progression and departure are correct but mean new moon is off, cross-checking across dynasties will inevitably reveal gaps.

sentences.zh: 三者迭相為經，若權衡相持，使千有五百年間朔必在晝，望必在夜，其加時又合，則三術之交，自然各當其正，此最微者也。

translations.literal: The three in turn serve as warp, like balance scales opposing—so that across 1,500 years new moon is always by day, full moon by night, and added time also agrees; then the three methods' conjunction naturally each hits correctness—this is the most subtle point.
translations.idiomatic: The three elements must work as mutual checks, like paired scales: over 1,500 years new moons should fall by day, full moons by night, and added times should agree—then the three methods naturally align. This is the finest calibration.

sentences.zh: 若乾度盈虛，與時消息，告譴於經數之表，變常於潛遯之中，則聖人且猶不質，非籌曆之所能及矣。

translations.literal: If the qian-degree's fullness and emptiness shifts with the season, warning and reproof beyond the warp numbers, change from constants in hidden retreat—then even sages would not fix it; calculation calendars cannot reach it.
translations.idiomatic: When celestial degrees wax and wane seasonally, sending warnings beyond what standard rates predict and altering constants in ways hidden from ordinary reckoning, even sages would not pretend to nail it down—no arithmetic calendar can capture that.

sentences.zh: 昔人考天事，多不知定朔。

translations.literal: When ancients examined celestial affairs, most did not know fixed new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars studying heaven mostly did not understand fixed new moon.

sentences.zh: 假蝕在二日，而常朔之晨，月見東方；

translations.literal: Supposing an eclipse on the second day, yet on the morning of the regular new moon the moon is seen in the east;
translations.idiomatic: Suppose an eclipse falls on the second day, yet on the morning of the regular new moon the moon is still visible in the east;

sentences.zh: 食在晦日，則常朔之夕，月見西方。

translations.literal: When the eclipse is on the last day, then on the evening of the regular new moon the moon is seen in the west.
translations.idiomatic: When an eclipse falls on the last day, on the evening of the regular new moon the moon can still be seen in the west.

sentences.zh: 理數然也。

translations.literal: Reason and number are so.
translations.idiomatic: That follows from the underlying logic.

sentences.zh: 而或以為朓朒變行，或以為曆術疎闊，遇常朔朝見則增朔餘，夕見則減朔餘，此紀曆所以屢遷也。

translations.literal: Yet some thought it crescent and gibbous changing course, some thought calendar methods coarse—when the regular new moon showed at dawn they increased new-moon remainder, at dusk they decreased it; this is why era calendars were repeatedly revised.
translations.idiomatic: Some blamed irregular crescent motion, others blamed crude calendar methods—adding to the new-moon remainder when the moon appeared at dawn on regular new-moon day, subtracting when it appeared at dusk. That is why era calendars were revised again and again.

sentences.zh: 漢編訢、李梵等又以晦猶月見，欲令蔀首先大。

translations.literal: Han's Bian Xin, Li Fan, and others also, because the last day still had the moon visible, wanted to make the obscuration head precede greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han, Bian Xin, Li Fan, and others, seeing the moon still visible on the last day, tried to make the obscuration-cycle head run ahead.

sentences.zh: 賈逵曰：「春秋書朔晦者，朔必有朔，晦必有晦，晦朔必在其月前也。

translations.literal: Jia Kui said: "When the Spring and Autumn records new moon or last day, new moon must have new moon, last day must have last day—the last day and new moon must come before their month."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui said: "When the Spring and Autumn records a new moon or last day, each must genuinely occur—the last day and new moon must fall within the month they belong to."

sentences.zh: 先大，則一月再朔，後月無朔，是朔不可必也。

translations.literal: Preceding greatly, then one month has two new moons and the next month has none—new moon cannot be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: "If the cycle runs too far ahead, one month gets two new moons and the next none—making new moon unreliable."

sentences.zh: 訢、梵等欲諧偶十六日，月朓昏，晦當滅而已。

translations.literal: Xin, Fan, and others wanted to harmonize the even sixteenth day—the crescent at dusk, last day should be invisible only.
translations.idiomatic: "Xin and Fan wanted to align with the sixteenth day—the crescent visible at dusk, the last day when it should disappear."

sentences.zh: 又晦與合朔同時，不得異日。

translations.literal: Also last day and conjunction are simultaneous—cannot be different days.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, last day and conjunction occur at the same time—they cannot fall on different days."

sentences.zh: 」考逵等所言，蓋知之矣。

translations.literal: Examining what Kui and others said, they probably understood.
translations.idiomatic: Considering what Kui and his colleagues said, they essentially understood the point.

sentences.zh: 晦朔之交，始終相際，則光盡明生之限，度數宜均。

translations.literal: Where last day and new moon meet, beginning and end adjoin—then the limit where light ends and brightness begins, the degrees ought to be even.
translations.idiomatic: At the junction of last day and new moon, where darkness ends and light begins, the degree-count should be symmetrical.

sentences.zh: 故合於子正，則晦日之朝，猶朔日之夕也，是以月皆不見。

translations.literal: Therefore when conjunction falls at zi midnight, the last day's morning is like the new moon day's evening—thus the moon is not seen at all.
translations.idiomatic: When conjunction falls at midnight (zi), the last day's dawn matches the new moon day's dusk, so the moon is invisible throughout.

sentences.zh: 若合於午正，則晦日之晨，猶二日之昏也，是以月或皆見。

translations.literal: If conjunction falls at wu midday, the last day's morning is like the second day's dusk—thus the moon may be seen throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When conjunction falls at noon (wu), the last day's dawn resembles the second day's dusk, so the moon may be visible at both times.

sentences.zh: 若陰陽遲速，軌漏加時不同，舉其中數率，去日十三度以上而月見，乃其常也。

translations.literal: If yin and yang are slow or fast, clepsydra added time differs—for the mean rate in general, when more than thirteen degrees from the sun the moon is seen, that is normal.
translations.idiomatic: Because yin and yang advance unevenly and clepsydra times differ, as a rule the moon becomes visible when it stands more than thirteen degrees from the sun.

sentences.zh: 且晦日之光未盡也，如二日之明已生也。

translations.literal: Moreover on the last day light is not yet exhausted, as on the second day brightness is already born.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day its light is not yet fully gone, just as on the second day light has already begun.

sentences.zh: 一以為是，一以為非。

translations.literal: One takes it as right, one as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: One school treats it as correct, another as erroneous.

sentences.zh: 又常朔進退，則定朔之晦、二也。

translations.literal: Also when the regular new moon advances or retreats, then the fixed new moon's last day and second day.
translations.idiomatic: Shifts in the regular new moon produce the fixed new moon's last-day and second-day cases.

sentences.zh: 或以為變，或以為常。

translations.literal: Some treat it as change, some as constant.
translations.idiomatic: Some call it an anomaly, others call it normal.

sentences.zh: 是未通於四三交質之論也。

translations.literal: This is not having mastered the four-three exchange-substance discourse.
translations.idiomatic: That shows a failure to grasp the four-three exchange principle.

sentences.zh: 綜近代諸曆，以百萬為率齊之，其所差，少或一分，多至十數失一分。

translations.literal: Synthesizing recent dynasties' calendars and aligning them at the rate of one million, their discrepancies—from as little as one part to as much as ten-plus parts missing one part.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing recent calendars on a denominator of one million, their errors range from one part to over ten parts short of one full unit.

sentences.zh: 考春秋纔差一刻，而百數年間不足成朓朒之異。

translations.literal: Examining the Spring and Autumn, the difference is barely one quarter—but across several hundred years insufficient to produce crescent-gibbous difference.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Spring and Autumn the discrepancy is only about one quarter—but over a few centuries that is too small to produce visible crescent anomalies.

sentences.zh: 施行未幾，旋復疎闊，由未知躔離經朔相求耳。

translations.literal: Implemented not long, soon again coarse and broad—from not knowing progression, departure, and mean new moon seek each other.
translations.idiomatic: Implemented briefly, each calendar soon grew coarse again because its makers did not understand how progression, departure, and mean new moon must be solved together.

sentences.zh: 李業興、甄鸞等欲求天驗，輒加減月分，遷革不已，朓朒相戾，又未知昏明之限與定朔故也。
