translations.literal: Li Yexing, Zhen Luan, and others wanting heavenly verification repeatedly added and subtracted lunar parts, revising without end, crescent and gibbous opposing—from not knowing the twilight limit and fixed new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing, Zhen Luan, and others, seeking celestial confirmation, kept adjusting lunar fractions and revising endlessly, producing contradictory crescent readings—because they did not understand twilight limits and fixed new moon.

sentences.zh: 楊偉採乾象為遲疾陰陽曆，雖知加時後天，蝕不在朔，而未能有以更之也。

translations.literal: Yang Wei drew on Qianxiang for the slow-fast yin-yang calendar; though knowing added time lagged heaven and eclipses were not at new moon, he could not revise it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei adapted the Qianxiang into a slow-fast yin-yang calendar; although he knew added times lagged heaven and eclipses did not always fall on new-moon day, he could not fix it.

sentences.zh: 何承天欲以盈縮定朔望小餘。

translations.literal: He Chengtian wished to use expansion-contraction to fix new-moon and full-moon small remainders.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian wanted to use solar expansion and contraction to fix the small remainders for new and full moons.

sentences.zh: 錢樂之以為：「推交會時刻雖審，而月頻三大二小。

translations.literal: Qian Yuezhi held: "Extrapolating conjunction times though meticulous, yet months frequently have three long and two short."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yuezhi argued: "Even if conjunction times are precise, months will too often run three long and two short."

sentences.zh: 日蝕不唯在朔，亦有在晦、二者。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses are not only at new moon—some are at last day or second day.
translations.idiomatic: "Solar eclipses occur not only on new-moon day but also on the last day or the second day."

sentences.zh: 」皮延宗又以為：「紀首合朔，大小餘當盡，若每月定之，則紀首位盈，當退一日，便應以故歲之晦為新紀之首。

translations.literal: Pi Yanzong further held: "At era head conjunction, great and small remainders should be exhausted; if fixed every month, the era head position overflows and should retreat one day—one ought to take the former year's last day as the new era head."
translations.idiomatic: Pi Yanzong added: "At era-head conjunction the great and small remainders should read zero; if the new moon is fixed month by month, the era head overflows and must retreat a day—meaning the previous year's last day becomes the new era head."

sentences.zh: 立法之制，如為不便。

translations.literal: The form of establishing law seems inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: "Such a legislative arrangement would be impractical."

sentences.zh: 」承天乃止。

translations.literal: Chengtian then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 虞𠠎曰：「所謂朔在會合，苟躔次既同，何患於頻大也？

translations.literal: Yu Xi said: "What is called new moon at conjunction—if progression positions are already the same, what worry about frequent largeness?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi said: "They say new moon should coincide with conjunction—if celestial positions already agree, why worry about months being too often long?"

sentences.zh: 日月相離，何患於頻小也？

translations.literal: Sun and moon separate—what worry about frequent smallness?
translations.idiomatic: "When sun and moon diverge, why worry about months being too often short?"

sentences.zh: 」春秋日蝕不書朔者八，公羊曰：「二日也。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn solar eclipses not recording new moon number eight; Gongshen says: "The second day."
translations.idiomatic: "Eight Spring and Autumn eclipses omit the new-moon marker; the Gongshen Commentary says: 'The second day.'"

sentences.zh: 」穀梁曰：「晦也。

translations.literal: Guliang says: "The last day."
translations.idiomatic: "The Guliang Commentary says: 'The last day.'"

sentences.zh: 」左氏曰：「官失之也。

translations.literal: Zuoshi says: "The officials missed it."
translations.idiomatic: "The Zuozhuan says: 'The record-keepers erred.'"

sentences.zh: 」劉孝孫推俱得朔日，以丘明為是，乃與劉焯皆議定朔，為有司所抑不得行。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosun calculated all obtaining new-moon day, taking Qiuming as correct; he and Liu Chuo both proposed fixed new moon, suppressed by the authorities and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun calculated that all eight should fall on new-moon day and sided with Qiu Ming; he and Liu Chuo both advocated fixed new moon but were blocked by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 傅仁均始為定朔，而曰「晦不東見，朔不西朓」，以為昏晦當滅，亦訢、梵之論。

translations.literal: Fu Renjun first made fixed new moon, saying "last day not seen in the east, new moon not waxing in the west"—holding dusk of last day should be invisible; also Xin's and Fan's theory.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Renjun pioneered fixed new moon but held that "the last day should not appear in the east, nor new moon wax in the west"—the moon should vanish at last-day dusk—the same logic as Xin and Fan.

sentences.zh: 淳風因循皇極，皇極密於麟德，以朔餘乘三千四十，乃一萬除之，就全數得千六百一十三。

translations.literal: Chunfeng followed the Huangji; the Huangji is denser than Lindé—multiplying new-moon remainder by three thousand forty, then dividing by ten thousand, taking the whole number yields one thousand six hundred thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng followed the Huangji calendar, which is finer than the Lindé; multiplying the new-moon remainder by 3,040 and dividing by 10,000 gives the whole number 1,613.

sentences.zh: 又以九百四十乘之，以三千四十而一，得四百九十八秒七十五太彊，是為四分餘率。

translations.literal: Again multiplying by nine hundred forty, dividing by three thousand forty, yields four hundred ninety-eight seconds seventy-five great-strong—this is the quarter-remainder surplus rate.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying again by 940 and dividing by 3,040 yields 498 seconds plus 75/96—forming the Quarter-Remainder surplus rate.

sentences.zh: 劉洪以古曆斗分太彊，久當後天，乃先正斗分，而後求朔法，故朔餘之母煩矣。

translations.literal: Liu Hong held the ancient calendar's dipper fraction too strong; long it should lag heaven—so he first corrected the dipper fraction, then sought the new-moon method; thus the new-moon remainder's denominator grew cumbersome.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong found the ancient calendar's dipper fraction too large, which would eventually make dates lag heaven; he corrected the dipper fraction first and then derived the new-moon method, making the new-moon denominator unwieldy.

sentences.zh: 韓翊以乾象朔分太弱，久當先天，乃先考朔分，而後覆求度法，故度餘之母煩矣。

translations.literal: Han Yi held the Qianxiang new-moon fraction too weak; long it should precede heaven—so he first examined the new-moon fraction, then overlaid the degree method; thus the degree remainder's denominator grew cumbersome.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yi found the Qianxiang new-moon fraction too small, which would eventually make dates run ahead of heaven; he fixed the new-moon fraction first and then reworked the degree method, making the degree denominator unwieldy.

sentences.zh: 何承天反覆相求，使氣朔之母合簡易之率，而星數不得同元矣。

translations.literal: He Chengtian repeatedly sought each other, making qi and new-moon denominators match a simple rate—yet star numbers could not share the same origin.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian iterated until qi and new-moon denominators matched a simpler rate, but star-cycle numbers could no longer share a common origin.

sentences.zh: 李業興、宋景業、甄鸞、張賓欲使六甲之首眾術同元，而氣朔餘分，其細甚矣。

translations.literal: Li Yexing, Song Jingye, Zhen Luan, and Zhang Bin wished to make the six jia heads of all methods share the same origin—yet qi, new-moon, and remainder fractions were exceedingly fine.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing, Song Jingye, Zhen Luan, and Zhang Bin wanted all methods to share the same origin at the six jia heads, but the qi, new-moon, and remainder fractions were extraordinarily fine.

sentences.zh: 麟德曆有總法，開元曆有通法，故積歲如月分之數，而後閏餘偕盡。

translations.literal: The Lindé calendar has a general method, the Kaiyuan calendar a universal method—thus accumulated years like month-fraction numbers, and then intercalary remainder is jointly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar has a general method and the Kaiyuan a universal method, so accumulated years match the month-fraction count and the intercalary remainder is fully exhausted together.

sentences.zh: 考漢元光已來史官注記，日蝕有加時者凡三十七事，麟德曆得五，開元曆得二十二。

translations.literal: Examining historiographers' annotated records from Han Yuanguang onward, solar eclipses with added time total thirty-seven cases—the Lindé calendar gets five, the Kaiyuan calendar twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing historiographers' notes from Han Yuanguang onward, thirty-seven solar eclipses record an added time; the Lindé calendar matches five, the Kaiyuan twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 其四沒滅略例曰：

translations.literal: Its fourth, the summary rules for obscuration and extinction, says:
translations.idiomatic: The fourth section, summary rules for obscuration and extinction, states:

sentences.zh: 古者以中氣所盈之日為沒，沒分偕盡者為滅。

translations.literal: In antiquity the day filled by mid-qi was called obscuration; when obscuration fractions were jointly exhausted it was called extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Anciently, the day when mid-qi filled the month was called obscuration; when obscuration fractions were fully exhausted it was called extinction.

sentences.zh: 開元曆以中分所盈為沒，朔分所虛為滅。

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan calendar takes what mid-fraction fills as obscuration, what new-moon fraction empties as extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar treats what the mid-fraction fills as obscuration and what the new-moon fraction empties as extinction.

sentences.zh: 綜終歲沒分，謂之策餘。

translations.literal: Summing the year's obscuration fraction is called the divination remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The year's total obscuration fraction is called the divination remainder.

sentences.zh: 終歲滅分，謂之用差。

translations.literal: The year's extinction fraction is called the use difference.
translations.idiomatic: The year's total extinction fraction is called the use difference.

sentences.zh: 皆歸于揲易再扐而後掛也。

translations.literal: Both return to the Changes' divination of twice bending the stalks and then hanging.
translations.idiomatic: Both derive from the Yijing practice of dividing stalks twice before hanging the remainder.

sentences.zh: 其五卦候議曰：

translations.literal: Its fifth, the hexagram-season discourse, says:
translations.idiomatic: The fifth section, the hexagram-season discourse, states:

sentences.zh: 七十二候，原于周公時訓。

translations.literal: The seventy-two seasons originate in the Duke of Zhou's seasonal instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The seventy-two seasons originate in the Duke of Zhou's seasonal instructions.

sentences.zh: 月令雖頗有增益，然先後之次則同。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances though somewhat augmented, yet the order of sequence is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances adds some entries, but their sequence is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 自後魏始載于曆，乃依易軌所傳，不合經義。

translations.literal: From Northern Wei they were first loaded into calendars, relying on the Changes track transmitted— not matching canonical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei first embedded them in calendars, following a transmitted Yijing track that does not match canonical doctrine.

sentences.zh: 今改從古。

translations.literal: Now we change to follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar reverts to the ancient arrangement.

sentences.zh: 其六卦議曰：

translations.literal: Its sixth, the hexagram discourse, says:
translations.idiomatic: The sixth section, the hexagram discourse, states:

sentences.zh: 十二月卦出於孟氏章句，其說易本於氣，而後以人事明之。

translations.literal: The twelve-month hexagrams come from Meng's commentary; the theory grounds the Changes in qi, then clarifies it with human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve-month hexagrams come from Meng's commentary, grounding the Changes in seasonal qi and then explaining them through human affairs.

sentences.zh: 京氏又以卦爻配期之日，坎、離、震、兌，其用事自分、至之首，皆得八十分日之七十三。

translations.literal: Jing Fang further matched hexagram lines to period days—Kan, Li, Zhen, and Dui, their governing from equinox and solstice heads each get seventy-three parts of eighty day-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang further assigned hexagram lines to period days—Kan, Li, Zhen, and Dui, governing from equinox and solstice heads, each receive seventy-three parts in eighty day-parts.

sentences.zh: 頤、晉、井、大畜，皆五日十四分，餘皆六日七分，止於占災眚與吉凶善敗之事。

translations.literal: Yi, Jin, Jing, and Da Chu each get five days fourteen parts; the rest each six days seven parts—stopping at divining disasters and good and ill fortune, success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Jin, Jing, and Da Chu each get five days and fourteen parts; the rest six days and seven parts—limited to divining calamities and matters of fortune, success, and failure.

sentences.zh: 至於觀陰陽之變，則錯亂而不明。

translations.literal: As for observing yin-yang change, then confused and unclear.
translations.idiomatic: For tracking yin-yang transformation, however, the system becomes confused and unclear.

sentences.zh: 自乾象曆以降，皆因京氏。

translations.literal: From the Qianxiang calendar downward, all follow Jing Fang.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qianxiang calendar onward, all follow Jing Fang.

sentences.zh: 惟天保曆依易通統軌圖。

translations.literal: Only the Tianbao calendar follows the Changes Comprehensive Track Diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Tianbao calendar follows the Comprehensive Yijing Track Diagram.

sentences.zh: 自入十有二節、五卦、初爻，相次用事，及上爻而與中氣偕終，非京氏本旨及七略所傳。

translations.literal: From entering the twelve minor nodes, five hexagrams, first line, governing in succession, reaching the top line and jointly ending with mid-qi—not Jing Fang's original intent nor what the Seven Summaries transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Starting from the twelve minor nodes, five hexagrams, and the first line governing in turn until the top line ends with mid-qi—this is neither Jing Fang's original intent nor what the Seven Summaries records.

sentences.zh: 按郎顗所傳，卦皆六日七分，不以初爻相次用事，齊曆謬矣。

translations.literal: According to Lang Yi's transmission, hexagrams are all six days seven parts, not first-line governing in succession—the Qi calendar was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Per Lang Yi's transmission, each hexagram governs six days and seven parts without first-line succession—the Qi calendar erred.

sentences.zh: 又京氏減七十三分，為四正之候，其說不經，欲附會緯文「七日來復」而已。

translations.literal: Also Jing Fang reduced seventy-three parts for the four cardinal seasons—his theory uncanonical, merely wanting to attach to the apocryphal text "seven days and it returns."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang also cut seventy-three parts for the four cardinal seasons—an unorthodox theory meant only to fit the apocryphal line "it returns in seven days."

sentences.zh: 夫陽精道消，靜而無迹，不過極其正數，至七而通矣。

translations.literal: When yang essence's path wanes, still and without trace, it does not exceed its correct number—reaching seven it passes through.
translations.idiomatic: When yang essence wanes along its path, still and traceless, it does not exceed its proper count—at seven it completes its cycle.

sentences.zh: 七者，陽之正也，安在益其小餘，令七日而後雷動地中乎？

translations.literal: Seven is yang's correctness—where is increasing its small remainder, making thunder stir underground after seven days?
translations.idiomatic: Seven is yang's proper number—why inflate the small remainder to make thunder stir underground only after seven days?

sentences.zh: 當據孟氏，自冬至初，中孚用事，一月之策，九六、七八，是為三十。

translations.literal: One ought to follow Meng— from winter solstice beginning, Zhong Fu governs; one month's divination tally, nine-six and seven-eight, makes thirty.
translations.idiomatic: One should follow Meng: from winter solstice Zhong Fu governs; one month's divination tally of nine-six and seven-eight totals thirty.

sentences.zh: 而卦以地六，候以天五，五六相乘，消息一變，十有二變而歲復初。

translations.literal: Hexagrams use earth six, seasons use heaven five—five and six multiplied, one wax-wane change; twelve changes and the year returns to the start.
translations.idiomatic: Hexagrams use earth's six, seasons heaven's five—five times six yields one wax-wane shift; twelve shifts and the year begins anew.

sentences.zh: 坎、震、離、兌，二十四氣，次主一爻，其初則二至、二分也。

translations.literal: Kan, Zhen, Li, and Dui—the twenty-four qi, each in turn governing one line; at the start then the two solstices and two equinoxes.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, Zhen, Li, and Dui govern the twenty-four qi, each presiding over one line; at the outset come the two solstices and two equinoxes.

sentences.zh: 坎以陰包陽，故自北正，微陽動於下，升而未達，極於二月，凝涸之氣消，坎運終焉。

translations.literal: Kan wraps yang in yin—therefore from the northern cardinal, faint yang stirs below, rising yet not attained, reaching the second month; congealed frozen qi vanishes, Kan's course ends.
translations.idiomatic: Kan wraps yang within yin—starting from the northern cardinal, faint yang stirs below, rising but not yet fulfilled; by the second month frozen qi melts and Kan's turn ends.

sentences.zh: 春分出於震，始據萬物之元，為主於內，則羣陰化而從之，極于南正，而豐大之變窮，震功究焉。

translations.literal: Spring equinox comes from Zhen—first occupying the origin of the myriad things, governing within; then the mass yin transforms and follows, reaching the southern cardinal; then the great abundance change is exhausted, Zhen's work is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Spring equinox arises from Zhen, taking hold of the origin of all things and governing inward; yin transforms and follows until the southern cardinal, where abundant growth reaches its limit and Zhen's work is done.

sentences.zh: 離以陽包陰，故自南正，微陰生於地下，積而未章，至于八月，文明之質衰，離運終焉。

translations.literal: Li wraps yin in yang—therefore from the southern cardinal, faint yin is born underground, accumulating yet not manifest, reaching the eighth month; civilized substance wanes, Li's course ends.
translations.idiomatic: Li wraps yin within yang—starting from the southern cardinal, faint yin forms underground, gathering but not yet visible; by the eighth month cultured brilliance fades and Li's turn ends.

sentences.zh: 仲秋陰形于兌，始循萬物之末，為主於內，羣陽降而承之，極於北正，而天澤之施窮，兌功究焉。

translations.literal: Mid-autumn yin takes form in Dui—first following the myriad things' end, governing within; the mass yang descends and receives it, reaching the northern cardinal; then heaven's marsh bestowal is exhausted, Dui's work is complete.
translations.idiomatic: At mid-autumn yin manifests in Dui, tracing the waning of all things and governing inward; yang falls away and yields, reaching the northern cardinal where heaven's moist bounty ends and Dui's turn is complete.

sentences.zh: 故陽七之靜始於坎，陽九之動始于震，陰八之靜始于離，陰六之動始于兌。

translations.literal: Therefore yang-seven's stillness begins at Kan, yang-nine's movement begins at Zhen, yin-eight's stillness begins at Li, yin-six's movement begins at Dui.
translations.idiomatic: Thus yang-seven's quiescence starts with Kan, yang-nine's activity with Zhen, yin-eight's quiescence with Li, and yin-six's activity with Dui.

sentences.zh: 故四象之變，皆兼六爻，而中節之應備矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the four images' change all include six lines, and mid-node response is complete.
translations.idiomatic: The four images' transformations each encompass six lines, so the responses at mid-nodes are fully accounted for.

sentences.zh: 易爻當日，十有二中，直全卦之初；

translations.literal: Changes lines match days—the twelve mid-qi align with the whole hexagram's beginning;
translations.idiomatic: Each Yijing line corresponds to a day—the twelve mid-qi align with the start of the full hexagram;

sentences.zh: 十有二節，直全卦之中。

translations.literal: The twelve minor nodes align with the whole hexagram's middle.
translations.idiomatic: the twelve minor nodes align with its midpoint.

sentences.zh: 齊曆又以節在貞，氣在悔，非是。

translations.literal: The Qi calendar again puts minor nodes at Zhen and qi at Hui—not correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi calendar wrongly places minor nodes at Zhen and qi at Hui.

sentences.zh: 其七日度議曰：

translations.literal: Its seventh, the solar-degree discourse, says:
translations.idiomatic: The seventh section, the solar-degree discourse, states:

sentences.zh: 古曆，日有常度，天周為歲終，故係星度于節氣。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars held the sun has constant degrees and heaven's circuit completes the year—therefore star degrees were tied to seasonal nodes.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars assumed the sun moved at a fixed rate and that a full circuit of heaven marked the year's end, so star degrees were tied to seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 其說似是而非，故久而益差。

translations.literal: Its theory seems right yet is wrong—therefore over time error grows.
translations.idiomatic: The theory seems plausible but is wrong, so error accumulates over time.

sentences.zh: 虞喜覺之，使天為天，歲為歲，乃立差以追其變，使五十年退一度。

translations.literal: Yu Xi perceived this—let heaven be heaven, year be year—then established difference to track the change, making fifty years retreat one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi saw the problem: treat heaven and the year separately, then introduce a correction tracking the drift—one degree every fifty years.

sentences.zh: 何承天以為太過，乃倍其年，而反不及。

translations.literal: He Chengtian held this excessive—so he doubled the years, yet fell short instead.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian thought that too fast and doubled the interval, but that proved too slow.

sentences.zh: 皇極取二家中數為七十五年，蓋近之矣。

translations.literal: Huangji took the mean of the two schools as seventy-five years—nearly close.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangji calendar split the difference at seventy-five years per degree—close to the mark.

sentences.zh: 考古史及日官候簿，以通法之三十九分太為一歲之差。

translations.literal: Examining ancient histories and solar officials' observation logs, the universal method's thirty-nine parts great makes one year's difference.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing ancient histories and solar observation logs, the Kaiyuan universal method's 39 parts plus 39/96 yields one degree of precession per year.

sentences.zh: 自帝堯演紀之端，在虛一度。

translations.literal: From Emperor Yao's era-count beginning, at Xu one degree.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Yao's era-count, the sun stood at one degree of Xu.

sentences.zh: 及今開元甲子，却三十六度，而乾策復初矣。

translations.literal: Reaching today's Kaiyuan jiazi, it has retreated thirty-six degrees, and the qian tally returns to the start.
translations.idiomatic: By the Kaiyuan jiazi year it has retreated thirty-six degrees, and the qian tally has cycled back to its origin.

sentences.zh: 日在虛一，則鳥、火、昴、虛皆以仲月昏中，合于堯典。

translations.literal: Sun at Xu one—then Bird, Fire, Mao, and Xu all at mid-month dusk culmination, matching the Canon of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: With the sun at one degree of Xu, Bird, Fire, Mao, and Xu all culminate at dusk in their proper months, matching the Canon of Yao.

sentences.zh: 劉炫依大明曆四十五年差一度，則冬至在虛、危，而夏至火已過中矣。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan following the Daming calendar's forty-five years per degree difference—then winter solstice is at Xu and Wei, yet summer solstice Fire has already passed culmination.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, using the Daming calendar's rate of one degree every forty-five years, places winter solstice at Xu and Wei while summer solstice Fire has already passed culmination.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝據虞𠠎曆，百八十六年差一度，則唐、虞之際，日在斗、牛間，而冬至昴尚未中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang following Yu Xi's calendar, one hundred eighty-six years per degree difference—then at the Tang and Yu era the sun was between Dou and Niu, yet winter solstice Mao had not yet culminated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, using Yu Xi's rate of one degree every 186 years, puts the sun between Dou and Niu in the Tang-Yu era while winter solstice Mao has not yet culminated.

sentences.zh: 以為皆承閏後節前，月却使然。

translations.literal: He held all follow intercalation after, node before—the month retreating makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: He argued this all stemmed from intercalation lagging behind the nodes—the month falling back caused the mismatch.

sentences.zh: 而此經終始一歲之事，不容頓有四閏，故淳風因為之說曰：「若冬至昴中，則夏至秋分星火、星虛，皆在未正之西。

translations.literal: Yet this classic's account of a full year's events cannot suddenly have four intercalations—therefore Chunfeng offered this explanation: "If winter solstice Mao culminates, then summer solstice and autumn equinox Fire Star and Void Star are all west of wei midday."
translations.idiomatic: But a full year's events in this classic cannot involve four intercalations at once, so Chunfeng argued: "If winter solstice Mao culminates, then summer solstice and autumn equinox Fire and Void stars all lie west of the wei meridian."

sentences.zh: 若以夏至火中，秋分虛中，則冬至昴在巳正之東。

translations.literal: If taking summer solstice Fire culmination and autumn equinox Void culmination, then winter solstice Mao is east of si midday.
translations.idiomatic: "If summer solstice Fire and autumn equinox Void culminate instead, winter solstice Mao lies east of the si meridian."

sentences.zh: 互有盈縮，不足以為歲差證。

translations.literal: Each has surplus and deficit—insufficient to serve as precession proof.
translations.idiomatic: "The two cases contradict each other and cannot prove precession."

sentences.zh: 」是又不然。

translations.literal: This again is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That argument is also wrong.

sentences.zh: 今以四象分天，北正玄枵中，虛九度；

translations.literal: Now dividing heaven by the four images—northern cardinal Xuanxiao center, Xu nine degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Dividing heaven by the four images: the northern cardinal Xuanxiao centers on nine degrees of Xu;

sentences.zh: 東正大火中，房二度；

translations.literal: Eastern cardinal Great Fire center, Fang two degrees;
translations.idiomatic: the eastern cardinal Great Fire on two degrees of Fang;

sentences.zh: 南正鶉火中，七星七度；

translations.literal: Southern cardinal Quail Fire center, Seven Stars seven degrees;
translations.idiomatic: the southern cardinal Quail Fire on seven degrees of Seven Stars;

sentences.zh: 西正大梁中，昴七度。

translations.literal: Western cardinal Great Bridge center, Mao seven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: the western cardinal Great Bridge on seven degrees of Mao.

sentences.zh: 總晝夜刻以約周天，命距中星，則春分南正中天，秋分北正中天。

translations.literal: Summing day-night quarters to approximate the full circuit, assigning distance from culmination stars—then spring equinox southern cardinal at zenith, autumn equinox northern cardinal at zenith.
translations.idiomatic: Summing day-night quarters to approximate the full circuit and assigning distance from culmination stars, spring equinox finds the southern cardinal at zenith and autumn equinox the northern cardinal at zenith.

sentences.zh: 冬至之昏，西正在午東十八度；

translations.literal: Winter solstice dusk—the western cardinal eighteen degrees east of wu;
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice dusk the western cardinal lies eighteen degrees east of the wu meridian;

sentences.zh: 夏至之昏，東正在午西十八度：軌漏使然也。

translations.literal: Summer solstice dusk—the eastern cardinal eighteen degrees west of wu: clepsydra track makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: at summer solstice dusk the eastern cardinal lies eighteen degrees west of wu—the clepsydra track requires it.

sentences.zh: 冬至，日在虛一度，則春分昏張一度中；

translations.literal: Winter solstice, sun at Xu one degree—then spring equinox dusk Zhang one degree culminates;
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice with the sun at one degree of Xu, Zhang at one degree culminates at spring equinox dusk;

sentences.zh: 秋分虛九度中；

translations.literal: Autumn equinox Xu nine degrees culminates;
translations.idiomatic: Xu at nine degrees culminates at autumn equinox;

sentences.zh: 冬至胃二度中，昴距星直午正之東十二度；

translations.literal: Winter solstice Wei two degrees culminates, Mao distance star directly wu midday east twelve degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Wei at two degrees culminates at winter solstice, with Mao's distance star twelve degrees east of the wu meridian;

sentences.zh: 夏至尾十一度中，心後星直午正之西十二度。

translations.literal: Summer solstice Wei eleven degrees culminates, Xin rear star directly wu midday west twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Wei at eleven degrees culminates at summer solstice, with the rear star of Xin twelve degrees west of the wu meridian.

sentences.zh: 四序進退，不逾午正間。

translations.literal: The four seasons' advance and retreat do not exceed between wu midday.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons' advance and retreat stay within the wu meridian zone.

sentences.zh: 而淳風以為不叶，非也。

translations.literal: Yet Chunfeng held it did not harmonize—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng thought this did not harmonize—but he was wrong.

sentences.zh: 又王孝通云：「如歲差自昴至壁，則堯前七千餘載，冬至，日應在東井。

translations.literal: Also Wang Xiaotong said: "If precession runs from Mao to Bi, then seven thousand-plus years before Yao, winter solstice the sun should be at Dongjing."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaotong also argued: "If precession moved from Mao to Bi, then 7,000-plus years before Yao, winter solstice should find the sun at Dongjing."

sentences.zh: 井極北，故暑；

translations.literal: Jing is most north, therefore heat;
translations.idiomatic: "Jing is farthest north, so it would be hot;

sentences.zh: 斗極南，故寒。

translations.literal: Dou is most south, therefore cold.
translations.idiomatic: Dou is farthest south, so it would be cold.

sentences.zh: 寒暑易位，必不然矣。

translations.literal: Cold and heat exchanging positions—surely not so.
translations.idiomatic: Heat and cold would swap places—which cannot be right."

sentences.zh: 」所謂歲差者，日與黃道俱差也。

translations.literal: What is called precession—the sun and ecliptic both shift.
translations.idiomatic: Precession means both the sun and the ecliptic shift together.

sentences.zh: 假冬至日躔大火之中，則春分黃道交於虛九，而南至之軌更出房、心外，距赤道亦二十四度。

translations.literal: Suppose winter solstice sun progresses in Great Fire's center—then spring equinox ecliptic crosses Xu nine, and south-arrival's track further exits beyond Fang and Xin, distance from equator also twenty-four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose winter solstice finds the sun in Great Fire: spring equinox still places the ecliptic at Xu nine, and the south-arrival track still passes beyond Fang and Xin, twenty-four degrees from the equator.

sentences.zh: 設在東井，差亦如之。

translations.literal: Set at Dongjing—the difference is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same holds if the sun stood at Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 若日在東井，猶去極最近，表景最短，則是分、至常居其所。

translations.literal: If the sun is at Dongjing, still nearest the pole, gnomon shadow shortest—then equinox and solstice constantly dwell in their places.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun at Dongjing were still nearest the pole with the shortest gnomon shadow, equinoxes and solstices would stay fixed in place.

sentences.zh: 黃道不遷，日行不退，又安得謂之歲差乎？

translations.literal: The ecliptic does not shift, the sun's daily path does not retreat—how can one call it precession?
translations.idiomatic: With the ecliptic unmoved and the sun's daily motion unchanged, how could that be precession?

sentences.zh: 孝通及淳風以為冬至日在斗十三度，昏東壁中，昴在巽維之左，向明之位，非無星也。

translations.literal: Xiaotong and Chunfeng held winter solstice sun at Dou thirteen degrees, dusk Dongbi culminates, Mao at xun-wei's left, the position facing light—not without stars.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong and Chunfeng held that at winter solstice the sun stands at thirteen degrees of Dou, Dongbi culminates at dusk, and Mao lies in the bright southeast quadrant—stars are plainly visible there.

sentences.zh: 水星昏正可以為仲冬之候，何必援昴於始覿之際，以惑民之視聽哉！

translations.literal: Mercury at dusk culmination can serve as mid-winter's sign—why must one invoke Mao at first sight to confuse the people's eyes and ears!
translations.idiomatic: Mercury culminating at dusk suffices as a mid-winter marker—why drag in Mao at first visibility to mislead the people?

sentences.zh: 夏后氏四百三十二年，日却差五度。

translations.literal: Xia dynasty four hundred thirty-two years, sun retreating differs five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Over the Xia dynasty's 432 years the sun's position retreated five degrees.

sentences.zh: 太康十二年戊子歲冬至，應在女十一度。

translations.literal: Taikang year 12 wuzi year winter solstice should be at Nü eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice of Taikang year 12, a wuzi year, should fall at eleven degrees of Nü.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「乃季秋月朔，辰弗集于房。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Then the third month of autumn, new moon—the chen did not gather at Fang."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents record: "In the third month of autumn, at new moon, the chen did not gather at Fang."

sentences.zh: 」劉炫曰：「房，所舍之次也。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan said: "Fang—the lodge's station."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan said: "Fang is the station where the sun lodges."

sentences.zh: 集，會也。

translations.literal: Ji—meeting.
translations.idiomatic: "Ji means to meet."

sentences.zh: 會，合也。

translations.literal: Hui—conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: "Hui means conjunction."

sentences.zh: 不合則日蝕可知。

translations.literal: Not conjoined—then solar eclipse can be known.
translations.idiomatic: "If they fail to conjoin, an eclipse is implied."

sentences.zh: 或以房為房星，知不然者，且日之所在正可推而知之。

translations.literal: Some take Fang as the Fang star—knowing it is not so: the sun's position can rightly be extrapolated and known.
translations.idiomatic: Some take Fang to mean the Fang star, but the sun's position can be calculated directly.

sentences.zh: 君子慎疑，寧當以日在之宿為文？

translations.literal: The noble person is cautious in doubt—should one not take the lodge where the sun stands as the text?
translations.idiomatic: A careful scholar should read the text as naming the sun's lodge, not the star Fang.

sentences.zh: 近代善曆者，推仲康時九月合朔，已在房星北矣。

translations.literal: Recent skilled calendrists calculate Zhongkang's time ninth month conjunction already north of the Fang star.
translations.idiomatic: Recent skilled calendrists calculate that Zhongkang's ninth-month conjunction already lay north of the Fang star.

sentences.zh: 」按古文「集」與「輯」義同。

translations.literal: Examining ancient text, "ji" and "ji" (輯) share meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ancient text, "ji" (gather) and "ji" (harmonize) share the same sense.

sentences.zh: 日月嘉會，而陰陽輯睦，則陽不疚乎位，以常其明，陰亦含章示沖，以隱其形。

translations.literal: Sun and moon fine meeting, yin and yang harmoniously joined—then yang does not fault its position, maintaining its brightness; yin also holds its pattern showing emptiness, hiding its form.
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon meet properly and yin-yang harmonize, yang keeps its place and brightness while yin modestly hides its form.

sentences.zh: 若變而相傷，則不輯矣。

translations.literal: If they change and mutually harm, then not harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: When they clash and harm each other, harmony is lost.

sentences.zh: 房者，辰之所次，星者，所次之名，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Fang is the chen's station; star is the station's name—their measure is one.
translations.idiomatic: Fang names the chen station; "star" names the station itself—the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 又春秋傳「辰在斗柄」、「天策焞焞」、「降婁之初」、「辰尾之末」，君子言之，不以為繆，何獨慎疑於房星哉？

translations.literal: Also the Spring and Autumn Annals "chen at the Dipper's handle," "Heaven's tally blazing," "at the start of Jianglou," "at the end of chen's tail"—the noble person speaks thus, not holding it absurd—why alone be cautious in doubt about the Fang star?
translations.idiomatic: The Zuozhuan likewise says "chen at the Dipper's handle," "Heaven's tally blazing," "at Jianglou's start," "at chen-tail's end"—nobody treats those as absurd; why doubt only the Fang star?

sentences.zh: 新曆仲康五年癸巳歲九月庚戌朔，日蝕在房二度。

translations.literal: The new calendar Zhongkang year 5 guisi year ninth month gengxu new moon, solar eclipse at Fang two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar places Zhongkang year 5, a guisi year, ninth month gengxu new moon, with a solar eclipse at two degrees of Fang.

sentences.zh: 炫以五子之歌，仲康當是其一，肇位四海，復脩大禹之典，其五年，羲、和失職，則王命徂征。

translations.literal: Xuan by the Five Sons' Song holds Zhongkang should be one of them, ascending to rule the four seas, restoring Great Yu's canon—in his fifth year Xi and He neglected duty, then the king's command went to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, citing the Song of the Five Sons, identifies Zhongkang as one of them; he took the throne, restored Yu's institutions, and in his fifth year, when Xi and He failed in duty, the king sent an expedition against them.

sentences.zh: 虞𠠎以為仲康元年，非也。

translations.literal: Yu Xi held Zhongkang year 1—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi's claim that this was Zhongkang's first year is wrong.

sentences.zh: 國語單子曰：「辰角見而雨畢，天根見而水涸，本見而草木節解，駟見而隕霜，火見而清風戒寒。

translations.literal: The Discourses of the States, Master Shan said: "When Horn appears rain ends, when Sky Root appears waters dry up, when Root appears plants' nodes break, when Si appears frost falls, when Fire appears clear wind warns of cold."
translations.idiomatic: In the Discourses of the States, Master Shan said: "When the Horn rises, the rains finish; when the Sky Root appears, waters recede; when the Root appears, plants shed their leaves; when Si appears, frost falls; when Fire appears, the clear wind warns of cold."

sentences.zh: 」韋昭以為夏后氏之令，周人所因。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao held it the Xia dynasty's command, Zhou people followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao held this to be a Xia seasonal ordinance that the Zhou adopted.

sentences.zh: 推夏后氏之初，秋分後五日，日在氐十三度，龍角盡見，時雨可以畢矣。

translations.literal: Extrapolating the Xia dynasty's beginning, five days after autumn equinox the sun at Di thirteen degrees, Dragon Horn fully visible—seasonal rain can then finish.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating to early Xia, five days after autumn equinox the sun stood at thirteen degrees of Di and the Dragon Horn was fully visible—the seasonal rains could then end.

sentences.zh: 又先寒露三日，天根朝覿，時訓「爰始收潦」，而月令亦云「水涸」。

translations.literal: Also three days before Cold Dew, Sky Root visible at dawn—the seasonal instruction "then begin gathering the flood," and the Monthly Ordinances also say "waters dry up."
translations.idiomatic: Three days before Cold Dew the Sky Root appeared at dawn—the seasonal instruction says "then begin gathering the floodwaters," and the Monthly Ordinances likewise say "waters dry up."

sentences.zh: 後寒露十日，日在尾八度而本見，又五日而駟見。

translations.literal: Ten days after Cold Dew, sun at Wei eight degrees and Root appears; five days more and Si appears.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after Cold Dew the sun reached eight degrees of Wei and the Root appeared; five days later Si appeared.

sentences.zh: 故隕霜則蟄蟲墐戶。

translations.literal: Therefore when frost falls the hibernating insects seal their doors.
translations.idiomatic: When frost falls, hibernating insects seal their burrows.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成據當時所見，謂天根朝見，在季秋之末，以月令為謬。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan according to what was then seen held Sky Root visible at dawn in late autumn's end—the Monthly Ordinances erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, judging by what he could see in his own day, placed Sky Root's dawn visibility at late autumn and called the Monthly Ordinances wrong.

sentences.zh: 韋昭以仲秋水始涸，天根見乃竭。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao held mid-autumn waters begin drying, Sky Root appearing then exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao held that waters begin to recede in mid-autumn and are fully dry when the Sky Root appears.

sentences.zh: 皆非是。

translations.literal: Both are not so.
translations.idiomatic: Both are incorrect.

sentences.zh: 霜降六日，日在尾末，火星初見，營室昏中，於是始脩城郭、宮室。

translations.literal: Six days after Frost Descent, sun at Wei's end, Fire Star first appears, Encampment at dusk culmination—then begin repairing walls and palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Six days after Frost Descent the sun stood at the end of Wei, Mars first appeared, and Encampment culminated at dusk—time to begin repairing walls and palaces.

sentences.zh: 故時儆曰：「營室之中，土功其始。

translations.literal: Therefore the seasonal warning says: "Within Encampment, earthworks begin."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the seasonal warning: "When Encampment is centered, earthworks begin."

sentences.zh: 火之初見，期于司理。

translations.literal: Fire's first appearance, expected at the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: "When Fire first appears, the Minister of Works takes charge."

sentences.zh: 」麟德曆霜降後五日，火伏。

translations.literal: The Lindé calendar five days after Frost Descent, Fire hidden.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar has Fire hidden five days after Frost Descent.

sentences.zh: 小雪後十日，晨見。

translations.literal: Ten days after Lesser Snow, visible at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: It becomes visible at dawn ten days after Lesser Snow.

sentences.zh: 至大雪而後定星中，日且南至，冰壯地坼。

translations.literal: Reaching Greater Snow then fixed stars centered, sun also south arrival, ice solid ground splits.
translations.idiomatic: Only by Greater Snow are the fixed stars centered, the sun at south arrival, and ice thick enough to crack the ground.

sentences.zh: 又非土功之始也。

translations.literal: Again not earthworks' beginning.
translations.idiomatic: That is far too late to mark the start of earthworks.

sentences.zh: 夏曆十二次，立春，日在東壁三度，於太初星距壁一度太也。

translations.literal: Xia calendar's twelve stations—Start of Spring, sun at Dongbi three degrees, from Taichu stars distance from Bi one degree great.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xia calendar's twelve stations, at Start of Spring the sun stood at three degrees of Dongbi—one degree great from the Taichu star-distance at Bi.

sentences.zh: 顓頊曆上元甲寅歲正月甲寅晨初合朔立春，七曜皆直艮維之首。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu's calendar upper origin jiayin year first month jiayin dawn initial conjunction Start of Spring—the seven luminaries all directly at gen-wei's head.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanxu calendar's upper origin is jiayin year, first month: jiayin dawn, initial conjunction at Start of Spring, all seven luminaries aligned at gen-wei.

sentences.zh: 蓋重黎受職於顓頊，九黎亂德，二官咸廢，帝堯復其子孫，命掌天地四時，以及虞、夏。

translations.literal: Chongli received office from Zhuanxu; the Nine Li corrupted virtue; both officials were abolished; Emperor Yao restored their descendants, ordering them to govern heaven and earth and the four seasons—through to Yu and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli received his post from Zhuanxu; the Nine Li corrupted order and both offices lapsed until Emperor Yao restored their descendants to govern heaven, earth, and the four seasons through Yu and Xia.

sentences.zh: 故本其所由生，命曰顓頊，其實夏曆也。

translations.literal: Therefore naming from where it arose, called Zhuanxu—in fact the Xia calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Named after its originator Zhuanxu, it is in fact the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 湯作殷曆，更以十一月甲子合朔冬至為上元。

translations.literal: Tang made the Yin calendar, changing to eleventh month jiazi conjunction winter solstice as upper origin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang created the Yin calendar, making the eleventh month's jiazi conjunction at winter solstice the upper origin.

sentences.zh: 周人因之，距羲、和千祀，昏明中星率差半次。

translations.literal: Zhou people followed it—distance from Xi and He a thousand sacrifices, dusk-dawn culmination stars on average differ half a station.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou followed it; a thousand reign-years from Xi and He, dusk-and-dawn culmination stars differed by half a station on average.

sentences.zh: 夏時直月節者，皆當十有二中，故因循夏令。

translations.literal: Xia times directly at month nodes all should be at the twelve mid-qi—therefore following the Xia command.
translations.idiomatic: In Xia times the monthly nodes aligned with the twelve mid-qi, so the Zhou followed Xia seasonal practice.

sentences.zh: 其後呂不韋得之，以為秦法，更考中星，斷取近距，以乙卯歲正月己巳合朔立春為上元。

translations.literal: Later Lü Buwei obtained it, making it Qin law, again examining culmination stars, cutting nearest distance—taking yimao year first month jisi conjunction Start of Spring as upper origin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Buwei adopted it as Qin law, re-examined culmination stars, and took the nearest fit—yimao year, first month jisi conjunction at Start of Spring—as upper origin.

sentences.zh: 洪範傳曰：「曆記始於顓頊上元太始閼蒙攝提格之歲，畢陬之月，朔日己巳立春，七曜俱在營室五度。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Commentary says: "Calendar records begin at Zhuanxu upper origin Taishi Yuemeng Shetige year, Biyou month, new moon day jisi Start of Spring—the seven luminaries all at Encampment five degrees."
translations.idiomatic: The Hongfan Commentary says: "Calendars begin at Zhuanxu's upper origin, the year Taishi Yuemeng Shetige, month Biyou, new moon on jisi at Start of Spring—all seven luminaries at five degrees of Encampment."

sentences.zh: 」是也。

translations.literal: It is so.
translations.idiomatic: So it records.

sentences.zh: 秦顓頊曆元起乙卯，漢太初曆元起丁丑，推而上之，皆不值甲寅，猶以日月五緯復得上元本星度，故命曰閼蒙攝提格之歲，而實非甲寅。

translations.literal: Qin Zhuanxu calendar origin starts yimao, Han Taichu calendar origin starts dingchou—extrapolating upward, neither hits jiayin, yet still by sun, moon, and five planets recovering upper origin original star degrees—therefore named Yuemeng Shetige year, yet in fact not jiayin.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin Zhuanxu origin begins at yimao and the Han Taichu at dingchou; extrapolating backward neither lands on jiayin, yet by sun, moon, and five planets they still recover the upper origin's star positions—so the year is called Yuemeng Shetige though it is not truly jiayin.

sentences.zh: 夏曆章蔀紀首，皆在立春，故其課中星，揆斗建與閏餘之所盈縮，皆以十有二節為損益之中。

translations.literal: Xia calendar's rule, obscuration, and era heads all at Start of Spring—therefore its examining culmination stars, measuring Dipper Establishment and intercalary remainder's surplus and deficit, all use the twelve minor nodes as increase-decrease center.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia calendar's rules, obscurations, and era heads all begin at Start of Spring, so its culmination checks and Dipper Establishment and intercalary adjustments all use the twelve minor nodes as their pivot.

sentences.zh: 而殷、周、漢曆，章蔀紀首皆直冬至，故其名察發斂，亦以中氣為主。

translations.literal: Yet Yin, Zhou, and Han calendars' rule, obscuration, and era heads all directly at winter solstice—therefore their name "examining emission and gathering" also takes mid-qi as main.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin, Zhou, and Han calendars instead anchor rules, obscurations, and era heads at winter solstice, so their "examining emission and gathering" also centers on mid-qi.

sentences.zh: 此其異也。

translations.literal: This is their difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is the difference between them.

sentences.zh: 夏小正雖頗疎簡失傳，乃羲、和遺迹。

translations.literal: Xia Small Calendar though somewhat coarse and simple in lost transmission—is Xi and He's surviving trace.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia Small Calendar, though coarse and imperfectly transmitted, preserves Xi and He's legacy.

sentences.zh: 何承天循大戴之說，復用夏時，更以正月甲子夜半合朔雨水為上元，進乖夏曆，退非周正，故近代推月令、小正者，皆不與古合。

translations.literal: He Chengtian following the Dadai's theory, again using Xia times, further taking first month jiazi midnight conjunction Rain Water as upper origin—advancing contrary to Xia calendar, retreating not Zhou's correct month—therefore recent extrapolations of Monthly Ordinances and Small Calendar all do not match antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian, following the Dadai Liji, revived Xia reckoning with first month jiazi midnight conjunction at Rain Water as upper origin—ahead of the Xia calendar yet not Zhou's proper first month—so recent reconstructions of the Monthly Ordinances and Small Calendar all fail to match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 開元曆推夏時立春，日在營室之末，昏東井二度中。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan calendar extrapolates Xia times Start of Spring, sun at Encampment's end, dusk Dongjing two degrees culminates.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar extrapolates Xia Start of Spring with the sun at the end of Encampment and Dongjing at two degrees culminating at dusk.

sentences.zh: 古曆以參右肩為距，方當南正。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar takes Shen's right shoulder as distance—just at southern cardinal.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar takes Shen's right shoulder as the reference point, right at the southern cardinal.

sentences.zh: 故小正曰：「正月初昏，斗杓懸在下。

translations.literal: Therefore the Small Calendar says: "First month initial dusk, Dipper ladle hangs below."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Small Calendar says: "At first dusk of the first month, the Dipper's handle hangs low."

sentences.zh: 」魁枕參首，所以著參中也。

translations.literal: The ladle's head rests on Shen's head—thereby showing Shen at culmination.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper's head rests on Shen's head, marking Shen at culmination.

sentences.zh: 季春，在昴十一度半，去參距星十八度，故曰：「三月，參則伏。

translations.literal: Late spring, at Mao eleven and a half degrees, eighteen degrees from Shen's distance star—therefore it says: "Third month, Shen then hides."
translations.idiomatic: In late spring the sun stands at eleven and a half degrees of Mao, eighteen degrees from Shen's reference star—hence: "In the third month Shen sets."

sentences.zh: 」立夏，日在井四度，昏角中。

translations.literal: Start of Summer, sun at Jing four degrees, dusk Horn culminates.
translations.idiomatic: At Start of Summer the sun is at four degrees of Jing and Horn culminates at dusk.

sentences.zh: 南門右星入角距西五度，其左星入角距東六度，故曰：「四月初昏，南門正。

translations.literal: Southern Gate's right star enters Horn five degrees west of distance, its left star six degrees east of distance—therefore it says: "Fourth month initial dusk, Southern Gate centered."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Gate's right star lies five degrees west of Horn's reference point and its left six degrees east—hence: "At first dusk of the fourth month the Southern Gate is centered."

sentences.zh: 昴則見。

translations.literal: Mao then appears.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mao appears.

sentences.zh: 」五月節，日在輿鬼一度半。

translations.literal: Fifth month node, sun at Yugu one and a half degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth-month node the sun stands at one and a half degrees of Yugu.

sentences.zh: 參去日道最遠，以渾儀度之，參體始見，其肩股猶在濁中。

translations.literal: Shen farthest from the sun's path—measuring with the armillary, Shen's body first appears, its shoulder and thigh still in turbidity.
translations.idiomatic: Shen is farthest from the sun's path; on the armillary Shen's body first appears while its shoulder and thigh remain below the horizon.

sentences.zh: 房星正中。

translations.literal: Fang star centered.
translations.idiomatic: Fang is at culmination.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「五月，參則見。

translations.literal: Therefore it says: "Fifth month, Shen then appears.
translations.idiomatic: Hence: "In the fifth month Shen appears.

sentences.zh: 初昏，大火中。

translations.literal: Initial dusk, Great Fire centered."
translations.idiomatic: At first dusk Great Fire is centered."

sentences.zh: 」「八月，參中則曙」，失傳也。

translations.literal: "Eighth month, Shen centered then dawn"—lost in transmission.
translations.idiomatic: "In the eighth month Shen culminates at dawn"—a corrupted transmission.

sentences.zh: 辰伏則參見，非中也。

translations.literal: When chen hides then Shen appears—not centered.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun enters chen, Shen appears—it is not at culmination.

sentences.zh: 「十月初昏，南門見」，亦失傳也。

translations.literal: "Tenth month initial dusk, Southern Gate appears"—also lost in transmission.
translations.idiomatic: "At first dusk of the tenth month the Southern Gate appears"—also corrupted.

sentences.zh: 定星方中，則南門伏，非昏見也。

translations.literal: When fixed stars are centered, Southern Gate hides—not dusk appearance.
translations.idiomatic: When the fixed stars are centered the Southern Gate sets—it is not a dusk sighting.

sentences.zh: 商六百二十八年，日却差八度。

translations.literal: Shang six hundred twenty-eight years, sun retreating differs eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Over the Shang dynasty's 628 years the sun's position retreated eight degrees.

sentences.zh: 太甲二年壬午歲冬至，應在女六度。

translations.literal: Taikang year 12 renwu year winter solstice should be at Nü six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice of Taikang year 12, a renwu year, should fall at six degrees of Nü.

sentences.zh: 國語曰：「武王伐商，歲在鶉火，月在天駟，日在析木之津，辰在斗柄，星在天黿。

translations.literal: The Discourses say: "King Wu attacked Shang—year in Quail Fire, moon at Heavenly Si, sun at Ximu's ford, chen at the Dipper's handle, star at Heavenly Turtle."
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses record: "When King Wu attacked Shang, Jupiter was in Quail Fire, the moon at Heavenly Si, the sun at Ximu's ford, chen at the Dipper's handle, and the star at Heavenly Turtle."

sentences.zh: 」舊說歲在己卯，推其朏魄，迺文王崩，武王成君之歲也。

translations.literal: Old theory year at jimao—extrapolating its crescent and full moon, then King Wen died and Wu became lord that year.
translations.idiomatic: Older accounts place the year at jimao; extrapolating its lunar phases, that was the year King Wen died and Wu became ruler.

sentences.zh: 其明年，武王即位，新曆孟春定朔丙辰，於商為二月，故周書曰：「維王元祀二月丙辰朔，武王訪于周公。

translations.literal: The next year Wu took the throne; new calendar first month fixed new moon bingchen—in Shang reckoning the second month—therefore the Book of Zhou says: "In the king's first year, second month bingchen new moon, King Wu consulted Duke of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu took the throne. The new calendar gives first-month fixed new moon on bingchen—in Shang terms the second month—hence the Book of Zhou: "In the king's first year, second month bingchen new moon, King Wu consulted the Duke of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」竹書「十一年庚寅，周始伐商」。

translations.literal: Bamboo Annals "year 11 gengyin, Zhou first attacked Shang."
translations.idiomatic: The Bamboo Annals record: "Year 11 gengyin, Zhou first attacked Shang."

sentences.zh: 而管子及家語以為十二年，蓋通成君之歲也。

translations.literal: Yet Guanzi and Family Discourses say year 12—likely counting through the lordship year.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzi and the Family Discourses say year 12—probably counting through the year Wu became lord.

sentences.zh: 先儒以文王受命九年而崩；

translations.literal: Earlier scholars held King Wen received the mandate nine years then died;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that King Wen received the mandate and died in nine years;

sentences.zh: 至十年，武王觀兵盟津；

translations.literal: Reaching year 10, King Wu reviewed troops at Mengjin;
translations.idiomatic: in year 10 King Wu reviewed troops at Mengjin;

sentences.zh: 十三年，復伐商。

translations.literal: Year 13, again attacked Shang.
translations.idiomatic: and in year 13 attacked Shang again.

sentences.zh: 推元祀二月丙辰朔，距伐商日月，不為相距四年。

translations.literal: Extrapolating first year second month bingchen new moon, distance to attack-Shang day-moon—not four years apart.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from first-year second-month bingchen new moon to the attack on Shang, the interval is not four years.

sentences.zh: 所說非是。

translations.literal: Their account is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That chronology is wrong.

sentences.zh: 武王十年，夏正十月戊子，周師始起。

translations.literal: King Wu year 10, Xia first month tenth month wuzi, Zhou army first raised.
translations.idiomatic: In King Wu's tenth year, Xia tenth month wuzi, the Zhou army first mobilized.

sentences.zh: 於歲差日在箕十度，則析木津也。

translations.literal: By precession sun at Ji ten degrees—then Ximu's ford.
translations.idiomatic: By precession the sun stood at ten degrees of Ji—at Ximu's ford.

sentences.zh: 晨初，月在房四度。

translations.literal: Dawn initial, moon at Fang four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the moon stood at four degrees of Fang.

sentences.zh: 於易，雷乘乾曰大壯，房、心象焉。

translations.literal: In the Changes, thunder riding qian is Da Zhuang—Fang and Xin image it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yijing, thunder over qian is Da Zhuang—Fang and Xin embody it.

sentences.zh: 心為乾精，而房，升陽之駟也。

translations.literal: Xin is qian's essence, while Fang is ascending yang's si.
translations.idiomatic: Xin is qian's essence; Fang is the si of rising yang.

sentences.zh: 房與歲星實相經緯，以屬靈威仰之神，后稷感之以生。

translations.literal: Fang and Jupiter truly cross in longitude, belonging to the spirit Lingweiyang—Hou Ji was moved thereby to be born.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Jupiter truly cross in longitude, belonging to the spirit Lingweiyang; Hou Ji was moved by this to be born.

sentences.zh: 故國語曰：「月之所在，辰馬農祥，我祖后稷之所經緯也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Discourses say: "Where the moon stands, chen-horse and agricultural auspice—our ancestor Hou Ji's longitude."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Discourses: "Where the moon stands—chen-horse, agricultural auspice—the longitude of our ancestor Hou Ji."

sentences.zh: 」又三日得周正月庚寅朔，日月會南斗一度。

translations.literal: Again three days later obtaining Zhou first month gengyin new moon, sun and moon meeting Southern Dipper one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later came Zhou first month gengyin new moon, sun and moon conjoining at one degree of Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 故曰「辰在斗柄」。

translations.literal: Therefore "chen at the Dipper's handle."
translations.idiomatic: Hence "chen at the Dipper's handle."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，辰星夕見，在南斗二十度。

translations.literal: Renchen, Mercury visible at dusk at Southern Dipper twenty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Mercury appeared at dusk at twenty degrees of Southern Dippler.

sentences.zh: 其明日，武王自宗周次于師所。

translations.literal: The next day King Wu from Zongzhou halted at the army's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The next day King Wu left Zongzhou and halted at the army camp.

sentences.zh: 凡月朔而未見曰「死魄」，夕而成光則謂之「朏」。

translations.literal: Generally new moon not yet seen is called "dead soul"; dusk forming light is called "crescent."
translations.idiomatic: When the new moon is not yet visible it is called "dead soul"; when light forms at dusk it is called "crescent."

sentences.zh: 朏或以二日，或以三日，故武成曰：「維一月壬辰，旁死魄。

translations.literal: Crescent may be second day or third day—therefore Completion of War says: "First month renchen, beside dead soul."
translations.idiomatic: The crescent may fall on the second or third day—hence Completion of War: "First month renchen, beside dead soul."

sentences.zh: 翌日癸巳，王朝步自周，于征伐商。

translations.literal: Next day guisi, king at dawn stepped from Zhou, on expedition attacking Shang."
translations.idiomatic: "Next day guisi, the king at dawn marched from Zhou to attack Shang."

sentences.zh: 」是時辰星與周師俱進，由建星之末，歷牽牛、須女，涉顓頊之虛。

translations.literal: Then Mercury with Zhou army jointly advanced, from Jianxing's end, passing Ox, Maiden, through Zhuanxu's void.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury then advanced with the Zhou army from Jianxing's end through Ox, Maiden, and Zhuanxu's void.

sentences.zh: 戊午，師度盟津，而辰星伏于天黿。

translations.literal: Wuwu, army crossed Mengjin ford, Mercury hidden at Heavenly Turtle.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the army crossed Mengjin ford and Mercury set at Heavenly Turtle.

sentences.zh: 辰星，汁光紀之精，所以告顓頊而終水行之運，且木帝之所繇生也。

translations.literal: Mercury, Zhiguangji's essence—thereby announcing Zhuanxu and ending water's course, and where the Wood Emperor is born.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury is Zhiguangji's essence, announcing Zhuanxu and ending water's reign—the birthplace of the Wood Emperor.

sentences.zh: 故國語曰：「星與日辰之位皆在北維，顓頊之所建也，帝嚳受之。

translations.literal: Therefore the Discourses say: "Star and sun-chen positions all at north wei—what Zhuanxu established, Di Ku received.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Discourses: "Star and sun-chen positions all lie at north wei—what Zhuanxu established and Di Ku received.

sentences.zh: 我周氏出自天黿；

translations.literal: Our Zhou clan comes from Heavenly Turtle;
translations.idiomatic: "Our Zhou clan descends from Heavenly Turtle;

sentences.zh: 及析木，有建星、牽牛焉，則我皇妣太姜之姪、伯陵之後逢公之所憑神也。

translations.literal: Reaching Ximu, there are Jianxing and Ox—then our royal mother's niece, Earl Ling's descendant Lord Feng's relying spirit."
translations.idiomatic: reaching Ximu with Jianxing and Ox—the spirit on whom our royal mother's niece, Lord Feng of Earl Ling's line, relies."

sentences.zh: 」是歲，歲星始及鶉火。

translations.literal: That year Jupiter first reached Quail Fire.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jupiter first reached Quail Fire.

sentences.zh: 其明年，周始革命。

translations.literal: The next year Zhou first revolutionized.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhou completed the revolution.

sentences.zh: 歲又退行，旅於鶉首，而後進及鳥帑，所以返復其道，經綸周室。

translations.literal: Jupiter again retreated, lodging at Quail Head, then advancing to Bird Tail—thereby reversing its path, weaving Zhou's house.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter retreated again to Quail Head, then advanced to Bird Tail—reversing course to weave Zhou's destiny.

sentences.zh: 鶉火直軒轅之虛，以爰稼穡，稷星繫焉，而成周之大萃也。

translations.literal: Quail Fire directly at Xuanyuan's void, thereby cherishing grain—Ji's star attached, forming Zhou's great gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Quail Fire lies at Xuanyuan's void where grain is cherished; Ji's star is attached, forming Zhou's great gathering.

sentences.zh: 鶉首當山河之右，太王以興，后稷封焉，而宗周之所宅也。

translations.literal: Quail Head at the Yellow River's right—Great Ancestor rose there, Hou Ji enfeoffed, and Zongzhou's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Quail Head lies west of the Yellow River where the Great Ancestor rose, Hou Ji was enfeoffed, and Zongzhou was settled.

sentences.zh: 歲星與房實相經緯，而相距七舍；

translations.literal: Jupiter and Fang truly cross in longitude, seven lodges apart;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter and Fang truly cross in longitude, seven lodges apart;

sentences.zh: 木與水代終，而相及七月。

translations.literal: Wood and water end in succession, meeting across seven months.
translations.idiomatic: wood and water succeed each other across seven months.

sentences.zh: 故國語曰：「歲之所在，則我有周之分也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Discourses say: "Where Jupiter stands, there is our Zhou's allotment."
translations.idiomatic: Hence: "Where Jupiter stands is Zhou's allotted domain."

sentences.zh: 自鶉及駟七列，南北之揆七月。

translations.literal: From Quail to Si seven columns, south-north measure seven months."
translations.idiomatic: "From Quail to Si, seven columns; south to north, seven months."

sentences.zh: 」其二月戊子朔，哉生明，王自克商還，至于酆，於周為四月。

translations.literal: Its second month wuzi new moon, crescent bright, king from conquering Shang returned, reaching Feng—in Zhou the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: On second-month wuzi new moon at crescent brightness the king returned from conquering Shang to Feng—in Zhou reckoning the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 新曆推定望甲辰，而乙巳旁之。

translations.literal: New calendar extrapolates fixed full moon jiachen, with yisi beside it.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar places fixed full moon on jiachen with yisi adjacent.

sentences.zh: 故武成曰：「維四月，既旁生魄，粵六日庚戌，武王燎于周廟。

translations.literal: Therefore Completion of War says: "Fourth month, beside full soul, sixth day gengxu, King Wu burned at Zhou temple."
translations.idiomatic: Hence Completion of War: "Fourth month, beside full soul, sixth day gengxu, King Wu burned offerings at the Zhou temple."

sentences.zh: 」麟德曆，周師始起，歲在降婁，月宿天根，日躔心而合辰在尾，水星伏於星紀，不及天黿。

translations.literal: Lindé calendar Zhou army first raised, year at Jianglou, moon lodging Sky Root, sun progression at Xin conjoining chen at Tail, Mercury hidden at Star Record, not reaching Heavenly Turtle.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar has the Zhou army mobilize with Jupiter at Jianglou, the moon at Sky Root, the sun at Xin with chen at Tail, Mercury hidden at Star Record—not reaching Heavenly Turtle.

sentences.zh: 又周書，革命六年而武王崩。

translations.literal: Also Book of Zhou, six years after revolution King Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Zhou also says King Wu died six years after the revolution.

sentences.zh: 管子、家語以為七年，蓋通克商之歲也。

translations.literal: Guanzi and Family Discourses say seven years—likely counting through the conquest year.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzi and Family Discourses say seven years—probably counting through the conquest year.

sentences.zh: 周公攝政七年二月甲戌朔，己丑望，後六日乙未。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhou regent seven years second month jiaxu new moon, jichou full moon, six days later yimwei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duke of Zhou's regency, seventh year second month jiaxu new moon, jichou full moon, six days later yimwei.

sentences.zh: 三月定朔甲辰，三日丙午。

translations.literal: Third month fixed new moon jiachen, third day bingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Third month fixed new moon jiachen, third day bingwu.

sentences.zh: 故召誥曰：「惟二月既望，越六日乙未，王朝步自周，至于酆」，「三月，惟丙午朏，越三日戊申，太保朝至于洛。

translations.literal: Therefore Announcement says: "Second month full moon passed, six days yimwei, king at dawn stepped from Zhou reaching Feng," "Third month, only bingwu crescent, three days wushen, Grand Guardian at dawn reached Luo."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Announcement: "Second month after full moon, six days yimwei, the king at dawn marched from Zhou to Feng," and "Third month, bingwu crescent, three days wushen, the Grand Guardian at dawn reached Luo."

sentences.zh: 」其明年，成王正位。

translations.literal: The next year King Cheng took correct position.
translations.idiomatic: The next year King Cheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 三十年四月己酉朔甲子，哉生魄。

translations.literal: Thirty years fourth month jiyou new moon jiazi, crescent bright.
translations.idiomatic: Year 30, fourth month jiyou new moon jiazi, crescent brightness.

sentences.zh: 故書曰：「惟四月，才生魄。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents say: "Only fourth month, just crescent bright."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents: "In the fourth month, at first crescent."

sentences.zh: 」甲子，作顧命。

translations.literal: Jiazi, composed Testamentary Charge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he composed the Testamentary Charge.

sentences.zh: 康王十二年，歲在乙酉，六月戊辰朔，三日庚午。

translations.literal: King Kang year 12, year at yiyou, sixth month wuchen new moon, third day gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: King Kang's year 12, a yiyou year, sixth month wuchen new moon, third day gengwu.

sentences.zh: 故畢命曰：「惟十有二年，六月庚午朏。

translations.literal: Therefore Charge to Bi says: "Only twelve years, sixth month gengwu crescent."
translations.idiomatic: Hence Charge to Bi: "In the twelfth year, sixth month gengwu crescent."

sentences.zh: 越三日壬申，王以成周之眾命畢公。

translations.literal: Three days later renshen, king with Chengzou's masses commanded Duke of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: "Three days later on renshen the king commanded Duke of Bi with Chengzou's forces."

sentences.zh: 」自伐紂及此，五十六年，朏魄日名，上下無不合。

translations.literal: From attacking Zhou to this, fifty-six years—crescent and soul day-names all match without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: From the attack on Zhou to this point, fifty-six years—crescent and full-moon day-names all agree.

sentences.zh: 而三統曆以己卯為克商之歲，非也。

translations.literal: Yet Three Systems calendar takes jimao as conquest-Shang year—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Three Systems calendar takes jimao as the conquest year—which is wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫有効於古者，宜合於今。

translations.literal: What is effective toward antiquity should match the present.
translations.idiomatic: What works for antiquity should match the present.

sentences.zh: 三統曆自太初至開元，朔後天三日。

translations.literal: Three Systems calendar from Taichu to Kaiyuan, new moon lags heaven three days.
translations.idiomatic: From Taichu to Kaiyuan the Three Systems calendar's new moons lag heaven by three days.

sentences.zh: 推而上之，以至周初，先天，失之蓋益甚焉。

translations.literal: Extrapolating upward to Zhou's beginning, preceding heaven—the error grows worse.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating back to early Zhou they run ahead of heaven—the error grows worse.

sentences.zh: 是以知合於歆者，必非克商之歲。

translations.literal: Thus knowing what matches Xin must not be the conquest-Shang year.
translations.idiomatic: Thus what agrees with Liu Xin cannot be the conquest year.

sentences.zh: 自宗周訖春秋之季，日却差八度。

translations.literal: From Zongzhou to Spring and Autumn's end, sun retreating differs eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: From Zongzhou to the Spring and Autumn's end the sun retreated eight degrees.

sentences.zh: 康王十一年甲申歲冬至，應在牽牛六度。

translations.literal: King Kang year 11 jiashen year winter solstice should be at Ox six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice of King Kang year 11, a jiashen year, should fall at six degrees of Ox.

sentences.zh: 周曆十二次，星紀初，南斗十四度，於太初星距斗十七度少也。

translations.literal: Zhou calendar twelve stations, Star Record beginning Southern Dipper fourteen degrees—from Taichu stars distance from Dipper seventeen degrees small.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou calendar's twelve stations begin at fourteen degrees of Southern Dipper—seventeen degrees small from Taichu star-distance at Dipper.

sentences.zh: 古曆分率簡易，歲久輒差。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar fractional rates simple—long years then differ.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient fractional rates were simple; over long periods they drifted.

sentences.zh: 達曆數者隨時遷革，以合其變。

translations.literal: Those versed in calendar numbers revise with the times to match change.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled calendrists revise with the times to match celestial change.

sentences.zh: 故三代之興，皆揆測天行，考正星次，為一代之制。

translations.literal: Therefore the Three Dynasties' rise all measured heaven's motion, verified star stations, making one era's system.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the Three Dynasties measured heaven's motion and verified star stations to establish its calendar.

sentences.zh: 正朔既革，而服色從之。

translations.literal: Correct first month changed—then dress and color followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the calendar's first month changed, dress and color followed.

sentences.zh: 及繼體守文，疇人代嗣，則謹循先王舊制焉。

translations.literal: Reaching succession and preserving culture, calendar officers succeeded in generations—then carefully following former kings' old system.
translations.idiomatic: Under succession they preserved former kings' systems through generations of calendar officers.

sentences.zh: 國語曰：「農祥晨正，日月厎于天廟，土乃脈發。

translations.literal: Discourses say: "Agricultural auspice dawn correct, sun and moon reach heaven's temple, earth then pulse sends forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses say: "When agricultural auspice is correct at dawn and sun and moon reach heaven's temple, the earth's pulse stirs.

sentences.zh: 先時九日，太史告稷曰，自今至于初吉，陽氣俱蒸，土膏其動。

translations.literal: Nine days before, Grand Astrologer told Hou Ji: from now to first auspicious day, yang qi all steams, earth ointment moves.
translations.idiomatic: Nine days earlier the Grand Astrologer told Hou Ji: from now until the first auspicious day yang qi will steam and the earth's ointment stir.

sentences.zh: 弗震不渝，脈其滿眚，穀乃不殖。

translations.literal: Not shaken unchanged, pulse its full calamity—grain then not planted."
translations.idiomatic: "If it does not shake and shift, the pulse fills with calamity and grain will not sprout."

sentences.zh: 」周初，先立春九日，日至營室。

translations.literal: Zhou beginning, nine days before Start of Spring, sun arrives Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhou's beginning, nine days before Start of Spring the sun reached Encampment.

sentences.zh: 古曆距中九十一度，是日晨初，大火正中，故曰「農祥晨正，日月厎于天廟」也。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar distance from center ninety-one degrees—that day dawn initial, Great Fire centered—therefore "agricultural auspice dawn correct, sun and moon reach heaven's temple."
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar placed culmination ninety-one degrees from the sun; that day at dawn Great Fire was centered—hence "agricultural auspice correct at dawn, sun and moon at heaven's temple."

sentences.zh: 於易象，升氣究而臨受之，自冬至後七日，乾精始復。

translations.literal: In Changes imagery, ascending qi exhausted then Lin receives— from seven days after winter solstice qian essence first returns.
translations.idiomatic: In Yijing imagery, ascending qi completes and Lin receives it—from seven days after winter solstice qian essence first returns.

sentences.zh: 及大寒，地統之中，陽洽於萬物根柢，而與萌芽俱升，木在地中之象，升氣已達，則當推而大之，故受之以臨。

translations.literal: Reaching Greater Cold, earth system's center, yang harmonizes with myriad things' roots, with sprouts jointly ascending—wood in earth's image; ascending qi reached, then ought to expand greatly—therefore receives Lin.
translations.idiomatic: By Greater Cold, earth's midpoint, yang harmonizes with roots and sprouts rising together—wood underground; when ascending qi has risen it expands—hence Lin follows.

sentences.zh: 於消息，龍德在田，得地道之和澤，而動於地中，升陽憤盈，土氣震發，故曰：「自今至於初吉，陽氣俱蒸，土膏其動。

translations.literal: In message, dragon virtue in field, obtaining earth's way and marsh, moving in earth's center, ascending yang surges full, earth qi shakes forth—therefore: "From now to first auspicious day, yang qi all steams, earth ointment moves."
translations.idiomatic: In the wax-wane cycle, dragon virtue is in the field; earth's harmony stirs underground, yang surges, earth qi shakes—hence: "From now to the first auspicious day yang steams and earth stirs."

sentences.zh: 」又先立春三日，而小過用事，陽好節止於內，動作于外，矯而過正，然後返求中焉。

translations.literal: Also three days before Start of Spring, Xiao Guo governs—yang loves restraining within, acting without, correcting past excess then seeking center.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before Start of Spring Xiao Guo governs—yang restrains within while acting without, correcting excess to find the mean.

sentences.zh: 是以及于艮維，則山澤通氣，陽精闢戶，甲坼之萌見，而莩穀之際離，故曰：「不震不渝，脈其滿眚，穀乃不殖。

translations.literal: Thus reaching gen-wei, then mountain and marsh connect qi, yang essence opens doors, sprout-shell's bud appears, and husk-grain's interval departs—therefore: "Not shaken unchanged, pulse its full calamity, grain then not planted."
translations.idiomatic: Reaching gen-wei, mountain and marsh connect, yang opens the gate, buds appear and grain husks part—hence: "Without shaking, the pulse fills with calamity and grain fails."

sentences.zh: 」君子之道，必擬之而後言，豈億度而已哉！

translations.literal: The noble person's way must compare before speaking—how merely estimate degrees!
translations.idiomatic: The noble person compares before speaking—how could mere estimation of degrees suffice!

sentences.zh: 韋昭以為日及天廟，在立春之初，非也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao held sun reaching heaven's temple at Start of Spring's beginning—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao placed sun-at-heaven's-temple at Start of Spring's opening—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 於麟德曆則又後立春十五日矣。

translations.literal: In Lindé calendar then again fifteen days after Start of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar places it fifteen days after Start of Spring.

sentences.zh: 春秋「桓公五年，秋，大雩」。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn "Duke Huan year 5, autumn, great rain prayer."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records: "Duke Huan's year 5, autumn, great rain-prayer."

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「書不時也。

translations.literal: Commentary says: "Recorded not at proper season."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "Recorded because the season was wrong."

sentences.zh: 凡祀，啟蟄而郊，龍見而雩。

translations.literal: Generally sacrifice—Awakening of Insects then suburban rite, dragon appears then rain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: "Sacrifices generally: suburban rite at Awakening of Insects, rain-prayer when the dragon appears."

sentences.zh: 」周曆立夏日在觜觽二度。

translations.literal: Zhou calendar Start of Summer sun at Zizi two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou calendar places Start of Summer with the sun at two degrees of Zizi.

sentences.zh: 於軌漏，昏角一度中，蒼龍畢見。

translations.literal: On clepsydra track, dusk Horn one degree centered, azure dragon fully visible.
translations.idiomatic: On the clepsydra track Horn culminates at one degree at dusk and the azure dragon is fully visible.

sentences.zh: 然則當在建巳之初，周禮也。

translations.literal: Then ought to be at jian-si's beginning—Zhou rites.
translations.idiomatic: That falls at the start of jian-si—per Zhou ritual.

sentences.zh: 至春秋時，日已潛退五度，節前月却，猶在建辰。

translations.literal: Reaching Spring and Autumn times, sun already secretly retreated five degrees, node before month retreating, still at jian-chen.
translations.idiomatic: By Spring and Autumn the sun had retreated five degrees; the month lagged before the node and still fell in jian-chen.

sentences.zh: 月令以為五月者，呂氏以顓頊曆芒種亢中，則龍以立夏昏見，不知有歲差，故雩祭失時。

translations.literal: Monthly Ordinances take as fifth month—Lü's Zhuanxu calendar Grain in Ear Kang centered, then dragon visible at Start of Summer dusk, not knowing precession—therefore rain prayer lost season.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances place it in the fifth month—Lü's Zhuanxu calendar has Grain in Ear with Kang centered, making the dragon appear at Start of Summer dusk without accounting for precession, so the rain-prayer season was wrong.

sentences.zh: 然則唐禮當以建巳之初，農祥始見而雩。

translations.literal: Then Tang rites ought to take jian-si's beginning, agricultural auspice first appearing then rain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ritual should therefore rain-pray at jian-si's start when agricultural auspice first appears.

sentences.zh: 若據麟德曆，以小滿後十三日，則龍角過中，為不時矣。

translations.literal: If according to Lindé calendar, thirteen days after Lesser Fullness, then Horn past center—not at proper season.
translations.idiomatic: By the Lindé calendar, thirteen days after Lesser Fullness puts Horn past culmination—out of season.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「凡土功，龍見而畢務，戒事。

translations.literal: Commentary says: "Generally earthworks—dragon appears then finish affairs, warn of tasks.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "For earthworks generally: when the dragon appears finish the work and warn of tasks.

sentences.zh: 火見而致用，水昏正而栽，日至而畢。

translations.literal: Fire appears then put to use, water dusk correct then plant, sun arrives then finish."
translations.idiomatic: When Fire appears put tools to use; when water is correct at dusk, plant; when the sun arrives, finish."

sentences.zh: 」十六年冬，城向。

translations.literal: Year 16 winter, walled Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 winter they walled Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，衞侯朔出奔齊。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Marquis Wei Shuo fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Marquis Wei Shuo fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 「冬，城向，書時也。

translations.literal: "Winter, walled Xiang—recorded at proper season."
translations.idiomatic: "Winter: walled Xiang—recorded as timely."

sentences.zh: 」以歲差推之，周初霜降，日在心五度，角、亢晨見。

translations.literal: By precession extrapolation, Zhou beginning Frost Descent sun at Xin five degrees, Horn and Kang visible at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: By precession, at early Zhou Frost Descent the sun stood at five degrees of Xin with Horn and Kang visible at dawn.

sentences.zh: 立冬，火見營室中。

translations.literal: Start of Winter, Fire visible Encampment centered.
translations.idiomatic: At Start of Winter Fire appeared with Encampment centered.

sentences.zh: 後七日，水星昏正，可以興板幹。

translations.literal: Seven days later, Mercury dusk correct—can raise beams and timbers.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later Mercury was correct at dusk—time to raise beams and timbers.

sentences.zh: 故祖沖之以為定之方中，直營室八度。

translations.literal: Therefore Zu Chongzhi held Ding's square centered, directly Encampment eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi therefore placed "Ding's square centered" at eight degrees of Encampment.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月六日霜降，二十一日立冬。

translations.literal: That year ninth month sixth day Frost Descent, twenty-first day Start of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: That year Frost Descent fell on the 6th of the ninth month and Start of Winter on the 21st.

sentences.zh: 十月之前，水星昏正，故傳以為得時。

translations.literal: Before tenth month, Mercury dusk correct—therefore commentary held it timely.
translations.idiomatic: Before the tenth month Mercury was correct at dusk—hence the commentary judged it timely.

sentences.zh: 杜氏據晉曆，小雪後定星乃中，季秋城向，似為大早。
