translations.literal: Du's according to Jin calendar, after Lesser Snow fixed stars then centered, late autumn walling Xiang, seems greatly early.
translations.idiomatic: Du, using the Jin calendar, has fixed stars centered only after Lesser Snow—walling Xiang in late autumn seems far too early.

sentences.zh: 因曰功役之事，皆總指天象，不與言曆數同。

translations.literal: Therefore says labor affairs all generally point to celestial signs, not same as speaking calendar numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He argues labor affairs point generally to celestial signs, not to calendar arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 引詩云「定之方中」，乃未正中之辭，非是。

translations.literal: Citing Odes "Ding's square centered"—not yet centered language—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the Odes' "Ding's square centered" as not-yet-centered language—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 麟德曆，立冬後二十五日火見，至大雪後營室乃中。

translations.literal: Lindé calendar twenty-five days after Start of Winter Fire appears, reaching Greater Snow后 Encampment then centered.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar has Fire appear twenty-five days after Start of Winter and Encampment centered only after Greater Snow.

sentences.zh: 而春秋九月書時，不已早乎。

translations.literal: Yet Spring and Autumn ninth month records timely—already not too early?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Spring and Autumn records ninth-month work as timely—is that not already too early?

sentences.zh: 大雪，周之孟春，陽氣靜復，以繕城隍，治宮室，是謂發天地之房，方於立春斷獄，所失多矣。

translations.literal: Greater Snow, Zhou's first month of spring, yang qi still recovering—to repair walls and cities, govern palaces, called opening heaven-earth's chamber—compared with Start of Spring cutting punishments, what is lost is much.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Snow is Zhou's first spring month when yang is still recovering—repairing walls and palaces opens heaven-earth's chamber; compared with Start of Spring for ending punishments, much is lost.

sentences.zh: 然則唐制宜以玄枵中天興土功。

translations.literal: Then Tang system ought to take Xuanxiao centered to start earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Tang practice should therefore start earthworks when Xuanxiao is centered.

sentences.zh: 僖公五年，晉侯伐虢。

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 5, Marquis of Jin attacked Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi's year 5: the Marquis of Jin attacked Guo.

sentences.zh: 卜偃曰：「克之。

translations.literal: Diviner Yan said: "Will conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Diviner Yan said: "Victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 童謠云：『丙之辰，龍尾伏辰，袀服振振，取虢之旂，鶉之賁賁，天策焞焞，火中成軍。

translations.literal: Children's song says: 'Bing's chen, Dragon Tail hidden chen, sacrificial robes fluttering, take Guo's banner, Quail's blazing, Heaven's tally blazing, Fire centered forming army.'"
translations.idiomatic: A children's song runs: 'On bing-chen, Dragon Tail hides chen, sacrificial robes flutter, seize Guo's banner, Quail blazes, Heaven's tally blazes, Fire centered forms the army.'"

sentences.zh: 』其九月十月之交乎！

translations.literal: Its ninth-tenth month crossing!
translations.idiomatic: "It falls at the ninth-tenth month crossing!"

sentences.zh: 丙子旦，日在尾，月在策，鶉火中，必是時。

translations.literal: Bingzi dawn, sun at Tail, moon at Ce, Quail Fire centered—must be that time.
translations.idiomatic: At bingzi dawn the sun is at Tail, the moon at Ce, Quail Fire centered—that must be the time.

sentences.zh: 」策，入尾十二度。

translations.literal: Ce, entering Tail twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Ce enters twelve degrees of Tail.

sentences.zh: 新曆是歲十月丙子定朔，日月合尾十四度於黃道。

translations.literal: New calendar that year tenth month bingzi fixed new moon, sun and moon conjoin Tail fourteen degrees on ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar gives that year's tenth month bingzi fixed new moon with sun and moon conjoined at fourteen degrees of Tail on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 古曆日在尾，而月在策，故曰「龍尾伏辰」，於古距張中而曙，直鶉火之末，始將西降，故曰「賁賁」。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar sun at Tail, moon at Ce—therefore "Dragon Tail hidden chen"—at ancient distance Zhang centered then dawn, directly Quail Fire's end, just about to descend west—therefore "blazing."
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar has the sun at Tail and moon at Ce—hence "Dragon Tail hidden chen"; at ancient distance Zhang culminates at dawn near Quail Fire's end, just descending west—hence "blazing."

sentences.zh: 昭公七年四月甲辰朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao year 7 fourth month jiachen new moon, solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao's year 7, fourth month jiachen new moon: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 士文伯曰：「去衞地，如魯地。

translations.literal: Shi Wenbo said: "Leaving Wei's territory, like Lu's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenbo said: "Leaving Wei's territory it is like Lu's.

sentences.zh: 於是有災，魯實受之。

translations.literal: At this there is disaster, Lu truly receives it."
translations.idiomatic: Disaster falls there, and Lu truly receives it."

sentences.zh: 」新曆是歲二月甲辰朔入常，雨水後七日，在奎十度。

translations.literal: New calendar that year second month jiachen new moon entering regular, seven days after Rain Water, at Kui ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar places that year's second month jiachen new moon in regular sequence, seven days after Rain Water, at ten degrees of Kui.

sentences.zh: 周度為降婁之始，則魯、衞之交也。

translations.literal: Zhou degree is Jianglou's beginning—then Lu and Wei's border.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou reckoning that is Jianglou's start—the border of Lu and Wei.

sentences.zh: 自周初至是已退七度，故入雨水。

translations.literal: From Zhou beginning to then already retreated seven degrees—therefore entering Rain Water.
translations.idiomatic: From early Zhou to then the sun had retreated seven degrees—hence it falls after Rain Water.

sentences.zh: 七日方及降婁，雖日度潛移，而周禮未改，其配神主祭之宿，宜書於建國之初。

translations.literal: Seven days then reaching Jianglou—though solar degree secretly shifts, Zhou rites unchanged, its paired spirit-host sacrifice lodge ought to be written at state-founding's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later it reaches Jianglou; though the sun's degree shifts, Zhou ritual is unchanged—the spirit-host lodge should be recorded at the state's founding.

sentences.zh: 淳風駁戊寅曆曰：「漢志降婁初在奎五度，今曆日蝕在降婁之中，依無歲差法，食於兩次之交。

translations.literal: Chunfeng refuted Wuyin calendar saying: "Han Treatise Jianglou beginning at Kui five degrees—now calendar eclipse in Jianglou's center, by no-precession method, eclipse at two stations' crossing."
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng refuted the Wuyin calendar: "The Han Treatise places Jianglou's start at five degrees of Kui—the current calendar's eclipse falls mid-Jianglou; by a no-precession method it is at a station crossing."

sentences.zh: 」是又不然。

translations.literal: This again is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That too is wrong.

sentences.zh: 議者曉十有二次之所由生，然後可以明其得失。

translations.literal: Discussants understanding twelve stations' origin—then can clarify their gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Only after understanding how the twelve stations arose can one judge their merits.

sentences.zh: 且劉歆等所定辰次，非能有以覩陰陽之賾，而得於鬼神，各據當時中節星度耳。

translations.literal: And Liu Xin and others' fixed chen stations—not able to see yin-yang's depths, obtaining from ghosts and spirits—each according to then mid-node star degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin and others fixed the chen stations not by penetrating yin-yang but from then-current mid-node star positions.

sentences.zh: 歆以太初曆冬至日在牽牛前五度，故降婁直東壁八度。

translations.literal: Xin by Taichu calendar winter solstice sun at Ox front five degrees—therefore Jianglou directly Dongbi eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, using the Taichu calendar's winter solstice at five degrees before Ox, placed Jianglou at eight degrees of Dongbi.

sentences.zh: 李業興正光曆，冬至在牽牛前十二度，故降婁退至東壁三度。

translations.literal: Li Yexing's Zhengguang calendar winter solstice at Ox front twelve degrees—therefore Jianglou retreated to Dongbi three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing's Zhengguang calendar puts winter solstice twelve degrees before Ox, retreating Jianglou to three degrees of Dongbi.

sentences.zh: 及祖沖之後，以為日度漸差，則當據列宿四正之中，以定辰次，不復係於中節。

translations.literal: After Zu Chongzhi, holding solar degree gradually differs—then ought to according to lodges four cardinals' centers fix chen stations, no longer tied to mid-nodes.
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Chongzhi, as solar degrees drift, chen stations should be fixed by the four cardinal lodges' centers, not mid-nodes.

sentences.zh: 淳風以冬至常在斗十三度，則當以東壁二度為降婁之初，安得守漢曆以駁仁均耶？

translations.literal: Chunfeng holding winter solstice always at Dipper thirteen degrees—then ought to take Dongbi two degrees as Jianglou's beginning—how keep Han calendar to refute Renjun?
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng fixed winter solstice at thirteen degrees of Dipper, making Dongbi two degrees Jianglou's start—how can he use the Han calendar to refute Renjun?

sentences.zh: 又三統曆昭公二十年，己丑，日南至，與麟德及開元曆同。

translations.literal: Also Three Systems calendar Duke Zhao year 20, jichou, sun south arrival—same as Lindé and Kaiyuan calendars.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Systems calendar also gives Duke Zhao year 20 jichou south arrival—matching Lindé and Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 然則入雨水後七日，亦入降婁七度，非魯、衞之交也。

translations.literal: Then entering Rain Water seven days later also entering Jianglou seven degrees—not Lu and Wei's border.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days after Rain Water also enters seven degrees of Jianglou—not the Lu-Wei border.

sentences.zh: 三十一年十二月辛亥朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: Year 31 twelfth month xinhai new moon, solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Year 31, twelfth month xinhai new moon: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 史墨曰：「日月在辰尾，庚午之日，日始有讁。

translations.literal: Shi Mo said: "Sun and moon at chen-tail, gengwu day, sun first has reproof."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mo said: "Sun and moon at chen-tail; on gengwu day the sun first showed reproof."

sentences.zh: 」開元曆是歲十月辛亥朔，入常立冬。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan calendar that year tenth month xinhai new moon, entering regular Start of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar gives that year's tenth month xinhai new moon, entering regular Start of Winter.

sentences.zh: 五日，日在尾十三度，於古距辰尾之初。

translations.literal: Five days, sun at Tail thirteen degrees—at ancient distance chen-tail's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the sun is at thirteen degrees of Tail—at ancient distance from chen-tail's start.

sentences.zh: 麟德曆日在心三度於黃道，退直于房矣。

translations.literal: Lindé calendar sun at Xin three degrees on ecliptic, retreated directly at Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar places the sun at three degrees of Xin on the ecliptic, retreated to Fang.

sentences.zh: 哀公十二年冬十有二月，螽。

translations.literal: Duke Ai year 12 winter twelfth month, locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai's year 12, winter twelfth month: locusts.

sentences.zh: 開元曆推置閏當在十一年春，至十二年冬，失閏已久。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan calendar extrapolates intercalation ought at year 11 spring—reaching year 12 winter, lost intercalation long.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar places intercalation in year 11 spring; by year 12 winter intercalation had been missing too long.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月己亥朔，先寒露三日，於定氣，日在亢五度，去心近一次。

translations.literal: That year ninth month jihai new moon, three days before Cold Dew—in fixed qi sun at Kang five degrees, near Xin by one station.
translations.idiomatic: That year ninth month jihai new moon, three days before Cold Dew: by fixed qi the sun stood at five degrees of Kang, one station from Xin.

sentences.zh: 火星明大，尚未當伏。

translations.literal: Mars bright great, not yet ought to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Mars was bright and large and had not yet should set.

sentences.zh: 至霜降五日，始潛日下。

translations.literal: Reaching five days after Frost Descent, first hidden below sun.
translations.idiomatic: Only five days after Frost Descent did it first set below the sun.

sentences.zh: 乃月令「蟄蟲咸俯」，則火辰未伏，當在霜降前。

translations.literal: Then Monthly Ordinances "hibernating insects all bow"—then Fire's station not yet hidden, ought before Frost Descent.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say "hibernating insects all bow"—but Mars had not yet set and should have been before Frost Descent.

sentences.zh: 雖節氣極晚，不得十月昏見。

translations.literal: Though seasonal nodes extremely late, cannot tenth month dusk visible.
translations.idiomatic: Even with very late nodes it could not appear at dusk in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼曰：「丘聞之，火伏而後蟄者畢。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: "I have heard, Fire hidden then hibernators finish.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius therefore said: "I have heard that after Fire hides the hibernators finish.

sentences.zh: 今火猶西流，司曆過也。

translations.literal: Now Fire still flows west, calendar officers excessive."
translations.idiomatic: Now Fire still moves west—the calendar officers erred."

sentences.zh: 」方夏后氏之初，八月辰伏，九月內火，及霜降之後，火已朝覿東方，距春秋之季千五百餘年，乃云「火伏而後蟄者畢」。

translations.literal: At early Xia beginning, eighth month chen hidden, ninth month within Fire—reaching after Frost Descent, Fire already dawn visible east, distance Spring and Autumn's end fifteen hundred-plus years—yet says "Fire hidden then hibernators finish."
translations.idiomatic: At early Xia, chen hid in the eighth month and Fire within in the ninth; by Frost Descent Fire was already visible at dawn in the east—1,500 years before Spring and Autumn—yet the text says "after Fire hides hibernators finish."

sentences.zh: 向使冬至常居其所，則仲尼不得以西流未伏，明是九月之初也。

translations.literal: If winter solstice always dwelled in its place, then Confucius could not by west-flowing not hidden clarify it is ninth month's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: If winter solstice never moved, Confucius could not use west-flowing Fire to show this was early ninth month.

sentences.zh: 自春秋至今又千五百歲，麟德曆以霜降後五日，日在氐八度，房、心初伏，定增二日，以月蝕衝校之，猶差三度。

translations.literal: From Spring and Autumn to now another fifteen hundred years, Lindé calendar five days after Frost Descent sun at Di eight degrees, Fang and Xin first hidden, adding fixed two days—by lunar eclipse opposition checking, still three degrees short.
translations.idiomatic: From Spring and Autumn to now another 1,500 years: the Lindé calendar has the sun at eight degrees of Di five days after Frost Descent with Fang and Xin first setting; adding two fixed days and checking by lunar eclipse opposition it still falls three degrees short.

sentences.zh: 閏餘稍多，則建亥之始，火猶見西方。

translations.literal: Intercalary remainder slightly more, then jian-hai's beginning Fire still visible west.
translations.idiomatic: With slightly too much intercalary remainder, at jian-hai's start Fire still appears in the west.

sentences.zh: 向使宿度不移，則仲尼不得以西流未伏，明非十月之候也。

translations.literal: If lodge degrees unmoved, then Confucius could not by west-flowing not hidden clarify not tenth month's sign.
translations.idiomatic: If lodge degrees never moved, Confucius could not use west-flowing Fire to show this was not a tenth-month marker.

sentences.zh: 自羲、和已來，火辰見伏，三覩厥變。

translations.literal: From Xi and He onward, Fire's station appear-hide, thrice witnessed its change.
translations.idiomatic: From Xi and He onward Fire's appearances and settings changed three times.

sentences.zh: 然則丘明之記，欲令後之作者參求微象，以探仲尼之旨。

translations.literal: Then Qiu Ming's record—wanting later makers to compare seeking subtle signs, to probe Confucius's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Ming's record invites later calendrists to compare subtle signs and grasp Confucius's intent.

sentences.zh: 是歲失閏寖久，季秋中氣後天三日，比及明年仲冬，又得一閏。

translations.literal: That year lost intercalation gradually long, mid-autumn mid-qi lagged heaven three days—reaching next year mid-winter, again obtaining one intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: That year intercalation had been missing too long; mid-autumn mid-qi lagged heaven three days—by the next mid-winter another intercalation was needed.

sentences.zh: 寤仲尼之言，補正時曆，而十二月猶可以螽。

translations.literal: Awakening to Confucius's words, correcting current calendar—yet twelfth month still can have locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding Confucius's words and correcting the calendar, locusts could still appear in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 至哀公十四年五月庚申朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: Reaching Duke Ai year 14 fifth month gengshen new moon, solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: By Duke Ai's year 14, fifth month gengshen new moon: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 以開元曆考之，則日蝕前又增一閏，魯曆正矣。

translations.literal: By Kaiyuan calendar checking, before eclipse again added one intercalation—Lu calendar correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar adds another intercalation before the eclipse—the Lu calendar is then correct.

sentences.zh: 長曆自哀公十年六月，迄十四年二月，纔置一閏，非是。

translations.literal: Long Calendar from Duke Ai year 10 sixth month to year 14 second month, only placed one intercalation—not so.
translations.idiomatic: The Long Calendar places only one intercalation from Duke Ai year 10 sixth month to year 14 second month—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 戰國及秦，日却退三度。

translations.literal: Warring States and Qin, sun retreating three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: From Warring States through Qin the sun retreated three degrees.

sentences.zh: 始皇十七年辛未歲冬至，應在斗二十二度。

translations.literal: First Emperor year 17 xinwei year winter solstice should be at Dipper twenty-two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice of the First Emperor's year 17, a xinwei year, should fall at twenty-two degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 秦曆上元正月己巳朔，晨初立春，日、月、五星俱起營室五度，蔀首日名皆直四孟。

translations.literal: Qin calendar upper origin first month jisi new moon, dawn initial Start of Spring, sun, moon, five planets all rise Encampment five degrees, obscuration head day-names all directly four meng.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin calendar's upper origin is first month jisi new moon at dawn initial Start of Spring with sun, moon, and five planets all at five degrees of Encampment; obscuration-head day-names all align with the four meng.

sentences.zh: 假朔退十五日，則閏在正月前。

translations.literal: Suppose new moon retreats fifteen days—then intercalation before first month.
translations.idiomatic: If new moon retreats fifteen days, intercalation falls before the first month.

sentences.zh: 朔進十五日，則閏在正月後。

translations.literal: New moon advances fifteen days—then intercalation after first month.
translations.idiomatic: If new moon advances fifteen days, intercalation falls after the first month.

sentences.zh: 是以十有二節，皆在盈縮之中，而晨昏宿度隨之。

translations.literal: Therefore twelve minor nodes all in expansion-contraction's center, and dawn-dusk lodge degrees follow.
translations.idiomatic: Thus all twelve minor nodes fall within expansion-contraction and dawn-dusk lodge degrees follow.

sentences.zh: 以顓頊曆依月令自十有二節推之，與不韋所記合。

translations.literal: By Zhuanxu calendar following Monthly Ordinances from twelve minor nodes extrapolating—matches Lü's record.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from twelve minor nodes per the Zhuanxu calendar matches Lü's record.

sentences.zh: 而潁子嚴之倫謂月令晨昏距宿，當在中氣，致雩祭太晚，自乖左氏之文，而杜預又據春秋以月令為否。

translations.literal: Yet Ying Ziyan and cohort held Monthly Ordinances dawn-dusk distance lodges ought at mid-qi—making rain prayer too late, self-contradicting Zuoshi's text, while Du Yu again according to Spring and Autumn holds Monthly Ordinances false.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ying Ziyan and others held Monthly Ordinances' dawn-dusk distances should fall at mid-qi—making rain-prayer too late, contradicting the Zuozhuan, while Du Yu rejected the Monthly Ordinances using the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 皆非是。

translations.literal: Both not so.
translations.idiomatic: Both are wrong.

sentences.zh: 梁大同曆夏后氏之初，冬至日在牽牛初，以為明堂、月令乃夏時之記，據中氣推之不合，更以中節之間為正，迺稍相符。

translations.literal: Liang Datong calendar early Xia beginning winter solstice sun at Ox beginning—held Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances are Xia-time records; according to mid-qi extrapolating not matching, changed to mid-node intervals as correct—then slightly matching.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Datong calendar placed early Xia winter solstice at Ox's start, treating Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances as Xia records; mid-qi extrapolation failed, so they used mid-node intervals instead and got rough agreement.

sentences.zh: 不知進在節初，自然契合。

translations.literal: Not knowing advance at node's beginning naturally matches.
translations.idiomatic: They did not see that advancing to the node's start naturally matches.

sentences.zh: 自秦初及今，又且千歲，節初之宿，皆當中氣。

translations.literal: From Qin beginning to now, again thousand years—node beginning's lodges all ought at mid-qi.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin to now, another thousand years: lodges at node beginnings should align with mid-qi.

sentences.zh: 淳風因為說曰：「今孟春中氣，日在營室，昏明中星，與月令不殊。

translations.literal: Chunfeng therefore says: "Now first spring mid-qi, sun at Encampment, dusk-dawn culmination stars, with Monthly Ordinances not different."
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng argued: "Now at first-spring mid-qi the sun is at Encampment and dusk-dawn stars match the Monthly Ordinances."

sentences.zh: 」按秦曆立春，日在營室五度。

translations.literal: Examining Qin calendar Start of Spring, sun at Encampment five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin calendar places Start of Spring with the sun at five degrees of Encampment.

sentences.zh: 麟德曆以啟蟄之日迺至營室，其昏明中宿十有二建，以為不差，妄矣。

translations.literal: Lindé calendar on Awakening of Insects day then reaches Encampment—its dusk-dawn centered stars twelve jian, holding not different—absurd.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar reaches Encampment only on Awakening of Insects and claims twelve jian dusk-dawn stars match—absurd.

sentences.zh: 古曆，冬至昏明中星去日九十二度，春分、秋分百度，夏至百一十八度，率一氣差三度，九日差一刻。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar winter solstice dusk-dawn centered stars distance sun ninety-two degrees, spring-autumn equinoxes one hundred degrees, summer solstice one hundred eighteen degrees—rate one qi differs three degrees, nine days differs one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar placed winter-solstice dusk-dawn stars ninety-two degrees from the sun, equinoxes at one hundred, summer solstice at one hundred eighteen—three degrees per qi, one quarter per nine days.

sentences.zh: 秦曆十二次，立春在營室五度，於太初星距危十六度少也。

translations.literal: Qin calendar twelve stations, Start of Spring at Encampment five degrees—from Taichu stars distance Wei sixteen degrees small.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin calendar's twelve stations place Start of Spring at five degrees of Encampment—sixteen degrees small from Taichu distance at Wei.

sentences.zh: 昏，畢八度中，月令參中，謂肩股也。

translations.literal: Dusk, Bi eight degrees centered—Monthly Ordinances Shen centered, meaning shoulder and thigh.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Bi at eight degrees is centered—the Monthly Ordinances' Shen centered means shoulder and thigh.

sentences.zh: 晨，心八度中，月令尾中，於太初星距尾也。

translations.literal: Dawn, Xin eight degrees centered—Monthly Ordinances Wei centered, from Taichu stars distance Tail.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xin at eight degrees is centered—the Monthly Ordinances' Wei centered uses Taichu distance at Tail.

sentences.zh: 仲春昏，東井十四度中，月令弧中，弧星入東井十八度。

translations.literal: Mid-spring dusk, Dongjing fourteen degrees centered—Monthly Ordinances Hu centered, Hu star enters Dongjing eighteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring dusk: Dongjing at fourteen degrees centered—the Monthly Ordinances' Hu centered has Hu entering eighteen degrees of Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 晨，南斗二度中，月令建星中，於太初星距西建也。

translations.literal: Dawn, Southern Dipper two degrees centered—Monthly Ordinances Jianxing centered, from Taichu stars distance West Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Southern Dipper at two degrees is centered—the Monthly Ordinances' Jianxing centered uses Taichu distance at West Jian.

sentences.zh: 甄耀度及魯曆，南方有狼、弧，無東井、鬼，北方有建星，無南斗，井、斗度長，弧、建度短，故以正昏明云。

translations.literal: Zhenyaodu and Lu calendar, south has Wolf and Hu, no Dongjing and Ghost; north has Jianxing, no Southern Dipper—Jing and Dipper degrees long, Hu and Jian degrees short—therefore by correct dusk-dawn speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyaodu and Lu calendars have Wolf and Hu in the south but not Dongjing and Ghost, Jianxing in the north but not Southern Dipper—Jing and Dipper degrees long, Hu and Jian short—hence correct dusk-dawn wording.

sentences.zh: 古曆星度及漢落下閎等所測，其星距遠近不同，然二十八之宿體不異。

translations.literal: Ancient star degrees and Han Luoxia Hong and others' measurements—their star distances near and far differ, yet twenty-eight lodges' bodies not different.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient star degrees and Han Luoxia Hong's measurements differ in reference distances, yet the twenty-eight lodges' bodies are the same.

sentences.zh: 古以牽牛上星為距，太初改用中星，入古曆牽牛太半度，於氣法當三十二分日之二十一。

translations.literal: Ancient taking Ox upper star as distance, Taichu changed to use center star, entering ancient calendar Ox great half degree—in qi method ought thirty-two parts day's twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Anciently Ox's upper star was the reference; Taichu switched to the center star, entering the ancient calendar at Ox by great half a degree—in qi reckoning that is twenty-one thirty-seconds of a day.

sentences.zh: 故洪範傳冬至日在牽牛一度，減太初星距二十一分，直南斗二十六度十九分也。

translations.literal: Therefore Hongfan Commentary winter solstice sun at Ox one degree, reducing Taichu star distance twenty-one parts, directly Southern Dipper twenty-six degrees nineteen parts.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongfan Commentary therefore places winter solstice at one degree of Ox; subtracting Taichu's star-distance of twenty-one parts yields twenty-six degrees nineteen parts of Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 顓頊曆立春起營室五度，冬至在牽牛一度少。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu calendar Start of Spring starts Encampment five degrees, winter solstice at Ox one degree small.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanxu calendar begins Start of Spring at five degrees of Encampment and winter solstice at one degree small of Ox.

sentences.zh: 洪範傳冬至所起無餘分，故立春在營室四度太。

translations.literal: Hongfan Commentary winter solstice starting no surplus fraction—therefore Start of Spring at Encampment four degrees great.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongfan Commentary's winter solstice start has no surplus fraction, so Start of Spring falls at four degrees great of Encampment.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之自營室五度，以太初星距命之，因云秦曆冬至，日在牽牛六度。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi from Encampment five degrees, by Taichu star distance naming—thereby saying Qin calendar winter solstice sun at Ox six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi, starting from five degrees of Encampment and using Taichu star-distance, concluded the Qin calendar's winter solstice stood at six degrees of Ox.

sentences.zh: 虞𠠎等襲沖之之誤，為之說云：「夏時冬至，日在斗末，以歲差考之，牽牛六度乃顓頊之代。

translations.literal: Yu Xi and others followed Chongzhi's error, making explanation: "Xia times winter solstice sun at Dipper's end—by precession checking, Ox six degrees is Zhuanxu's era.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi and others repeated Zu Chongzhi's error, arguing: "At Xia winter solstice the sun stood at Dipper's end; by precession that corresponds to six degrees of Ox in Zhuanxu's era.

sentences.zh: 漢時雖覺其差，頓移五度，故冬至還在牛初。

translations.literal: Han times though perceived the difference, suddenly moved five degrees—therefore winter solstice returned at Ox beginning."
translations.idiomatic: Han scholars noticed the drift and shifted five degrees, placing winter solstice back at Ox's beginning."

sentences.zh: 」按洪範古今星距，僅差四分之三，皆起牽牛一度。

translations.literal: Examining Hongfan ancient-modern star distances, only differ three-fourths—all starting Ox one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan's ancient and modern star distances differ by only three-fourths—all starting at one degree of Ox.

sentences.zh: 𠠎等所說，亦非是。

translations.literal: Xi and others' account—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi and colleagues are also wrong.

sentences.zh: 魯宣公十五年，丁卯歲，顓頊曆第十三蔀首與麟德曆俱以丁巳平旦立春。

translations.literal: Lu Duke Xuan year 15, dingmao year, Zhuanxu calendar thirteenth obscuration head with Lindé calendar both dingsi dawn Start of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duke Xuan's year 15, a dingmao year: the Zhuanxu calendar's thirteenth obscuration head and the Lindé calendar both give dingsi dawn at Start of Spring.

sentences.zh: 至始皇三十三年丁亥，凡三百八十歲，得顓頊曆壬申蔀首。

translations.literal: Reaching First Emperor year 33 dinghai, altogether three hundred eighty years, obtaining Zhuanxu calendar renshen obscuration head.
translations.idiomatic: By the First Emperor's year 33 dinghai, 380 years later, the Zhuanxu calendar reaches the renshen obscuration head.

sentences.zh: 是歲秦曆以壬申寅初立春，而開元曆與麟德曆俱以庚午平旦，差二日，日當在南斗二十二度。

translations.literal: That year Qin calendar by renshen yin initial Start of Spring, yet Kaiyuan and Lindé calendars both gengwu dawn, two days difference—sun ought at Southern Dipper twenty-two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Qin calendar has renshen yin initial Start of Spring while Kaiyuan and Lindé give gengwu dawn—two days apart—with the sun at twenty-two degrees of Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 古曆後天二日，又增二度。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar lagged heaven two days, again added two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar lagged heaven two days and added two degrees.

sentences.zh: 然則秦曆冬至，定在牛前二度。

translations.literal: Then Qin calendar winter solstice fixed at before Ox two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin calendar therefore fixed winter solstice two degrees before Ox.

sentences.zh: 氣後天二日，日不及天二度，微而難覺，故呂氏循用之。

translations.literal: Qi lagged heaven two days, sun not reaching heaven two degrees—subtle and hard to perceive—therefore Lü continued using it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi lagged heaven two days while the sun fell two degrees short—too subtle to notice—so Lü Buwei kept using it.

sentences.zh: 及漢興，張蒼等亦以為顓頊曆比五家疎闊中最近密。

translations.literal: Reaching Han rise, Zhang Cang and others also held Zhuanxu calendar compared to five schools coarse yet nearest dense.
translations.idiomatic: At the Han founding Zhang Cang and others also found the Zhuanxu calendar coarsest among five schools yet nearest to accuracy.

sentences.zh: 今考月蝕衝，則開元冬至，上及牛初正差一次。

translations.literal: Now examining lunar eclipse opposition, then Kaiyuan winter solstice upward reaching Ox beginning just one station short.
translations.idiomatic: Checking lunar eclipse opposition, Kaiyuan winter solstice extrapolated upward reaches just one station short of Ox's beginning.

sentences.zh: 淳風以為古術疎舛，雖弦望、昏明，差天十五度而猶不知。

translations.literal: Chunfeng held ancient methods coarse and wrong—though quarter-moon, dusk-dawn, differ heaven fifteen degrees yet still not knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng called ancient methods coarse and erroneous—they missed a fifteen-degree discrepancy in quarter-moons and dusk-dawn.

sentences.zh: 又引呂氏春秋，黃帝以仲春乙卯日在奎，始奏十二鍾，命之曰咸池。

translations.literal: Also citing Lüshi Chunqiu, Yellow Emperor mid-spring yimao day sun at Kui, first played twelve bells, named it Xianchi.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited Lüshi Chunqiu: at mid-spring on yimao with the sun at Kui the Yellow Emperor first played the twelve bells and named the pool Xianchi.

sentences.zh: 至今三千餘年，而春分亦在奎，反謂秦曆與今不異。

translations.literal: To now three thousand-plus years, yet spring equinox also at Kui—on the contrary saying Qin calendar same as present.
translations.idiomatic: After 3,000-plus years spring equinox still falls at Kui—yet he claimed the Qin calendar matches the present.

sentences.zh: 按不韋所記，以其月令孟春在奎，謂黃帝之時亦在奎，猶淳風曆冬至斗十三度，因謂黃帝時亦在建星耳。

translations.literal: Examining Lü's record, by its Monthly Ordinances first spring at Kui, saying Yellow Emperor's time also at Kui—like Chunfeng calendar winter solstice Dipper thirteen degrees, therefore saying Yellow Emperor's time also at Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lü placed first spring at Kui in his Monthly Ordinances and assumed the Yellow Emperor's era did too—just as Chunfeng fixed winter solstice at thirteen degrees of Dipper and assumed the Yellow Emperor's era matched Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 經籍所載，合於歲差者，淳風皆不取，而專取於呂氏春秋。

translations.literal: Classics' records matching precession—Chunfeng all not taking, yet exclusively taking from Lüshi Chunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Classical records that fit precession Chunfeng ignored, relying instead on Lüshi Chunqiu.

sentences.zh: 若謂十二紀可以為正，則立春在營室五度，固當不易，安得頓移，使當啟蟄之節？

translations.literal: If saying twelve chronicles can be correct, then Start of Spring at Encampment five degrees surely ought unchanged—how suddenly shift to match Awakening of Insects node?
translations.idiomatic: If the twelve chronicles were authoritative, Start of Spring at five degrees of Encampment should never move—how could it jump to Awakening of Insects?

sentences.zh: 此又其所不思也。

translations.literal: This again what he did not think.
translations.idiomatic: He never considered that contradiction.

sentences.zh: 漢四百二十六年，日却差五度。

translations.literal: Han four hundred twenty-six years, sun retreating differs five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Over the Han's 426 years the sun retreated five degrees.

sentences.zh: 景帝中元三年甲午歲冬至，應在斗二十一度。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing Zhongyuan year 3 jiawu year winter solstice should be at Dipper twenty-one degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice of Emperor Jing's Zhongyuan year 3, a jiawu year, should fall at twenty-one degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 太初元年，三統曆及周曆皆以十一月夜半合朔冬至，日月俱起牽牛一度。

translations.literal: Taichu year 1, Three Systems and Zhou calendars all eleventh month midnight conjunction winter solstice, sun and moon both rise Ox one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu year 1: the Three Systems and Zhou calendars both place eleventh-month midnight conjunction at winter solstice with sun and moon at one degree of Ox.

sentences.zh: 古曆與近代密率相較，二百年氣差一日，三百年朔差一日。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar compared with recent dense rates, two hundred years qi differs one day, three hundred years new moon differs one day.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with recent precise rates, the ancient calendar drifts one day in qi every 200 years and one day in new moon every 300 years.

sentences.zh: 推而上之，久益先天；

translations.literal: Extrapolating upward, long then precedes heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating backward it runs increasingly ahead of heaven;

sentences.zh: 引而下之，久益後天。

translations.literal: Drawing downward, long then lags heaven.
translations.idiomatic: extrapolating forward it falls increasingly behind.

sentences.zh: 僖公五年，周曆正月辛亥朔，餘四分之一，南至。

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 5, Zhou calendar first month xinhai new moon, remainder one quarter, south arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi's year 5: Zhou calendar first month xinhai new moon with one-quarter remainder at south arrival.

sentences.zh: 以歲差推之，日在牽牛初。

translations.literal: By precession extrapolation, sun at Ox beginning.
translations.idiomatic: By precession the sun stood at Ox's beginning.

sentences.zh: 至宣公十一年癸亥，周曆與麟德曆俱以庚戌日中冬至，而月朔尚先麟德曆十五辰。

translations.literal: Reaching Duke Xuan year 11 guihai, Zhou and Lindé calendars both gengxu midday winter solstice, yet month new moon still fifteen chen before Lindé.
translations.idiomatic: By Duke Xuan year 11 guihai, Zhou and Lindé calendars both give gengxu midday winter solstice, yet the month's new moon still precedes Lindé by fifteen chen.

sentences.zh: 至昭公二十年己卯，周曆以正月己丑朔日中南至，麟德曆以己丑平旦冬至。

translations.literal: Reaching Duke Zhao year 20 jimao, Zhou calendar first month jichou new moon midday south arrival, Lindé jichou dawn winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: By Duke Zhao year 20 jimao, the Zhou calendar has first month jichou new moon at midday south arrival while Lindé has jichou dawn winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 哀公十一年丁巳，周曆入己酉蔀首，麟德曆以戊申禺中冬至。

translations.literal: Duke Ai year 11 dingsi, Zhou calendar entering jiyou obscuration head, Lindé wushen mid-afternoon winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai year 11 dingsi: Zhou calendar enters jiyou obscuration head; Lindé has wushen mid-afternoon winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 惠王四十三年己丑，周曆入丁卯蔀首，麟德曆以乙丑日昳冬至。

translations.literal: King Hui year 43 jichou, Zhou calendar entering dingmao obscuration head, Lindé yichou mid-afternoon winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: King Hui year 43 jichou: Zhou enters dingmao obscuration head; Lindé has yichou mid-afternoon winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 呂后八年辛酉，周曆入乙酉蔀首，麟德曆以壬午黃昏冬至；

translations.literal: Empress Lü year 8 xinyou, Zhou calendar entering yiyou obscuration head, Lindé renwu dusk winter solstice;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü year 8 xinyou: Zhou enters yiyou obscuration head; Lindé has renwu dusk winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 其十二月甲申，人定合朔。

translations.literal: Its twelfth month jiashen, human-ding conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth month jiashen conjunction at the human-ding hour.

sentences.zh: 太初元年，周曆以甲子夜半合朔冬至，麟德曆以辛酉禺中冬至，十二月癸亥晡時合朔。

translations.literal: Taichu year 1, Zhou calendar jiazi midnight conjunction winter solstice, Lindé xinyou mid-afternoon winter solstice, twelfth month guihai late-afternoon conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu year 1: Zhou has jiazi midnight conjunction at winter solstice; Lindé has xinyou mid-afternoon winter solstice and twelfth month guihai late-afternoon conjunction.

sentences.zh: 氣差三十二辰，朔差四辰。

translations.literal: Qi difference thirty-two chen, new moon difference four chen.
translations.idiomatic: Qi differs by thirty-two chen, new moon by four chen.

sentences.zh: 此疎密之大較也。

translations.literal: This coarse-dense great comparison.
translations.idiomatic: That is the broad comparison of coarse versus precise.

sentences.zh: 僖公五年，周曆、漢曆、唐曆皆以辛亥南至。

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 5, Zhou, Han, and Tang calendars all xinhai south arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi's year 5: Zhou, Han, and Tang calendars all give xinhai south arrival.

sentences.zh: 後五百五十餘歲，至太初元年，周曆、漢曆皆得甲子夜半冬至，唐曆皆以辛酉，則漢曆後天三日矣。

translations.literal: After five hundred fifty-plus years reaching Taichu year 1, Zhou and Han both jiazi midnight winter solstice, Tang all xinyou—then Han calendar lags heaven three days.
translations.idiomatic: 550-plus years later at Taichu year 1, Zhou and Han both give jiazi midnight winter solstice while Tang gives xinyou—the Han calendar lags heaven three days.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之、張冑玄促上章歲至太初元年，沖之以癸亥雞鳴冬至，而冑玄以癸亥日出。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi and Zhang Zouxuan shortened upper chapter year to Taichu year 1—Chongzhi guihai cock-crow winter solstice, Zouxuan guihai sunrise.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi and Zhang Zouxuan shortened the upper chapter year to Taichu year 1—Chongzhi gives guihai cock-crow winter solstice and Zouxuan guihai sunrise.

sentences.zh: 欲令合於甲子，而適與魯曆相會。

translations.literal: Wishing to make match jiazi, yet by chance meeting Lu calendar.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to match jiazi while aligning with the Lu calendar.

sentences.zh: 自此推僖公五年，魯曆以庚戌冬至，而二家皆以甲寅。

translations.literal: From this extrapolating Duke Xi year 5, Lu calendar gengxu winter solstice, yet both families jiayin.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating back to Duke Xi year 5, the Lu calendar gives gengxu winter solstice while both give jiayin.

sentences.zh: 且僖公登觀臺以望而書雲物，出於表晷天驗，非時史億度。

translations.literal: And Duke Xi ascending observation tower to observe and record cloud things—coming from gnomon heavenly verification, not chronicle officers' estimated degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi observed from the tower and recorded cloud signs—gnomon verification, not chronicle estimates.

sentences.zh: 乖丘明正時之意，以就劉歆之失。

translations.literal: Contrary to Qiu Ming's correct-time intent, to accommodate Liu Xin's error.
translations.idiomatic: That betrays Qiu Ming's correct timing to fit Liu Xin's error.

sentences.zh: 今考麟德元年甲子，唐曆皆以甲子冬至，而周曆、漢曆皆以庚午。

translations.literal: Now examining Lindé year 1 jiazi, Tang calendars all jiazi winter solstice, yet Zhou and Han both gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: At Lindé year 1 jiazi the Tang calendars give jiazi winter solstice while Zhou and Han give gengwu.

sentences.zh: 然則自太初下至麟德差四日，自太初上及僖公差三日，不足疑也。

translations.literal: Then from Taichu down to Lindé four days difference, from Taichu up to Duke Xi three days—not enough to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: From Taichu down to Lindé differs four days; from Taichu up to Duke Xi three days—not enough to doubt.

sentences.zh: 以歲差考太初元年辛酉冬至加時，日在斗二十三度。

translations.literal: By precession examining Taichu year 1 xinyou winter solstice added time, sun at Dipper twenty-three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: By precession Taichu year 1 xinyou winter solstice added time places the sun at twenty-three degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 漢曆，氣後天三日，而日先天三度，所差尚少。

translations.literal: Han calendar, qi lagged heaven three days, yet sun preceded heaven three degrees—the difference still small.
translations.idiomatic: The Han calendar lagged three days in qi while the sun ran three degrees ahead—the net error was still small.

sentences.zh: 故落下閎等雖候昏明中星，步日所在，猶未覺其差。

translations.literal: Therefore Luoxia Hong and others though observing dusk-dawn centered stars, stepping sun's place, still not perceiving the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Luoxia Hong and colleagues therefore did not notice the discrepancy even when observing dusk-dawn stars and tracking the sun.

sentences.zh: 然洪範、太初所揆，冬至昏奎八度中，夏至昏氐十三度中，依漢曆，冬至，日在牽牛初太半度，以昏距中命之，奎十一度中；

translations.literal: Yet Hongfan and Taichu measured, winter solstice dusk Kui eight degrees centered, summer solstice dusk Di thirteen degrees centered—by Han calendar winter solstice sun at Ox beginning great half degree, by dusk distance center naming, Kui eleven degrees centered;
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan and Taichu measured winter-solstice dusk Kui at eight degrees and summer-solstice dusk Di at thirteen; by the Han calendar winter solstice is at great half of Ox beginning, naming dusk distance gives Kui at eleven degrees;

sentences.zh: 夏至，房一度中。

translations.literal: Summer solstice, Fang one degree centered.
translations.idiomatic: summer solstice Fang at one degree centered.

sentences.zh: 此皆閎等所測，自差三度，則劉向等殆已知太初冬至不及天三度矣。

translations.literal: These all Hong and others measured—self differing three degrees—then Liu Xiang and others probably already knew Taichu winter solstice not reaching heaven three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: These were Hong's measurements, off by three degrees—Liu Xiang and others probably already knew Taichu winter solstice fell three degrees short of heaven.

sentences.zh: 及永平中，治曆者考行事，史官注日，常不及太初曆五度。

translations.literal: Reaching Yongping, calendar makers examined affairs, historiographers' annotated days often not reaching Taichu calendar five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: By Yongping, calendar makers checking records found historiographers' dates often five degrees short of the Taichu calendar.

sentences.zh: 然諸儒守讖緯，以為當在牛初，故賈逵等議：「石氏星距，黃道規牽牛初直斗二十度，於赤道二十一度也。

translations.literal: Yet scholars guarding apocrypha held ought at Ox beginning—therefore Jia Kui and others proposed: "Shi's star distance, ecliptic rule Ox beginning directly Dipper twenty degrees, on equator twenty-one degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars clinging to apocrypha insisted on Ox's beginning; Jia Kui argued: "Shi's star distance places ecliptic Ox beginning at twenty degrees of Dipper, twenty-one on the equator.

sentences.zh: 尚書考靈耀斗二十二度，無餘分。

translations.literal: Documents Examining Spirit's Radiance Dipper twenty-two degrees, no surplus fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Spirit's Radiance gives Dipper twenty-two degrees with no remainder.

sentences.zh: 冬至，日在牽牛初，無牽牛所起文。

translations.literal: Winter solstice sun at Ox beginning, no Ox-starting text.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice at Ox beginning lacks Ox-starting documentation.

sentences.zh: 編訢等據今日所去牽牛中星五度，於斗二十一度四分一，與考靈耀相近。

translations.literal: Bian Xin and others according to today's distance from Ox center star five degrees, at Dipper twenty-one degrees quarter one—near Examining Spirit's Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Xin, using today's five degrees from Ox's center star, gets twenty-one and a quarter degrees of Dipper—near Examining Spirit's Radiance.

sentences.zh: 」遂更曆從斗二十一度起。

translations.literal: Then changed calendar following Dipper twenty-one degrees start.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore revised the calendar to start at twenty-one degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 然古曆以斗魁首為距，至牽牛為二十二度，未聞移牽牛六度以就太初星距也。

translations.literal: Yet ancient calendar taking Dipper head as distance, reaching Ox twenty-two degrees—never heard moving Ox six degrees to match Taichu star distance.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar used the Dipper's head as reference to twenty-two degrees of Ox—never shifting Ox six degrees to match Taichu distance.

sentences.zh: 逵等以末學僻於所傳，而昧天象，故以權誣之，而後聽從他術，以為日在牛初者，由此遂黜。

translations.literal: Kui and others by late learning narrow in transmission, obscured to celestial signs—therefore by authority deceiving—afterward listening following other methods, holding sun at Ox beginning—hereby dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and colleagues, ignorant of the heavens, used authority to mislead; later followers held the sun at Ox beginning and the correct view was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 今歲差，引而退之，則辛酉冬至，日在斗二十度，合於密率，而有驗於今。

translations.literal: Now precession drawing retreating, then xinyou winter solstice sun at Dipper twenty degrees, matching dense rate, and verified today.
translations.idiomatic: With precession, xinyou winter solstice places the sun at twenty degrees of Dipper—matching precise rates and verified today.

sentences.zh: 推而進之，則甲子冬至，日在斗二十四度，昏奎八度中，而有證於古。

translations.literal: Pushing advancing, then jiazi winter solstice sun at Dipper twenty-four degrees, dusk Kui eight degrees centered, and evidenced in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing forward, jiazi winter solstice is at twenty-four degrees of Dipper with Kui at eight degrees centered at dusk—confirmed in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其虛退之度，又適及牽牛之初。

translations.literal: Its void-retreating degrees again reaching Ox beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The retreating degrees again reach Ox's beginning.

sentences.zh: 而沖之雖促減氣分，冀符漢曆，猶差六度，未及於天。

translations.literal: Yet Chongzhi though shortened reducing qi fraction, hoping match Han calendar, still six degrees short, not reaching heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi shortened the qi fraction hoping to match the Han calendar yet still fell six degrees short of heaven.

sentences.zh: 而麟德曆冬至不移，則昏中向差半次。

translations.literal: Yet Lindé calendar winter solstice unmoved—then dusk centered toward half station difference.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar kept winter solstice fixed, so dusk culmination stars differ by half a station.

sentences.zh: 淳風以為太初元年得本星度，日月合璧，俱起建星。

translations.literal: Chunfeng held Taichu year 1 obtained original star degrees, sun and moon jade disk, both rise Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng held that Taichu year 1 recovered original star degrees with sun and moon conjoined, both rising at Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 賈逵考曆，亦云古曆冬至皆起建星。

translations.literal: Jia Kui examining calendar also says ancient calendar winter solstice all start Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui also said ancient calendars all start winter solstice at Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 兩漢冬至，日皆後天，故其宿度多在斗末。

translations.literal: Two Han winter solstice sun all lagged heaven—therefore its lodge degrees mostly at Dipper's end.
translations.idiomatic: Both Han winter solstices lagged heaven, so lodge degrees mostly fell at Dipper's end.

sentences.zh: 今以儀測，建星在斗十三四度間，自古冬至無差，審矣。

translations.literal: Now by instrument measuring, Jianxing at Dipper thirteen-four degrees between—from antiquity winter solstice no difference, examined clear.
translations.idiomatic: Instrument measurement places Jianxing between thirteen and fourteen degrees of Dipper—winter solstice has not shifted since antiquity; that is clear.

sentences.zh: 按古之六術，並同四分。

translations.literal: Examining ancient six methods, all same as Quarter-Remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient six methods all match the Quarter-Remainder system.

sentences.zh: 四分之法，久則後天。

translations.literal: Quarter-Remainder method long then lags heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-Remainder method eventually lags heaven.

sentences.zh: 推古曆之作，皆在漢初，却較春秋，朔並先天，則非三代之前明矣。

translations.literal: Extrapolating ancient calendar's making—all at Han beginning, comparing Spring and Autumn, new moon all precedes heaven—then not before Three Dynasties clear.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars were all devised in early Han; compared with the Spring and Autumn their new moons run ahead—clearly not pre-dating the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 古曆，南斗至牽牛上星二十一度，入太初星距四度，上直西建之初。

translations.literal: Ancient calendar Southern Dipper to Ox upper star twenty-one degrees, entering Taichu star distance four degrees, upper directly West Jian's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient calendar counts twenty-one degrees from Southern Dipper to Ox's upper star—four degrees into Taichu distance, directly at West Jian's start.

sentences.zh: 故六家或以南斗命度，或以建星命度。

translations.literal: Therefore six schools some by Southern Dipper naming degrees, some by Jianxing naming degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Hence some schools name degrees from Southern Dipper, others from Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 方周、漢之交，日已潛退，其襲春秋舊曆者，則以為在牽牛之首；

translations.literal: At Zhou-Han crossing, sun already secretly retreated—those following Spring and Autumn old calendar then held at Ox beginning;
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhou-Han transition the sun had already retreated; those following the Spring and Autumn calendar placed it at Ox's beginning;

sentences.zh: 其考當時之驗者，則以為入建星度中。

translations.literal: Those examining then verification then held entering Jianxing degrees center.
translations.idiomatic: those checking contemporary observation placed it within Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 然氣朔前後不逾一日，故漢曆冬至，當在斗末。

translations.literal: Yet qi and new moon before-after not exceeding one day—therefore Han calendar winter solstice ought at Dipper end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet qi and new moon differ by no more than a day—so Han winter solstice should fall at Dipper's end.

sentences.zh: 以為建星上得太初本星度，此其明據也。

translations.literal: Holding Jianxing upper obtaining Taichu original star degrees—this its clear evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Placing Jianxing upper at Taichu's original star degree is the clear evidence.

sentences.zh: 四分法雖疎，而先賢謹於天事，其遷革之意，俱有効於當時，故太史公等觀二十八宿疎密，立晷儀，下漏刻，以稽晦朔、分至、躔離、弦望，其赤道遺法，後世無以非之。

translations.literal: Quarter-Remainder method though coarse, yet sages careful in heaven's affairs—their revision intent all effective at the time—therefore Grand Historian and others observing twenty-eight lodges coarse-dense, establishing gnomon instrument, lowering clepsydra quarters, to examine new-dark, divide-arrive, progression-departure, quarter-moon, full-moon—their equatorial legacy method, later generations cannot refute.
translations.idiomatic: Though coarse, the Quarter-Remainder method reflects careful celestial work effective in its day; the Grand Historian and others observed lodge density, set gnomons and clepsydrae, and tracked new and full moons, solstices, and lunar motion—equatorial methods later generations cannot refute.

sentences.zh: 故雜候清臺，太初最密。

translations.literal: Therefore mixed observation Clear Terrace, Taichu most dense.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed observations at the Clear Terrace rank Taichu densest.

sentences.zh: 若當時日在建星，已直斗十三度，則壽王調曆宜允得其中，豈容頓差一氣而未知其謬，不能觀乎時變，而欲厚誣古人也。

translations.literal: If then sun at Jianxing, already directly Dipper thirteen degrees—then Shouwang adjusting calendar ought to hit center—how could it suddenly differ one qi and not know its error, cannot observe time's change, yet want thick slander ancients.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun were at Jianxing, already at thirteen degrees of Dipper, Shouwang's calendar adjustment should have hit center—how could it miss an entire qi unknowingly, fail to observe change, yet slander the ancients?

sentences.zh: 後百餘歲，至永平十一年，以麟德曆較之，氣當後天二日半，朔當後天半日。

translations.literal: After hundred-plus years reaching Yongping year 11, by Lindé calendar comparing, qi ought lag heaven two and a half days, new moon half day.
translations.idiomatic: A century later, by Yongping year 11 compared with Lindé, qi should lag two and a half days and new moon half a day.

sentences.zh: 是歲四分曆得辛酉蔀首，已減太初曆四分日之三，定後天二日太半。

translations.literal: That year Quarter-Remainder obtained xinyou obscuration head, already reduced Taichu calendar three-quarters day, fixed lag heaven two and a half days great.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Quarter-Remainder reached xinyou obscuration head, having cut three-quarters day from Taichu, fixing lag at two and a half days.

sentences.zh: 開元曆以戊午禺中冬至，日在斗十八度半弱，潛退至牛前八度。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan calendar by wuwu mid-afternoon winter solstice, sun at Dipper eighteen and a half weak degrees, secretly retreated to before Ox eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar gives wuwu mid-afternoon winter solstice with the sun at eighteen and a half weak degrees of Dipper, retreated to eight degrees before Ox.

sentences.zh: 進至辛酉夜半，日在斗二十一度半弱。

translations.literal: Advancing to xinyou midnight, sun at Dipper twenty-one and a half weak degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to xinyou midnight places the sun at twenty-one and a half weak degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 續漢志云：「元和二年冬至，日在斗二十一度四分之一。

translations.literal: Continued Han Treatise says: "Yuanhe year 2 winter solstice, sun at Dipper twenty-one degrees quarter one."
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Han Treatise says: "Yuanhe year 2 winter solstice, sun at twenty-one and a quarter degrees of Dipper."

sentences.zh: 」是也。

translations.literal: It is so.
translations.idiomatic: So it records.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之曰：「四分曆立冬景長一丈，立春九尺六寸，冬至南極日晷最長。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi said: "Quarter-Remainder calendar Start of Winter shadow one zhang, Start of Spring nine chi six cun, winter solstice south pole gnomon shadow longest.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: "The Quarter-Remainder calendar gives Start of Winter shadow one zhang and Start of Spring nine chi six cun; winter solstice has the longest south-pole gnomon shadow.

sentences.zh: 二氣去至日數既同，則中景應等。

translations.literal: Two qi distance to solstice days same, then midday shadows ought equal.
translations.idiomatic: The two qi are equally distant from solstice, so midday shadows should match.

sentences.zh: 而相差四寸，此冬至後天之驗也。

translations.literal: Yet differ four cun—this winter solstice lagging heaven's verification.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they differ four cun—proof that winter solstice lags heaven.

sentences.zh: 二氣中景，日差九分半弱，進退調均，略無盈縮。

translations.literal: Two qi midday shadows, day difference nine and a half weak parts, advance-retreat evenly adjusted, slightly no surplus-deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Midday shadows at the two qi differ by nine and a half weak parts per day; evenly adjusted there is almost no surplus or deficit.

sentences.zh: 各退二日十二刻，則景皆九尺八寸。

translations.literal: Each retreat two days twelve quarters, then shadows all nine chi eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: Retreat two days twelve quarters each and shadows become nine chi eight cun.

sentences.zh: 以此推冬至後天亦二日十二刻矣。

translations.literal: By this extrapolate winter solstice also lags heaven two days twelve quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating, winter solstice also lags heaven by two days twelve quarters.

sentences.zh: 」東漢晷漏定於永元十四年，則四分法施行後十五歲也。

translations.literal: Eastern Han gnomon clepsydra fixed at Yongyuan year 14—then Quarter-Remainder method implemented fifteen years after.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han gnomon and clepsydra were fixed in Yongyuan year 14—fifteen years after the Quarter-Remainder method was implemented.

sentences.zh: 二十四氣加時，進退不等，其去午正極遠者四十九刻有餘。

translations.literal: Twenty-four qi added time, advance-retreat not equal—their distance from wu midday extreme farthest forty-nine-plus quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four qi added times advance and retreat unevenly, farthest from wu midday by forty-nine-plus quarters.

sentences.zh: 日中之晷，頗有盈縮，故治曆者皆就其中率，以午正言之。

translations.literal: Midday gnomon shadow, quite has surplus-deficit—therefore calendar makers all take among them the mean rate, by wu midday speak.
translations.idiomatic: Midday gnomon shadows vary; calendrists therefore use the mean rate and speak relative to wu midday.

sentences.zh: 而開元曆所推氣及日度，皆直子半之始。

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan calendar's derived qi-periods and solar degrees all align straight with the start of midnight at Zi.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan calendar's derived qi-periods and solar degrees all align with the start of midnight at Zi.

sentences.zh: 其未及日中，尚五十刻。

translations.literal: Before reaching midday it still lacked fifty ke.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching midday it still fell short by fifty ke.

sentences.zh: 因加二日十二刻，正得二日太半。

translations.literal: Adding two days and twelve ke yields exactly two and a half days.
translations.idiomatic: Adding two days and twelve ke gives exactly two and a half days.

sentences.zh: 與沖之所算及破章二百年間輒差一日之數，皆合。

translations.literal: Compared with Chong's calculations and the one-day discrepancy every two hundred years when breaking a rule, all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Chong's calculations and the one-day drift every two hundred years when a rule cycle breaks, everything matched.

sentences.zh: 自漢時辛酉冬至，以後天之數減之，則合於今曆歲差斗十八度。

translations.literal: From the Xinyou winter solstice of Han times, subtracting the later-heaven numbers, it matches the present calendar's precession of eighteen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han-era Xinyou winter solstice, subtracting the later-heaven numbers matches the present calendar's precession of eighteen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 自今曆戊午冬至，以後天之數加之，則合於賈逵所測斗二十一度。

translations.literal: From the Wuwu winter solstice of the present calendar, adding the later-heaven numbers, it matches the twenty-one degrees in Dipper measured by Jia Kui.
translations.idiomatic: From the present calendar's Wuwu winter solstice, adding the later-heaven numbers matches the twenty-one degrees in the Dipper measured by Jia Kui.

sentences.zh: 反復僉同。

translations.literal: Repeated checks all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated checks all agreed.

sentences.zh: 而淳風冬至常在斗十三度，豈當時知不及牽牛五度，而不知過建星八度耶？

translations.literal: Yet Chunfeng's winter solstice constantly stood at thirteen degrees in Dipper—could he then have known it fell five degrees short of Ox but not known it passed eight degrees beyond Jian?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chunfeng placed the winter solstice constantly at thirteen degrees in the Dipper—could he have known it fell five degrees short of Ox yet not known it overshot Jian by eight degrees?

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太始三年丁亥歲冬至，日當在斗十六度。

translations.literal: In Taishi year 3 of Emperor Wu of Jin, the Dinghai year's winter solstice, the sun ought to have been at sixteen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: At the Dinghai winter solstice in Jin Emperor Wu's Taishi year 3, the sun should have stood at sixteen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 晉用魏景初曆，其冬至亦在斗二十一度少。

translations.literal: Jin used Wei's Jingchu calendar; its winter solstice also stood at a little more than twenty-one degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Jin used Wei's Jingchu calendar, whose winter solstice also fell at just over twenty-one degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 太元九年，姜岌更造三紀術，退在斗十七度。

translations.literal: In Taiyuan year 9, Jiang Ji remade the Three Era method, retreating to seventeen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 9 Jiang Ji remade the Three Era method, placing the solstice at seventeen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 曰：「古曆斗分彊，故不可施於今；

translations.literal: He said: 'Ancient calendars' Dipper parts were too strong, therefore they cannot be applied to the present;
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'Ancient calendars used too large a Dipper fraction, so they cannot be applied today;

sentences.zh: 乾象斗分細，故不可通於古。

translations.literal: the Supernal Icon calendar's Dipper parts were too fine, therefore they cannot connect with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: the Supernal Icon calendar's Dipper fraction was too fine, so it cannot connect with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 景初雖得其中，而日之所在；

translations.literal: Jingchu though hit the mean, yet the sun's position
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu though it hit the mean, the sun's position

sentences.zh: 乃差四度，合朔虧盈，皆不及其次。

translations.literal: was off by four degrees; conjunction new moons and eclipse fullness and deficiency all missed their proper nodes.
translations.idiomatic: was four degrees off; conjunction new moons and eclipse phases all missed their proper nodes.

sentences.zh: 假月在東井一度蝕，以日檢之，乃在參六度。

translations.literal: Suppose the moon eclipsed at one degree in Well—checking by the sun, it was actually at six degrees in Three Stars.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the moon eclipsed at one degree in Well—checking against the sun, it was actually at six degrees in Three Stars.

sentences.zh: 」岌以月蝕衝知日度，由是躔次遂正，為後代治曆者宗。

translations.literal: ' Ji, by lunar eclipse opposition, knew the sun's degree; thereby the lodge positions were corrected, and later calendar makers took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ji determined the sun's degree from lunar eclipse opposition; thereby the lodge positions were corrected, and later calendar makers took him as their authority.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝時，何承天上元嘉曆，曰：「四分、景初曆，冬至同在斗二十一度，臣以月蝕檢之，則今應在斗十七度。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wen of Song, He Chengtian presented the Shangyuan-Jia calendar, saying: 'The Four Quarters and Jingchu calendars both placed the winter solstice at twenty-one degrees in Dipper; I checked by lunar eclipse and found it ought now to be at seventeen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Song, He Chengtian presented the Shangyuan-Jia calendar, saying: 'The Four Quarters and Jingchu calendars both placed the winter solstice at twenty-one degrees in the Dipper; I checked by lunar eclipse and found it should now be at seventeen degrees.

sentences.zh: 又土圭測二至，晷差三日有餘，則天之南至，日在斗十三四度矣。

translations.literal: Also measuring the two solstices with the gnomon, the shadow difference exceeded three days; then heaven's southern extreme—the sun stood at thirteen or fourteen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring the two solstices with the gnomon, the shadow difference exceeded three days—meaning at heaven's southern extreme the sun stood at thirteen or fourteen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 」事下太史考驗，如承天所上。

translations.literal: ' The matter was sent down to the Grand Astrologer for verification, matching what Chengtian submitted.
translations.idiomatic: ' The matter was referred to the Grand Astrologer for verification, and matched Chengtian's figures.

sentences.zh: 以開元曆考元嘉十年冬至，日在斗十四度，與承天所測合。

translations.literal: Checking Yuanjia year 10's winter solstice with the Kaiyuan calendar, the sun stood at fourteen degrees in Dipper, matching Chengtian's measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Checking Yuanjia 10's winter solstice with the Kaiyuan calendar, the sun stood at fourteen degrees in the Dipper, matching Chengtian's measurement.

sentences.zh: 大明八年，祖沖之上大明曆，冬至在斗十一度，開元曆應在斗十三度。

translations.literal: In Daming year 8, Zu Chongzhi submitted the Daming calendar; the winter solstice stood at eleven degrees in Dipper—the Kaiyuan calendar places it at thirteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 8 Zu Chongzhi submitted the Daming calendar, placing the winter solstice at eleven degrees in the Dipper; the Kaiyuan calendar places it at thirteen degrees.

sentences.zh: 梁天監八年，沖之子員外散騎侍郎暅之上其家術。

translations.literal: In Liang Tiantian year 8, Chongzhi's son, Attendant Outside the Scattereds Xu, submitted their family method.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Tiantian 8, Zu Chongzhi's son Xu, Attendant Outside the Scattereds, submitted their family method.

sentences.zh: 詔太史令將作大匠道秀等較之，上距大明又五十年，日度益差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Astrologer and Master of Works Dao Xiu and others to compare it; upward from Daming another fifty years had passed, and solar degrees had grown still more divergent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Grand Astrologer and Master of Works Dao Xiu and others to compare it; fifty years after Daming, solar degrees had diverged still further.

sentences.zh: 其明年，閏月十六日，月蝕，在虛十度，日應在張四度。

translations.literal: The next year, on the sixteenth of the intercalary month, a lunar eclipse occurred at ten degrees in Void—the sun ought to have been at four degrees in Extended Net.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the sixteenth of the intercalary month, the moon eclipsed at ten degrees in Void—the sun should have stood at four degrees in Extended Net.

sentences.zh: 承天曆在張六度，沖之曆在張二度。

translations.literal: Chengtian's calendar placed it at six degrees in Extended Net; Chongzhi's calendar at two degrees in Extended Net.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian's calendar placed it at six degrees in Extended Net; Chongzhi's at two degrees.

sentences.zh: 大同九年，虞𠠎等議：「姜岌、何承天俱以月蝕衝步日所在。

translations.literal: In Datong year 9, Yu Xiao and others argued: 'Jiang Ji and He Chengtian both stepped off the sun's position by lunar eclipse opposition.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 9 Yu Xiao and others argued: 'Jiang Ji and He Chengtian both determined the sun's position from lunar eclipse opposition.

sentences.zh: 承天雖移岌三度，然其冬至亦上岌三日。

translations.literal: Chengtian though shifted Ji by three degrees, yet his winter solstice also advanced Ji by three days.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian though he shifted Ji by three degrees, his winter solstice also advanced Ji's date by three days.

sentences.zh: 承天在斗十三四度，而岌在斗十七度。

translations.literal: Chengtian placed it at thirteen or fourteen degrees in Dipper, while Ji at seventeen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian placed it at thirteen or fourteen degrees in the Dipper, while Ji at seventeen degrees.

sentences.zh: 其實非移。

translations.literal: In fact there was no shift.
translations.idiomatic: In fact there was no true shift.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之謂為實差，以推今冬至，日在斗九度，用求中星不合。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi called it a real discrepancy; projecting the present winter solstice, the sun stood at nine degrees in Dipper—using it to seek the culminating stars, it did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi treated it as a real discrepancy; projecting the present winter solstice to nine degrees in the Dipper and seeking the culminating stars from that, the result did not agree.

sentences.zh: 自岌至今，將二百年，而冬至在斗十二度。

translations.literal: From Ji to the present, nearly two hundred years, and the winter solstice stands at twelve degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: From Ji to the present, nearly two hundred years have passed, and the winter solstice stands at twelve degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 然日之所在難知，驗以中星，則漏刻不定。

translations.literal: Yet the sun's position is hard to know; verifying by culminating stars, the clepsydra graduations are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sun's position is hard to know directly; verifying by culminating stars leaves clepsydra graduations uncertain.

sentences.zh: 漢世課昏明中星，為法已淺。

translations.literal: Han times gauged twilight and dawn culminating stars—a method already shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Han practice gauged twilight and dawn culminating stars—a method already too coarse.

sentences.zh: 今候夜半中星，以求日衝，近於得密。

translations.literal: Now observing culminating stars at midnight to seek solar opposition is closer to obtaining precision.
translations.idiomatic: Observing culminating stars at midnight to find solar opposition is closer to precision.

sentences.zh: 而水有清濁，壺有增減，或積塵所擁，故漏有遲疾。

translations.literal: Yet water has clarity and turbidity, vessels increase and decrease, or accumulated dust blocks them—therefore the clepsydra runs slow and fast.
translations.idiomatic: Yet water varies in clarity, vessels in capacity, and dust may clog them—so clepsydra flow runs slow or fast.

sentences.zh: 臣等頻夜候中星，而前後相差或至三度。

translations.literal: We repeatedly observed culminating stars at night, yet the before-and-after difference sometimes reached three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: We repeatedly observed culminating stars at night, yet successive readings sometimes differed by as much as three degrees.

sentences.zh: 大略冬至遠不過斗十四度，近不出十度。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the winter solstice never recedes beyond fourteen degrees in Dipper, nor advances short of ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, the winter solstice never recedes beyond fourteen degrees in the Dipper nor falls short of ten degrees.

sentences.zh: 」又以九年三月十五日夜半，月在房四度蝕。

translations.literal: ' They also took the midnight of the fifteenth of the third month in year 9: the moon eclipsed at four degrees in Room.
translations.idiomatic: ' They also took midnight on the fifteenth of the third month in year 9, when the moon eclipsed at four degrees in Room.

sentences.zh: 九月十五日夜半，月在昴三度蝕。

translations.literal: The midnight of the fifteenth of the ninth month: the moon eclipsed at three degrees in Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: Midnight on the fifteenth of the ninth month, when the moon eclipsed at three degrees in Hairy Head.

sentences.zh: 以其衝計，冬至皆在斗十二度。

translations.literal: Computing from their opposition, the winter solstice in both cases stood at twelve degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Computing from their opposition, both winter solstices fell at twelve degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 自姜岌、何承天所測，下及大同，日已却差二度。

translations.literal: From the measurements of Jiang Ji and He Chengtian down to Datong, the sun had already retreated two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiang Ji and He Chengtian's measurements down to Datong, the sun had already retreated two degrees.

sentences.zh: 而淳風以為晉、宋以來三百餘歲，以月蝕衝考之，固在斗十三四度間，非矣。

translations.literal: Yet Chunfeng held that for three hundred-odd years from Jin and Song, checked by lunar eclipse opposition, it firmly stood between thirteen and fourteen degrees in Dipper—which was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chunfeng held that for three hundred-odd years from Jin and Song, checked by lunar eclipse opposition, it firmly stood between thirteen and fourteen degrees in the Dipper—which was wrong.

sentences.zh: 劉孝孫甲子元曆，推太初冬至在牽牛初，下及晉太元、宋元嘉皆在斗十七度。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosun's Jiazi Origin calendar projected Taichu's winter solstice at the start of Ox, down through Jin Taiyuan and Song Yuanjia all at seventeen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun's Jiazi Origin calendar projected Taichu's winter solstice at the start of Ox, and down through Jin Taiyuan and Song Yuanjia at seventeen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年，在斗十三度。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang year 14 it stood at thirteen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 14 it stood at thirteen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 而劉焯曆仁壽四年冬至，日在黃道斗十度，於赤道斗十一度也。

translations.literal: Yet Liu Chuo's calendar for Renshou year 4's winter solstice placed the sun at ten degrees in Dipper on the Yellow Path—in ten degrees in Dipper on the Red Path.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Chuo's calendar for Renshou 4's winter solstice placed the sun at ten degrees in the Dipper on the ecliptic—eleven degrees in the Dipper on the equator.

sentences.zh: 其後孝孫改從焯法，而仁壽四年冬至，日亦在斗十度。

translations.literal: Afterward Xiaosun changed to follow Chuo's method, and Renshou year 4's winter solstice also placed the sun at ten degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaosun adopted Chuo's method, and Renshou 4's winter solstice also placed the sun at ten degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 焯卒後，冑玄以其前曆上元起虛五度，推漢太初，猶不及牽牛，乃更起虛七度，故太初在斗二十三度，永平在斗二十一度，並與今曆合。

translations.literal: After Chuo died, Zouxuan, using his earlier calendar's upper origin at five degrees in Void, projected Han Taichu—still falling short of Ox—then restarted at seven degrees in Void; thus Taichu stood at twenty-three degrees in Dipper, Yongping at twenty-one degrees in Dipper, both matching the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuo died, Zouxuan used his earlier calendar's upper origin at five degrees in Void to project Han Taichu—still falling short of Ox—then restarted at seven degrees in Void; thus Taichu fell at twenty-three degrees in the Dipper and Yongping at twenty-one degrees, both matching the present calendar.

sentences.zh: 而仁壽四年，冬至在斗十三度，以驗近事，又不逮其前曆矣。

translations.literal: Yet Renshou year 4's winter solstice stood at thirteen degrees in Dipper—checking recent events, it fell short of his earlier calendar still more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Renshou 4's winter solstice stood at thirteen degrees in the Dipper—checked against recent events, it fell even further behind his earlier calendar.

sentences.zh: 戊寅曆，太初元年辛酉冬至，進及甲子，日在牽牛三度。

translations.literal: The Wuyin calendar: Taichu year 1's Xinyou winter solstice advanced to Jiazi—the sun at three degrees in Ox.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyin calendar: Taichu year 1's Xinyou winter solstice advanced to Jiazi—the sun at three degrees in Ox.

sentences.zh: 永平十一年，得戊午冬至，進及辛酉，在斗二十六度。

translations.literal: Yongping year 11 obtained the Wuwu winter solstice, advancing to Xinyou—at twenty-six degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping 11 obtained the Wuwu winter solstice, advancing to Xinyou—at twenty-six degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 至元嘉，中氣上景初三日，而冬至猶在斗十七度。

translations.literal: By Yuanjia the mid-qi advanced Jingchu by three days, yet the winter solstice still stood at seventeen degrees in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanjia the mid-qi had advanced three days ahead of Jingchu, yet the winter solstice still stood at seventeen degrees in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 欲以求合，反更失之。

translations.literal: Seeking agreement, they instead lost it further.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking agreement, they lost it further still.

sentences.zh: 又曲循孝孫之論，而不知孝孫已變從皇極，故為淳風等所駁。

translations.literal: Again bending to Xiaosun's discourse, not knowing Xiaosun had already changed to follow Huangji—therefore Chunfeng and others refuted it.
translations.idiomatic: Again bending to Xiaosun's argument, unaware that Xiaosun had already switched to Huangji—therefore Chunfeng and others refuted it.

sentences.zh: 歲差之術，由此不行。

translations.literal: The method of annual precession thereby went unused.
translations.idiomatic: The method of annual precession thereby fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 以太史注記月蝕衝考日度，麟德元年九月庚申，月蝕在婁十度。

translations.literal: Checking solar degrees by lunar eclipse opposition in the Grand Astrologer's records: in Lindé year 1, ninth month Gengshen, the moon eclipsed at ten degrees in Bond.
translations.idiomatic: Checking solar degrees by lunar eclipse opposition in the Grand Astrologer's records: Lindé 1, ninth month Gengshen, the moon eclipsed at ten degrees in Bond.

sentences.zh: 至開元四年六月庚申，月蝕在牛六度。

translations.literal: To Kaiyuan year 4, sixth month Gengshen, the moon eclipsed at six degrees in Ox.
translations.idiomatic: By Kaiyuan 4, sixth month Gengshen, the moon eclipsed at six degrees in Ox.

sentences.zh: 較麟德曆率差三度，則今冬至定在赤道斗十度。

translations.literal: Compared with the Lindé calendar rate, the difference is three degrees—then the present winter solstice is fixed at ten degrees in Dipper on the equator.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the Lindé calendar rate, the difference is three degrees—fixing the present winter solstice at ten degrees in the Dipper on the equator.

sentences.zh: 又皇極曆歲差皆自黃道命之，其每歲周分，常當南至之軌，與赤道相較，所減尤多。

translations.literal: Also the Huangji calendar's annual precession is all named from the Yellow Path; its yearly circuit fraction ought constantly to match the southern extreme's track—compared with the equator, the reduction is especially great.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangji calendar's annual precession is reckoned from the ecliptic; its yearly circuit fraction should match the southern extreme's track—compared with the equator, the reduction is especially large.

sentences.zh: 計黃道差三十六度，赤道差四十餘度，雖每歲遯之，不足為過。

translations.literal: The ecliptic difference totals thirty-six degrees, the equator difference forty-odd degrees—though each year it retreats, this is not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic difference totals thirty-six degrees and the equator difference forty-odd—though each year it retreats, that is not excessive.

sentences.zh: 然立法之體，宜盡其原，是以開元曆皆自赤道推之，乃以今有術從變黃道。

translations.literal: Yet the body of establishing methods ought to exhaust the origin; therefore the Kaiyuan calendar all derives from the equator, then converts to the Yellow Path by present methods.
translations.idiomatic: Yet method-making should reach back to the root; therefore the Kaiyuan calendar derives everything from the equator, then converts to the ecliptic by present methods.

sentences.zh: 校勘記0.85em|columns=2

translations.literal: Collation notes 0.85em|columns=2
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes for this chapter.

sentences.zh: 其八日躔盈縮略例曰：

translations.literal: The eighth, the summary of principles on lodge advance, expansion and contraction, says:
translations.idiomatic: The eighth section, the summary of principles on lodge advance, expansion and contraction, states:

sentences.zh: 北齊張子信積候合蝕加時，覺日行有入氣差，然損益未得其正。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Zhang Zixin accumulated observations matching eclipses and added times, perceiving the sun's motion had an entry-qi discrepancy—yet the increase and decrease did not obtain the correct value.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Zhang Zixin accumulated observations matching eclipses and added times, perceiving the sun's motion had an entry-qi discrepancy—yet the increase and decrease did not hit the correct value.

sentences.zh: 至劉焯，立盈縮躔衰術，與四象升降。

translations.literal: When Liu Chuo established the expansion-contraction lodge-decline method, it joined the four images' ascent and descent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chuo established the expansion-contraction lodge-decline method, joining it to the four images' ascent and descent.

sentences.zh: 麟德曆因之，更名躔差。

translations.literal: The Lindé calendar followed it, renaming it lodge discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar followed it, renaming it lodge discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 凡陰陽往來，皆馴積而變。

translations.literal: Yin and yang coming and going all change by tame accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang in their coming and going all change by gradual accumulation.

sentences.zh: 日南至，其行最急，急而漸損，至春分及中而後遲。

translations.literal: At the sun's southern extreme its motion is swiftest; swift, it gradually lessens—reaching the spring equinox and its mid, afterward slow.
translations.idiomatic: At the sun's southern extreme its motion is swiftest; swift, it gradually slows—reaching the spring equinox and its midpoint, then slower still.

sentences.zh: 迨日北至，其行最舒，而漸益之，以至秋分又及中而後益急。

translations.literal: Awaiting the sun's northern extreme, its motion is most leisurely; leisurely, it gradually increases—until the autumn equinox again reaches mid, afterward swift again.
translations.idiomatic: At the sun's northern extreme its motion is most leisurely; leisurely, it gradually quickens—until the autumn equinox again reaches midpoint, then swift once more.

sentences.zh: 急極而寒若，舒極而燠若，及中而雨暘之氣交，自然之數也。
